# Human Capability Development Principles Framework

**DocID:** `HCD` within **FPF Library**.


HCD is a pattern language for deriving human capability demand from later Work, designing and sustaining development arrangements, judging human contribution, transfer and retention, and evaluating instructional material under stated audience, task, support and time conditions.

> **Author:** Anatoly Levenchuk with AI-assisted development and review.
> **Edition:** Twenty-nine-pattern edition dated 12 October 2026
> **Status:** Eternal alpha: used in working development projects and open to continuing correction.
> **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for original framework content; third-party material retains its own terms.
> **Publication:** [FPF Library repository](https://github.com/ailev/FPF). [Citation](#hcdsources3---citation).

# Table of Contents

Use the Readme when you have a working difficulty but do not yet know the direct pattern. Use this Table of Contents when you already know the PatternID. The links open the full instructions for all twenty-nine patterns.

`HCD.*` is the PatternID namespace. The numbers are stable addresses for HCD.1–HCD.28 and the nested HCD.6.1. Enter in the order the work requires.

# Human Capability Development Principles Framework Readme

## Practical entries

Human Capability Development connects what a person needs to contribute in later work with a feasible way to develop that contribution and evidence of what the person can now do. Tools, AI and providers can support the work; their contribution must remain visible when interpreting the person's performance. Instructional material can also be evaluated and repaired without making a claim about a particular person's development.

The selected examples below show how results from several methods work together. If no example matches your question, use the Table of Contents' working questions to enter the smallest relevant pattern. For a question outside human capability development, follow [Framework Boundary and Refresh](#human-capability-development-principles-framework-architectural-reference) to the named domain owner. Use an adequate existing result where it fits; return only to the question left open by a missing input or changed condition.

You can ask an assisting agent to explain or apply these methods in the language of your work, using the distinctions that matter to your question.

### HCD-PRODUCT - Build a learning offer before the learners are known

**Situation:** An author has a future audience and intended work, but topics, materials, practice and promised support do not yet form an attainable product.

**Question:** What complete learning route can this audience use, and which subject, material or supply contribution is missing?

**First useful result or blocker:** Comparable whole-product variants for a bounded task family, with entry branches, complete burdens and an exact missing contribution where a connection fails.

**Start with:** [HCD.28 - Construct and Revise a Whole Learning Product for a Future Audience](#hcd28---construct-and-revise-a-whole-learning-product-for-a-future-audience). Its solution explains how to join the contributions; the links below locate the suppliers.

**Stop or return:** Stop with the construction needed for the design or offer decision. Use an applicable subject method. If a required criterion has yet to be established, return that question to the practice responsible for it. For a material defect, use HCD.19. Use HCD.7 to arrange available help or HCD.8 to obtain or build a missing contribution. When an individual learner becomes known, return usable product variants and requirements to HCD.2 for personal comparison.

Future diagnosticians may calculate an indicator correctly while choosing the wrong model. HCD.28 first checks whether the subject selection criterion is available, implicit in expert action or unresolved. With an adequate subject basis, HCD.5 and HCD.6 construct the learning mechanism and task; HCD.7 establishes available assistance, with HCD.8 used for a contribution that must be obtained or built. HCD.20 compares individual and group options, and HCD.22 constructs the selected shared task. An individual arrangement remains an option when it provides the needed practice. The [constructed whole-product application](#hcdapplication5---app-hcd-04---constructed-whole-learning-product-and-shared-task) shows how the complete load can change the design.

### HCD-GROUP - Make joint activity develop the intended personal contribution

**Situation:** A shared answer is good, but it is unclear what each participant did, or the proposed interaction cannot fit the available people, time and help.

**Question:** Which contributions make learning together useful, and how can the task elicit them under a feasible arrangement?

**First useful result or blocker:** An assessment of a proposed or existing arrangement, a comparison of alternatives or a limiting condition. For a shared task, return the design or a finding about how it supports the intended personal work, material transfers, feedback and recovery.

**Start with:** [HCD.20 - Compose and Compare Arrangements for Individual and Group Learning](#hcd20---compose-and-compare-arrangements-for-individual-and-group-learning) when the configuration is unsettled; enter [HCD.22 - Design Shared Learning Tasks with Necessary Individual Contributions](#hcd22---design-shared-learning-tasks-with-necessary-individual-contributions) directly when the target and arrangement constraints already exist.

**Stop or return:** Finish when the comparison, feasibility finding or task design answers the request. Use HCD.7 or HCD.8 for a support condition that still needs work and HCD.28 for an affected connection in the learning product. Ground claims about personal performance, the common result, team capability and the material’s contribution in the relevant observations.

For a cohort of 24, group size depends on the interaction the task requires. Two three-minute contributions each plus six minutes of reconciliation give an initial bound of four people in thirty minutes, excluding separate help. The worked construction adds six minutes of qualified help per group and staggers the starts, allowing two mentors to make all six visits before the dependent personal actions. HCD.20 shows the participant and mentor timeline and the changed burden. At a shared instrument, meaningful observation and operator turns produce different constraints; the discussion formula does not determine that group size.

To establish or change actual membership and contact, use [HCD.21](#hcd21---form-and-change-learning-work-groups). To develop understanding through reasons, use [HCD.23](#hcd23---learn-through-explanation-and-comparison-of-solutions); for evaluative judgement and revision, use [HCD.24](#hcd24---learn-evaluation-and-revision-through-peer-review); for a relation that must reach another project, use [HCD.25](#hcd25---learn-transfer-through-comparison-of-projects). A group whose work has drifted can use [HCD.26](#hcd26---regulate-shared-learning), while incompatible preparation, material transfers or return windows lead to [HCD.27](#hcd27---coordinate-personal-learning-routes-with-a-shared-rhythm). Return what participants could actually contribute or use, and the limits they encountered, to the learning arrangement that depends on them.

### HCD-FEASIBLE - Make a development proposal fit the work and available support

**Situation:** A development proposal contains useful topics and exercises, but its complete tasks, learner effort and provider contribution have not been shown to fit together.

**Question:** What can be offered within the available time and support while preserving the intended contribution to later work?

**First useful result or blocker:** A feasible arrangement or task fragment for comparison, or the target, resource or support constraint that prevents a viable comparison.

**Start with:** [HCD.2 - Compose and Compare Human Capability-Development Programmes for Later Work](#hcd2---compose-and-compare-human-capability-development-programmes-for-later-work) for one known person with compatible work, target and starting evidence. For an author with a future audience, start directly with [HCD.28](#hcd28---construct-and-revise-a-whole-learning-product-for-a-future-audience); its product variants can later supply the personal comparison.

**Stop or return:** Stop with the comparison needed for the present decision. For missing support, identify or consult a provider that can supply it. A change to the intended outcome needs the responsible party’s decision. If the cause concerns working conditions, seek the contribution that can address it. Programme comparison does not authorize launch.

1. **Establish whose contribution the proposal concerns.** For one person, [HCD.1 - Derive Human Capability Demand from Representative Later Work](#hcd1--derive-human-capability-demand-from-representative-later-work) supplies the required contribution and its basis. [HCD.3 - Diagnose Whether a Capability, Misconception, or Behaviour Limits Work](#hcd3--diagnose-whether-a-capability-misconception-or-behaviour-limits-work) distinguishes a human development target from a tool, access, assignment or other limitation. Where simultaneous work competes for development effort, [HCD.4 - Architect a Balanced Human Capability Profile Across Simultaneous Work](#hcd4--architect-a-balanced-human-capability-profile-across-simultaneous-work) supplies the priorities and contributions to protect. Use those results to compare feasible alternatives through HCD.2. For a future audience whose individual learners are not yet known, it returns the design question and available fragments to HCD.28. A product variant returns to HCD.2 only with the named person’s compatible starting evidence, work, support and participation conditions.
2. **Make the alternatives comparable through complete tasks.** In the constructed [programme-design application](#hcdapplication6---application-return-to-a-programme-and-instrument-designer), three compositions each use 340 learner hours over 34 weeks. A change from ten to six hours per week leaves 204 hours: each original proposal exceeds the allowance by 136 hours. HCD.2 asks what work, practice and evidence would be removed or replaced. Check whether the complete tasks required for the promised outcomes still fit the reduced allocation.
3. **Construct the missing development contribution.** Retain the detailed task fragment already available for one option and construct the smallest comparable fragment for another, using the same intended output and audience assumptions. [HCD.5 - Select Human Capability-Development Methods](#hcd5---select-human-capability-development-methods) selects how to develop the target action from the starting evidence, or proposes conditional choices from stated entry assumptions for a future audience; [HCD.6 - Design Representative Practice Tasks](#hcd6---design-representative-practice-tasks) turns that choice into a whole task, criterion, permitted help and relevant variation. If the learner cannot yet notice a distinction required by the task, [HCD.6.1 - Help a Learner Discern a Needed Distinction in Practice](#hcd61---help-a-learner-discern-a-needed-distinction-in-practice) helps design an accessible contrast and use the learner’s response to guide the next attempt. Return the noticed distinction to the whole task; recognizing it does not establish the ability to perform that task. These results let HCD.2 compare what the options actually provide.
4. **Test the support needed at the time of use.** [HCD.7 - Arrange Providers, Access, Tools, and AI Support for Human Capability Development](#hcd7---arrange-providers-access-tools-and-ai-support-for-human-capability-development) uses those tasks to establish actual feedback, assessment, access and capacity. The example's 240 teaching hours divided among twelve participants is a planning allocation, not twenty hours of individual contact each. Doubling participants with unchanged individual checking demand doubles that checking work. [HCD.8 - Obtain or Build Missing Human Capability-Development Support with Bounded Recursion](#hcd8---obtain-or-build-missing-human-capability-development-support-with-bounded-recursion) enters only for a missing contribution that must be obtained or built. Return its cost and operating limits to the comparison.

A useful substitution may emerge from comparing the fragments. Establish whether the complete programme fits the 204 hours before offering it on those terms. Changing the intended outcome is another possible decision, which must be explicit before comparing a narrower offer.

### HCD-EVIDENCE - Decide what a successful attempt permits you to rely on

**Situation:** A learner reaches a correct answer after help, or succeeds in familiar work, and someone needs to decide what this permits them to rely on in later work.

**Question:** Which contribution is supported, under what conditions, and does the development arrangement need to change?

**First useful result or blocker:** A bounded performance conclusion and, when needed, a targeted change to the task or assistance; an unresolved transfer, delay or support question remains separate.

**Start with:** [HCD.11 - Assess Human Performance in Representative Work](#hcd11--assess-human-performance-in-representative-work), using the attempt and its actual conditions. If practice is being conducted, [HCD.9 - Perform Deliberate Practice with Feedback](#hcd9---perform-deliberate-practice-with-feedback) preserves the first attempt, supplied help, feedback, learner correction or supported retention. A correction requires a targeted retry; after retaining an action, retry only for a remaining practice question.

**Stop or return:** Stop when the available evidence is sufficient for the intended reliance or local revision. Seek a further observation when it can settle or materially improve a consequential claim and its value warrants the cost.

1. **Separate the successful product from the person's contribution.** In the constructed [APP-HCD-02](#hcdapplication3---app-hcd-02---constructed-performance-transfer-retention-and-revision), a teacher initially helps Learner-L17 reject a release proposal supported by the wrong firmware evidence. That correction is assisted. Two later fresh attempts show L17 detecting the mismatch before a teacher or AI cue, supporting a narrower independent configuration-checking conclusion.
2. **Change the condition relevant to the next use.** [HCD.12 - Test Transfer to Unfamiliar Work or Learning from a New Source](#hcd12--test-transfer-to-unfamiliar-work-or-learning-from-a-new-source) uses unfamiliar work when transfer matters. A compatible release case requires two hours per change plus one hour per batch of at most four changes. Ten changes need `20 + 3 = 23` hours and fit a 24-hour allowance. At 22 hours, ten no longer fit; nine need `18 + 3 = 21`. L17's corrected nine-change answer after feedback supports helped resource adaptation while preserving the earlier configuration result.
3. **Repair the development contribution exposed by that result.** [HCD.14 - Revise the Human Capability-Development Arrangement from Evidence](#hcd14--revise-the-human-capability-development-arrangement-from-evidence) can replace a cue-led resource exercise with cases requiring both a justified proposal and a justified refusal. It need not discard sound arithmetic or configuration practice. [HCD.10 - Choose Whether and How to Vary, Space, Interleave, or Progress Practice](#hcd10---choose-whether-and-how-to-vary-space-interleave-or-progress-practice) uses the attempt history to select a consequential variation, separated return, competing task or assistance change; select the condition that matters to the learner’s next use.
4. **Open a delay or support question only when it affects reliance.** [HCD.13 - Test Human Capability Retention and Dependence on Tools or Other Support](#hcd13--test-human-capability-retention-and-dependence-on-tools-or-other-support) compares performance after a delay and under changed support with suitable earlier conditions. A delayed attempt with AI also removed tests the combined condition. Isolating either effect requires a comparison that distinguishes delay from the withdrawal of help. Keep intervening practice and remaining tools visible. An immediate local repair need not wait for this separate investigation.

### HCD-CONTINUATION - Keep a useful arrangement while its conditions change

**Situation:** Development already has useful results, but later work, support or a claim about a development method changes; a successful work episode may also raise a question about what to retain or learn next.

**Question:** What should continue for this person, and does the change also affect the method repertoire or a group's development practice?

**First useful result or blocker:** A bounded lesson from successful Work, a continuing arrangement for the person, a decision to retain, revise or stop a specified use of a development method, or a supported account or decision about a specified cultural relation. Each uses evidence appropriate to its own question.

**Start with:** [HCD.15 - Sustain Continuing Human Capability Development](#hcd15--sustain-continuing-human-capability-development) for the person's continuing development, using current work and evidence, including an applicable HCD.14 revision. Open a repertoire or culture question only when that is the affected object.

**Stop or return:** Continue what remains adequate. Use the allocation already in force or seek any missing allocation from its authorized holder. Keep the comparison open when a needed investigation is infeasible. A change to one use does not by itself establish a population-wide effect.

For an episode that succeeded but whose useful lesson is unclear, start with **HCD.15:4.2.1** and the import case in **HCD.15:5.4**. Connect the person's explanation to the work record, actual help and an alternative account before choosing another application. The result can justify keeping the action and returning to Work.

1. **Locate what changed and what can be retained.** The constructed [APP-HCD-03](#hcdapplication4---app-hcd-03---constructed-continuation-method-repertoire-and-culture) preserves practice in tracing a release claim to its supporting evidence and referring safety or maintenance questions to the relevant specialist, while proposing a replacement for one cue-led correction exercise. HCD.15 uses that result to specify relevant cases, help, responsible providers and reopening conditions for the person. Until the needed learner and provider time is allocated, the affected practice cannot be arranged; the useful prior result remains available. HCD.15:5.3 shows a separate resourced variant: first, helped and fresh attempts lead to a local continuation decision, then an AI change reopens only source access.
2. **Carry evidence to the method claim only when it fits.** [HCD.16 - Keep Human Capability-Development Method Claims Current](#hcd16--keep-human-capability-development-method-claims-current) can use compatible observations from continuing development to retain a supported use or narrow a claim. In the example, retain the method for practising evidence tracing and specialist referral through attempts, feedback, correction and retry. The available result supports performance with help; its contribution to independent learning remains unresolved. The proposed comparison needs three learner hours and two provider hours; only half a provider hour is available. Its useful return is the narrower claim and unresolved comparison. A later resource window may make the probe feasible. Its expected contribution must still justify its cost, and the outcome depends on running it. Fresh success after both practice episodes can support the observed contribution while leaving each candidate's separate effect unresolved.
3. **Distinguish a group's continuation question.** [HCD.17 - Deliberately Continue and Change Human Capability-Development Culture](#hcd17--deliberately-continue-and-change-human-capability-development-culture) asks about the specified transmission, receiving use, recognition or retention of practice within a population. Its example observes receiving trainers using a teaching sequence after combined preparation and coaching. Reducing refresher coaching for those previously prepared trainers changes that basis: a feasible, authorized comparison can support a branch proposal, while the trainers' later use and the learners' performance remain separate observations. It does not establish that materials alone prepare a new group. Use observations of the trainers’ subsequent practice for the population claim and evidence of each learner’s contribution for the individual claim.

### HCD-MATERIAL - Find what instructional material supports and what to repair

**Situation:** An explanation, worksheet or learning route is meant to support a reader's task, but a correct reader answer may have depended on prior knowledge or help.

**Question:** What does the material supply for the promised use? Where a contribution is missing, which conclusion or repair depends on it?

**First useful result or blocker:** A compatible specification, a supported finding about what the material supplies, a limiting defect and its reach, or the particular criterion or evidence still needed.

**Start with:** [HCD.19 - Evaluate Instructional Material through Representative Reader Work and Diagnose Its Repair](#hcd19---evaluate-instructional-material-through-representative-reader-work-and-diagnose-its-repair) when a compatible specification exists. Otherwise use [HCD.18 - Select or Construct a Characterization and Evaluation Specification for Instructional Material](#hcd18---select-or-construct-a-characterization-and-evaluation-specification-for-instructional-material) to connect the promised task, audience, permitted help, criteria and evidence to the question or decision the evaluation must support.

**Stop or return:** Finish with the requested material finding or the supported use or repair conclusion. Identify any gap that limits a stronger claim. For a requested improvement, use E.23 with the affected material and use. Apply a human-performance method when the question concerns the person’s contribution or learning.

1. **Use the specification to decide what must be inspected.** The [instructional-material evaluation profile](#hcdapplication1---instructional-material-evaluation-profile) explains how HCD.18 and HCD.19 work together. Select the properties needed for the requested finding or decision. Inspection can establish a local false relation.
2. **Distinguish material contribution from reader repair.** In its Time-use S1 case, an uninterrupted example gives the same value for active effort and elapsed turnaround, so it cannot distinguish the two rules. A prepared reader separates them correctly using prior knowledge. HCD.19 preserves that fact rather than crediting the missing distinction to the material.
3. **Repair the relation and inspect its affected use.** The revised material distinguishes the quantities, changes the columns, adds interruption and population conditions, and supports a changed two-person comparison of three consumed person-hours with four available person-hours. This supports the bounded repair and use, not a novice-learning claim.
4. **Return remaining requirements at their actual reach.** The full specification still requires a concurrent-person example, an inspected task and key, and suitable explanatory and feedback evidence. Keep these gaps visible without withholding the narrower supported repair. Seek additional reader work when its attainable contribution to the requested conclusion or decision warrants its full burden.

# Human Capability Development Principles Framework Architectural Reference

## HCD.Reference:1 - Start from the contribution that later Work needs

Use HCD when a person, manager or development practitioner needs to establish what a person contributes to later Work or decide how to develop or sustain that contribution within available time, access and support. The question may arise before a programme, during a difficult practice attempt, after a successful assessment, or years later when the Work changes. A learning-product author can also use the framework while the future audience is still an assumption.

The recurring difficulty is connecting a development activity to the contribution it should change. A curriculum may cover every topic while leaving whole tasks out of reach. A good assisted answer may conceal the action the person still cannot supply. A once useful arrangement may become unsuitable after a tool, task or provider changes. Identify the contribution required and what available evidence establishes. If a development change is needed, compare candidate ways to make it and their feasibility. For a selected change, use or arrange the support it needs and assess what the subsequent observations establish.

Begin with the question or decision at hand. Identify whose contribution matters, the later Work and its conditions, what is already known, and the finding or decision still needed. Then enter the relevant body through the [Practical entries](#practical-entries). The first useful result can be small: a demand hypothesis, two comparable task fragments, a corrected practice attempt, one qualified performance claim, or an exact missing contribution to obtain. A known person needs compatible personal evidence; an author without named learners can proceed directly to [HCD.28](#hcd28---construct-and-revise-a-whole-learning-product-for-a-future-audience), which constructs the product before personal comparison through HCD.2.

The main choices concern complete-task attainability, preservation of useful existing contributions, and the effort displaced by development. More practice, realism, independence, assessment or provider preparation can improve one condition while making the whole arrangement too burdensome or changing the task being judged. Select these contributions for the live question and compare their combined demands. The [programme and instrument application](#hcdapplication6---application-return-to-a-programme-and-instrument-designer) makes that whole-arrangement constraint concrete.

## HCD.Reference:2 - What the framework connects


Human Capability Development concerns deliberate efforts to change or sustain a person’s capability for intended later Work. Establishing whether capability actually changed is a separate evidence question. A demand account states what later Work requires; a diagnostic target names what may need to change; a profile describes contribution claims; a programme sets out a bounded development arrangement; HCD.2 composes and compares programme candidates. Learning Work and clinical treatment are performed activities. Assessment provides observations and bounded inferences about performance, transfer, or retained capability. Programme, employment and other consequential decisions require their own authority.

HCD.1–HCD.17 connect the question to the person’s contribution or the practice being examined in a specified population. Keep the later Work, conditions, available resources, relevant specialist results and remaining uncertainty in view. Enter the method directly when its inputs fit the use.

FPF supplies the transdisciplinary distinctions used here: human and other Systems, capability holders, Methods and MethodDescriptions, Work and results, evidence, architecture, decision objects, agency, authority, and precise plain language. Direct human-learning and behaviour sources supply bounded mechanism and evidence claims. Target-domain and specialist sources provide criteria and evidence for correctness, criticality, safety, clinical, legal, and employment questions. Qualified specialists exercise professional judgement, and authorized actors make the corresponding decisions.

HCD.28 connects programme, material, practice and actual supply as a learning product for an audience. HCD.20 compares individual and group arrangements; HCD.22 designs a shared task when interaction supplies a needed contribution. HCD.21 establishes membership and actual contact; HCD.23–HCD.25 develop explanation, evaluative exchange and cross-project learning. HCD.26 regulates the current shared attempt, and HCD.27 connects personal routes with useful shared occasions. A personal action, a common work product and a team capability have different bearers and evidence. Use evidence for the person, work product or team according to the claim being made.

HCD.18 and HCD.19 address a different immediate object: the instructional material's contribution under a declared audience, task, and support arrangement. Their specification and diagnosis can improve a learning product before particular learners are known. A conclusion about learning or capability requires evidence about the person. A conclusion about a complete programme requires evidence about the whole arrangement.

## HCD.Reference:3 - Human demand, capability evidence, development revision and transformation remain distinct

`HCD.1` identifies what a person must contribute in later Work. To assess what that person can do now, use evidence of their performance. `HCD.3` identifies a supported human limitation, explains an external constraint or states what evidence is missing. If another practice must answer a question, return it there when known. Selecting an intervention is a further question. `HCD.4` compares the person’s current and target contributions and may support a bounded choice. Designing a programme and establishing change over time require their own work and evidence.

`HCD.2` composes and compares feasible programme candidates for one person's later Work, including complete contributions, burdens, support dependence and evidence needs; a programme choice and its launch require the relevant decisions and provision. When no particular person is yet known, it returns the learning-product question to HCD.28. HCD.28 supplies conditional variants, not a diagnosis or programme assignment for each future member. `HCD.5` selects a development Method for a qualified target and starting attempt, or proposes conditional Methods with entry evidence for a future audience. Neither result is an effectiveness finding. `HCD.6` designs a sufficiently whole, criterion-bearing practice task without treating surface realism as representation. Its nested `HCD.6.1` helps a learner discern a needed difference, use it and separate it from an incidental cue. That preparatory teaching operation returns to whole-task use and preserves the difference between recognition and performance.

`HCD.7` establishes the provider, access, source, tool, AI, environment, human-check, capacity and fallback contributions required by a bounded use. `HCD.8` compares obtaining a missing contribution with building it, follows the first blocking dependency and checks representative operating evidence under the required conditions. If operating evidence is missing, use a feasible representative test or identify what prevents reliance on the provision. `HCD.9` preserves the first attempt, actual help, information-bearing feedback and the learner's response. It requires a targeted retry after correction; supported retention can end the episode when no question remains. `HCD.10` selects variation, spacing, retrieval, source, interleaving, support and challenge conditions separately across episodes.

HCD.11 returns observations and a bounded capability inference. HCD.12 tests a material unfamiliar variation. HCD.13 compares delayed performance and support conditions. HCD.14 uses relevant observations to assess a development assumption and propose a revision when warranted. A correct first attempt, a correction after feedback, learning from a newly supplied source, delayed performance, transfer, retention and a causal development effect are separately reportable.

HCD.15 uses changes in work or evidence, including lessons from successful Work, to shape a continuing development arrangement. Establishing what the learner did and what changed requires observations. HCD.16 evaluates a particular Method claim within the repertoire, preserving whether it concerns an admitted Method or a candidate. State the strongest use the evidence supports and its limits. That may confirm the current use, narrow the claim, leave a comparison unresolved or stop a use that violates a protection. Assess any proposed change or inquiry against its attainable benefit and the full burden on learners and providers. HCD.17 can establish what happened to a practice in a specified population. When a decision is requested, compare how to continue or change it, or identify an attainable inquiry worth pursuing. Use evidence about the people, practices and conditions concerned, and identify the authority needed for a proposed change.

Distinguish instructional events, learner activity, learning outcomes, later transfer, and job performance, and use corresponding evidence for claims about each. A MethodDescription, course completion, self-report, platform prediction, assisted score, published schedule or reserved provider hours can inform a bounded question. A capability, transfer, retention or effect claim needs a justified inference from appropriate observations.

## HCD.Reference:4 - Several contributions can be simultaneous

Perception, reasoning, bodily action, coordination, decision, evidence return, tool use, and specialist interfaces can all matter in one representative Work occurrence. Establish how these contributions work together in the representative task.

A profile and programme comparison therefore preserve claim identity, conditions, support dependence, uncertainty, critical-error boundaries, trade-offs and finite burdens. Use an aggregate score only if it preserves the distinctions needed for the question or decision.

Describe the contribution required in the person's work role and the conditions under which it is needed. The human capability holder is the person who fills that role. The same person can review evidence, coordinate a specialist and make a bounded proposal in the same Work, or fill different roles in different Work. HCD.4 therefore compares that person's contribution claims and their interfaces. A role description can help derive demand through HCD.1; personal starting evidence is still needed for diagnosis or a personal programme comparison.

Several people's development can support an organization's work, but an organizational result also depends on assignments, coordination, resources and other system contributions. Keep each person's evidence identifiable and use OCE and the relevant evidence or authorized provider for claims about organizational capability or change. A bounded cultural population is a different subject again: HCD.17 asks how one HCD practice value is transmitted, received, selected or retained among specified participants. It can examine that relation while individual capability consequences remain an HCD.11–HCD.13 question. A population becomes a capability holder only if the independent-System condition of E.23.CDI is separately established; HCD.1's population use otherwise preserves member or representative demand accounts.


**Constituent actions in ongoing work.** Consider a dancer who has adequate strength, holds an axis when stationary and remembers a figure, but cannot maintain balance during its required rotation. During an attempted figure, muscular actions support rotational coordination, and that coordinated rotation is a constituent of performing the figure. The missing capability is in the middle. HCD.3 locates the supported limitation; HCD.2 includes its development in a programme that retains already mastered contributions; HCD.6 and HCD.10 prepare the combination and needed variation. Knowing the figure and succeeding in separate strength exercises do not fill this gap. Use suitable teaching, space, time and support already available for this practice, and arrange what is missing.

## HCD.Reference:5 - Pattern relations do not prescribe a lifecycle

`HCD.1` may supply evidence input to `HCD.3` and scope or result frames to `HCD.4`, `HCD.2` and `HCD.11`. HCD.3 and HCD.4 may supply target, starting-evidence, protected-strength and priority values to HCD.2 or HCD.5. Use equivalent qualified inputs directly.

Before programme choice, HCD.5 can select a development Method for a candidate, HCD.6 can prepare its practice task, and HCD.7 can determine the support it needs and what is available. Use HCD.8 when obtaining or building a missing contribution changes the comparison. Develop only enough of each candidate to make the comparison useful. After a separate programme choice, complete or revise the selected Methods, tasks and support.

HCD.5, HCD.6, support arranged through HCD.7, and support obtained or built through HCD.8 when needed may supply HCD.9. HCD.9 may supply practice history to HCD.10 or an attempt to HCD.11; HCD.10 designs later episodes. Use observations of performance for any claim about what happened or was retained.

HCD.11 can supply performance evidence to HCD.12 and HCD.13. Equivalent qualified observations permit direct entry. HCD.14 may use a compatible result from any one of HCD.11, HCD.12 or HCD.13; it need not wait for all of them. New evidence may also update HCD.3's diagnosis, HCD.4's profile, HCD.2's comparison or HCD.5's selection when it changes their question.

A compatible HCD.14 revision hypothesis may inform HCD.15's continuing-arrangement decision or HCD.17's cultural-variation comparison. Observed HCD.15 arrangement use and human-development evidence may inform HCD.16. A bounded HCD.16 repertoire disposition or status-preserved candidate variation may inform HCD.17. Use each result when its conditions fit the receiving question. For a missing, stale or differently scoped contribution, use a qualified substitute or identify the result still needed and the conclusion it limits.

HCD.18 supplies a specification to HCD.19 only when construction or revision is needed. A compatible existing specification permits direct evaluation. For improvement under E.23, use the material-specific diagnosis and affected-use test. For HCD.11–HCD.13, use only observations qualified for the corresponding human-evidence question. Narrative attachment and progressive reconstruction use NSTD.6 and NSTD.8 when that branch is live.

HCD.28 joins the required subject, teaching, task and supply results into a whole learning route and compares serious alternatives. HCD.20 supplies the applicable arrangement comparison; HCD.22 supplies the actual shared task. Their results can return a changed burden or missing contribution to HCD.28. HCD.2 consumes a suitable product variant only after adding the known person’s relevant conditions. HCD.21 supplies compatible participants and contact; HCD.23–HCD.25 supply a selected interaction method. HCD.26 can return a missing subject or support contribution from an actual attempt, and HCD.27 supplies the material and timing connections among episodes. Start with the method that supplies the missing contribution. A sufficient individual arrangement can finish the question.

Use the smallest pattern that supplies the result needed for the current question or decision. A new observation reopens only the claims and receiving decisions whose evidence, conditions, or retry predicates it changes.

To combine uses, first name the result the combination should produce and the values each receiving Method actually needs. Reuse a result only when person or population, contribution, later Work, conditions and evidence window fit that receiving use. Then identify dependencies that require order, contributions used together, and competing demands on time or support. An available direct result can close a dependency immediately. HCD.8's obtain-or-build comparison is useful only when an exact missing contribution blocks the selected use. The [Direct result relations](#hcdreference12---direct-result-relations) table locates these returns; the bodies explain how each result is produced.

For example, a practitioner can combine HCD.6, HCD.7 and HCD.9 for one supported practice task when the target and Method are already qualified. A fresh transfer miss can instead combine HCD.12 with HCD.14 to test a local revision, without rebuilding demand or waiting for a delayed observation. In a programme comparison, HCD.2 needs enough task, Method and support detail to compare complete candidates; fuller elaboration follows the separately selected use. These combinations share contributions, while their result, evidence and stopping question differ.

## HCD.Reference:6 - Choose the scope and the evidence that change this use

The broad subject is deliberate human capability development. A personal programme comparison narrows it to finite changes for one person's later Work: HCD.2 compares complete candidate arrangements from that person's supported baseline. HCD.28’s future-audience learning-product design has a different result. It keeps audience assumptions, output tasks, alternatives, support and budgets explicit so that the author can develop a comparable product fragment; personal recommendation waits for the relevant person and evidence. This difference gives the author a useful direct start and identifies what individualization must later add.

Performance, unfamiliar transfer and retention narrow the evidence question in different ways. HCD.11 asks what the person contributed under specified conditions. HCD.12 asks what survives a material unfamiliar change to an already demonstrated contribution. HCD.13 compares earlier and delayed performance with the intervening practice and support conditions preserved. For a claim about learning a newly supplied Method, use HCD.12:4.5 with the intended use of the new source made explicit. These are useful distinct questions because the same correct answer can support different inferences, or fail to distinguish them.

The intended capability may include competent use of sources: a person may need to recognize a question, find a current rule, use a calculator and obtain a specialist result. Independence concerns the particular contribution being judged. If independent recognition is required, the person must select the relevant response before a teacher or AI supplies that selection; permitted references and accessibility support can remain. HCD.6 specifies the intended task conditions, HCD.7 establishes available support, and HCD.9 and HCD.11 preserve the help actually received in practice and assessment, respectively. HCD.12 and HCD.13 then interpret transfer or delay under those conditions. A delayed attempt with AI also withdrawn answers that combined condition; separate delay and support-dependence claims need an interpretable comparison.

Continuing development extends beyond a fixed course. HCD.15 connects changes in later Work or evidence, and worthwhile questions from successful work episodes, to opportunities for practice, current sources, coaching, specialist access and reassessment under an agreed burden. A material change can reopen one contribution while the rest stays in ordinary use. Use HCD.14 for a local revision; enter HCD.15 when a continuing arrangement must respond to further changes. If the question concerns which human-development Method claim remains warranted for a population and use, HCD.16 compares that claim with serious alternatives. If it concerns how a practice continues among participants, HCD.17 tests the cultural relation. The [continuation application](#hcdapplication4---app-hcd-03---constructed-continuation-method-repertoire-and-culture) shows all three questions with their consequences kept separate.

Choose the scope from the person or audience concerned, the intended use and the evidence needed. The same domain, source and authority conditions apply wherever a narrower question relies on them.

### HCD.Reference:6.1 - Learning a practice whose usable regularities exceed its rules

A learner can state a grammatical rule yet miss a familiar phrase in conversation; copy a dance sequence yet fail to respond to a new partner; complete a work procedure yet miss the exception that calls for help. Conversely, a person can make a sound distinction or perform a coordinated action before being able to explain it. Begin from the contribution the receiving practice needs. A verbal account, recognition, fluent execution, adaptation and participation can be related targets without being interchangeable observations.

[HCD.5:4.2.1](#hcd5421---compose-learning-from-the-contribution-not-an-explicitimplicit-ratio) explains how to combine explanation, examples, exposure, practice, feedback and participation from that target. [HCD.6.1:4.2.2](#hcd61422---learn-a-family-of-regularities-without-forcing-a-single-rule) develops learning across a family of examples when a single contrast or explicit rule is insufficient. HCD.6 reconnects focused work to simultaneous coordination; HCD.9 makes feedback usable through the response the target actually requires. [HCD.Application:10](#hcdapplication10---combine-explanation-experience-and-participation-in-a-changing-practice) follows these connections through language, movement, ordinary workplace learning and a team of engineers.

A cultural practice supplies uses, exemplars, conventions and disputed or changing judgements as well as explicit rules. Learning can therefore begin from competent demonstrations and usable comparisons without waiting for a complete verbal theory. Establish which practice and conditions those examples represent. A conventional variant in one community is not automatically an error in another. Developing the learner's participation differs from changing the practice's repertoire or recognition arrangements; MDPE supplies that latter music-and-dance question.

Learning inside work adds another connection. For learning at work, identify a contribution the person can perform and arrange help where needed. For future use, arrange or identify a suitable later opportunity. To establish whether use continued, examine the later work, including whether the person had such an opportunity. HCD.15 develops that arrangement. HCD.22 distinguishes learning through interaction from learning to perform one's contribution in joint work; OCE addresses a needed change to the organization's assignments, access or contribution relations. A useful joint result may require all three without making every participant learn every profession.

## HCD.Reference:7 - Architectural Rationale

HCD organizes the repertoire around working questions whose inputs and useful results can differ. Demand can be supported while diagnosis remains open; a practice correction can be useful before transfer is demonstrated; an operational assessor contribution can exist before any learner receives it. Separating these Methods lets a practitioner obtain the missing result and preserve established contributions. Combining them around later Work keeps that separation from becoming a collection of unrelated techniques. The cost is attention to conditions and interfaces; reuse compatible results and keep the account only as detailed as the question or decision requires.

Several serious approaches can supply part or all of a particular development arrangement. Compare them by the contribution needed in the same working situation.

| Approach | Practical strength and appropriate use | Why HCD keeps a broader repertoire, and when to prefer the approach directly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A complex-skill programme designed through [4C/ID](https://www.4cid.org/about/) | Learning tasks connect supportive information for reasoning, procedural information during routine work, and additional part-task practice where automaticity needs more practice. This supplies a concrete architecture for a complex-skill curriculum. | HCD.2, HCD.5 and HCD.6 adapt this task-and-support organization while retaining diagnosis, personal baselines, complete resource comparison and later evidence questions. A designer whose demand, audience and delivery conditions are settled can use 4C/ID directly for that programme. HCD remains useful when a human target, available support, continued development or a particular transfer/retention inference is still undecided. |
| [Cognitive apprenticeship and supervised participation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijme.2020.100417) | Modelling and coaching can expose expert reasoning in situated tasks; guided participation provides access to work that a text alone may not supply. Prefer this form when competent supervision and suitable tasks can supply the target contribution within the consequence and resource limits. | HCD.5 compares the development contribution, HCD.7 establishes provider and access conditions, and HCD.8 addresses an exact missing contribution. Protected or infrequent work may require bounded simulations or separately prepared cases to make the needed observation possible. Compare the judgement and variation the person can encounter in situated work with the supervision this requires. |
| A learning product as the main development arrangement | A course, guide or interactive product can coordinate explanation, practice, pacing and feedback for a defined audience, and can make an already selected development design usable at scale. HCD.28 connects that offer with the required subject basis and actual supply; Learning Product practice supplies Guide/Slidement construction within its own applicable profile. | Use that product directly when it fits the person's task, entry evidence and support. HCD adds the comparison when fit, alternatives, finite burdens or later-Work evidence are unresolved, and, through HCD.28, develops the whole-product construction before particular learners are known. A course's audience assumptions remain design assumptions until the person-specific questions they matter to are answered. |
| A generic evaluation or testing framework | A framework for claims, tasks, observations and intended interpretations helps an assessor obtain evidence for a bounded judgement. HCD.11 adapts that contribution from evidence-centred design and the [Testing Standards](https://www.testingstandards.net/uploads/7/6/6/4/76643089/9780935302356.pdf). | HCD distinguishes the development decisions that use the judgement: diagnosis, local revision, unfamiliar transfer, delay, support dependence and continuing arrangement. Direct evaluation is enough when only its bounded judgement is needed. The wider HCD combination earns its cost when the same result requires a different development response, or when the proposed assessment would change the contribution being observed. |

The shared source line is therefore task- and evidence-sensitive human development. Whole tasks and expertise-sensitive support inform what to practise; feedback, retrieval, spacing and task similarity inform candidate practice changes; assessment sources qualify what can be inferred. Provider and workplace-learning sources connect learning opportunities to the conditions of participation and later Work. Use each family for the claim it supports. Whether the local programme works requires evidence about that programme. The [Source use](#hcdsources1---source-use-and-currentness) account and each body's SoTA-Echoing section identify the specific adopted or adapted claim, population, task, support, horizon and limit. Reopen a choice when those conditions change or a serious alternative changes the next useful action; preserve unaffected source uses.

## HCD.Reference:8 - Check the combination, learn from its result and revise

Recognize the current difficulty and identify the first result needed to answer it. Stronger assurance begins when someone will rely on a claim of capability, transfer, retained performance, provider operation or effect. The selected body's criteria and recognition/assurance boundary govern that stronger question. At framework scope, check the connections that a local body cannot establish for the whole use:

- Does each consumed result concern the intended person or bounded population, contribution, later Work and conditions, with a clear distinction between observation, design and hypothesis?
- Does each required contribution have a feasible source, provider and time window, and does the whole proposed arrangement fit learner and provider budgets, including preparation, feedback, checking, and any retries or delayed observations it requires?
- Can the intended observation distinguish the human contribution from an answer supplied by help, and can its task and domain criteria support the declared inference?
- Do the receiving decisions preserve non-compensable errors, useful existing contributions, participation and access conditions, and the authority of their actual owners?
- Is the first result useful enough to stop or proceed now, with an observation or changed condition that can reopen only the affected claim?

The constructed applications show what those questions can change. In ImpactReview-17, a feasible probe is still worth doing before selecting a profile focus. In the L17 case, independent configuration checking survives one unfamiliar task while uncued resource adaptation remains unsupported; HCD.14 can propose a local practice change immediately. In ReleaseWork-R9, prospective demand remains useful while distinct missing observations block stronger same-holder conclusions. The observations in these examples are stipulated.

The future-diagnostician application adds a whole-product question. A missing selection criterion, an inaccessible explanation and a late mentor response require different repairs. HCD.28 preserves those distinctions; HCD.20 and HCD.22 expose the personal actions and peak demand hidden by a correct group answer. The numbers in that comparison are planning assumptions.

The likely practical gain is a smaller and more informative next development action: compare one missing task fragment, obtain one assessor contribution, revise one cue-dependent exercise, or retain a working arrangement until a relevant condition changes. The costs include representative task preparation, competent judgement, time for correction and evidence that sometimes requires later access. Shared observations can reduce duplicate work only when their conditions fit each receiving inference. The programme application shows how apparently useful local activities can still exceed the common budget.

The engineering examples foreground explicit sources, configurable tools, auditable work products and consequential error checks. Work whose contribution is bodily, interpersonal or difficult to observe may need different representative tasks and qualified domain judgement. Learners also differ in starting evidence, language, accessibility needs, consent, available time and access to competent providers. Preserve those conditions before transferring a task or programme; keep required accessibility support in an independence test. The [clinical unlike case](#hcdapplication9---clinical-unlike-case---return-diagnosis-and-treatment-to-their-owner) demonstrates one material boundary where the specialist owns diagnosis and treatment.

When an observation calls a development assumption into question, use HCD.14 to identify the smallest affected part. If a revision needs testing, name the feasible change, the fresh task, the contributions to protect and the conditions for retaining, adapting or abandoning it. Use HCD.15 when subsequent Work or evidence changes require a continuing arrangement, or when a useful lesson from successful Work still needs to be qualified before deciding what to learn next. A contradicted source claim or serious new Method alternative can reopen the bounded HCD.16 repertoire question; a changed receiving-use or retention relation among participants can reopen HCD.17. Practical revision can proceed under a proportionate reversible hypothesis while a stronger causal-effect claim remains a separate evidence question.

## HCD.Reference:9 - Intended use and ordinary non-use

Use this edition to identify the human contribution needed in later Work, construct or choose a feasible way to develop it, and interpret observations for a question about performance, transfer, retention or a development decision. It also supports learning-product and instructional-material work, individual and shared learning arrangements, and the continuation or revision of HCD Methods and cultural practices. The [Practical entries](#practical-entries) and [Available patterns](#hcdreference11---available-patterns) distinguish these working questions and their results.

Use domain findings for specialist correctness and safety, clinical services for treatment, and authorized decision makers for release or employment decisions. In HCD, use the evidence specific to a claim that a provider operated, a person performed or developed, a practice continued or an intervention had an effect. Use a curriculum, provider arrangement or assessment that fits the question. Select or construct the missing contribution when needed.

## HCD.Reference:10 - PatternID and reader order

HCD.* is the Human Capability Development PatternID namespace. Numbers are stable addresses, not steps. The [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents) gives the reading order. Demand is a useful cold start when the required human contribution is unknown; equivalent qualified input permits direct entry to any Method under its own conditions.

Claims about performed work, provider operation or changes in a person or population require evidence from the relevant setting. HCD.19 separately reports a bounded prepared-agent material walkthrough under its stated conditions.

## HCD.Reference:13 - FPF dependency and compatibility

This edition depends on **First Principles Framework (FPF) — Core Conceptual Specification, Version August 2026**, status **Normative kernel, eternal alpha**, with the bounded C.2.8 dependency below.

FPF supplies System and holder recognition, capability, Method and MethodDescription, Work occurrence and result distinctions, evidence and uncertainty, architecture, agency, decision objects, authority, cultural relations, and precise wording. HCD uses these distinctions in the domain Methods whose contributions and receiving uses are set out above.

`E.23.CDI` governs the independent-System holder condition and later capability-development evidence under its own entry conditions. `E.23.CAE` supplies an observation-first differential where applicability, access, adaptation, enactment, and actual capability change must be separated. Use `C.32.MWA` to derive profile relations from the required contributions and their conditions. A course sequence or organization chart can supply a relation only when its correspondence to the work is justified. `C.11.CRC` governs finite comparison inside HCD.2, while `C.11` governs a bounded current-option choice. Compatible FPF changes leave unaffected HCD results reusable; changed relied-on distinctions reopen only their consumers.

For HCD.18, HCD.19 and the instructional-material profile, this edition selects [extractable structural information (FPF C.2.8)](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/f4bad21274b54b57071afb2210a8bdb9f61a1c95/FPF-Spec.md#c28---uextractablestructuralinformation) from the FPF publication of 9 September 2026. It supplies the structural-recovery characteristic of the expressed episteme, its publication form and the reader or observer under specified comparison conditions. Use its own qualitative comparison or structural scale; the profile's material-use values, learning and burden claims keep their own meanings and evidence. Other FPF dependencies retain the basis above. Reopen this bounded dependency when the supplying definition or the receiving structural question changes.

A.19.ECS supplies general evaluation-specification construction to HCD.18. E.22 supplies comparison and E.23 improvement for a material result when those questions are live. General characterization and scale meanings remain with A.17, A.18 and C.16. Material evaluation does not alter the human-evidence or authority boundaries of the other HCD bodies.

## HCD.Reference:14 - External result and authority boundaries

Target-domain Methods and results govern what counts as correct, safe, critical, or useful in later Work. Clinical, safety, legal, employment, assignment, organization, provider, platform, tool, and specialist owners retain their direct results and authority. Use an applicable result directly, or identify the particular fact, qualified determination or permission still needed.

Identify who performs each part of the work and who supplies any needed assistance. A capable, authorized service can conduct an assessment or deliver a specified contribution when it has the necessary access and configuration. For a claim about human capability, identify the person’s own contribution under the observed support. For a decision, establish who holds the applicable authority. Managers may own allocation and assignment while the human holder participates and while programme, safety, release, clinical, or employment decisions stay separate.

## HCD.Reference:15 - Publication boundary and current full-body returns

The authoritative practitioner guidance is in the twenty-nine complete pattern bodies indexed in the [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents). This publication also contains the shared framework account and instructional-material profile; use the relevant body for its working conditions and full method.

This complete domain framework contains the Methods for direct use. Its Architectural Reference explains the language's subject, connections, selected arrangement, grounds, alternatives and limits. An instructional Guide is organized for learning and memory formation. A Suite Architectural Reference explains connections among the included frameworks: the Human Capability Engineering account explains HCD together with SOM, while the Engineering account returns to that specialization.

## HCD.Reference:End


# Part I — Human Capability Demand, Programme, Practice, Evidence, Continuation, Repertoire, Culture, Learning Products, and Shared Tasks

## HCD.1 — Derive Human Capability Demand from Representative Later Work

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable


### HCD.1:0 - Use This When

Use this pattern when someone asks what a named person must be able to contribute in later Work and the available request is still expressed as a job title, competency list, course request, platform score, MethodDescription, or technology rollout. Begin with the person and representative cases of their later Work.

The first useful result is a **human capability-demand account**. State what the person must contribute in the named Work family, under which configuration and conditions, over what horizon, and which question or decision the account will support. If the account of future Work is grounded but evidence of current performance is insufficient, return a **prospective demand hypothesis** and the observations that could qualify it. Use an applicable result already available for specialist judgement, assignment, access, tools or nonhuman capability. If another practice still needs to answer or decide a question, give it the question and available evidence. If its source is unknown, identify the contribution needed. State which conclusions still need evidence and what would support them.

The demand identifies what a later diagnosis or profile comparison should examine. Use `HCD.3` when the demand is known and the question is which changeable human limitation, if any, is supported. Use `HCD.4` when the demand is known and simultaneous capability claims must be compared. A separate programme comparison (`HCD.2`) may use the account; deriving demand does not select a programme.

Use the relevant professional practice and authority for clinical, curriculum, provider, employment, safety and release decisions or a judgement of target-domain correctness.

#### HCD.1:0.1 - Working Terms

| Name in this pattern | What it denotes |
| --- | --- |
| human holder | One identified person whose capability demand is being considered. For a population question, use separately identified member accounts or representative accounts. |
| later Work | A named family of future or recurring `U.Work` occurrences in which that person may contribute under stated conditions. |
| representative case | A case selected to examine a material variant of later Work, such as unfamiliar content, changed support, or a specialist interface. Its suitability depends on the conditions it represents and the conclusion for which it is used. |
| human capability demand | The contributions this person needs to be able to make under the named later-Work conditions. A demand account records those requirements; it does not establish the person's current capability. |
| demand claim | A statement that this person needs to be able to make a specified contribution under the named later-Work conditions, with the grounds for that requirement, remaining uncertainty and scope. |
| prospective demand hypothesis | A provisional account of future demand grounded in a supported future-Work frame. It states which demand claims remain provisional and which observations could qualify or revise them. |
| demand-evidence-blocked | A result that names each missing input, the conclusion it blocks, and the condition for retry. It also distinguishes available material from the missing input when that material could mislead the receiver. |
| outside-HCD return | The question and available evidence returned to the practice that can answer or decide it. If that practice is unknown, identify the contribution needed. |

The account records what later Work requires of the person. Use evidence and a method suited to the separate question about present capability, causes, learning or intervention effectiveness.

### HCD.1:1 - Problem Frame

Human development is often commissioned on the strength of a course catalogue, certification, role framework, AI platform, assessment dashboard, or manager's request. Those sources can be useful, but none identifies by itself what a particular person must contribute in later Work.

The same named task can require different contributions when the product configuration, Method, information access, AI support, time, authority, specialist interface, or critical-error boundary changes. Assisted performance may also conceal which contribution belongs to the person and which belongs to a tool, another Agent, or an organization.

Demand therefore has to be recovered from representative Work and its intended result. Current observations are valuable, but future planning sometimes precedes an actual Work occurrence. State what the future arrangement suggests and what observations would establish current demand.

### HCD.1:2 - Problem

A role-first or course-first description bundles unlike things. It can call a missing Method, inaccessible source, broken tool, absent specialist result, poor assignment, unsafe workload, or organizational constraint a human skill gap. It can also average across a population and then assign the average to one person.

The reverse mistake is to refuse any demand account until the exact future Work has occurred. An account of the planned arrangement can already identify a provisional human contribution and an observation that would test it. The practitioner needs a result that distinguishes what can be framed now, what is qualified now, what belongs elsewhere, and exactly what evidence blocks the stronger conclusion.

### HCD.1:3 - Forces

- A short role label is easy to communicate, while the consequential demand usually depends on case variants, interfaces, and error boundaries.
- A MethodDescription can describe how the Work should be done. Ground a claim about a particular performance or result in that occurrence. For a claim about representative work, use evidence from cases that fit the claim.
- Current task success is visible, while later transfer and unfamiliar variants must be established rather than presumed.
- AI and other supports can improve the joint result, while assisted output is not automatically human capability.
- Population summaries help allocation, while a person-specific decision requires a person-specific holder and compatible evidence.
- Evidence can be insufficient for a current demand while a useful prospective hypothesis may still guide observation.
- HCD can organize demand evidence, while target-domain correctness, specialist judgement, assignment, safety, release, and employment authority stay elsewhere.

### HCD.1:4 - Solution

Derive each required human contribution from representative later Work. Distinguish observed cases from plans, stipulations and assumptions. Identify which contributions the person must make, what others or the environment must supply, and how strongly the available evidence supports each requirement.

#### HCD.1:4.1 - Pattern-Use Unfolding

1. **Fix the use boundary and holder.** Identify the person, the question or decision the account will serve, later-Work family, subject configuration, effective horizon, and evidence window. If the question concerns a population, identify the separately observed members or representative accounts; do not manufacture one aggregate holder.
2. **Recover the later-Work basis.** For every case, distinguish what was observed from what is planned, stipulated, or assumed. Explain which later Work and material conditions the case represents, and why its evidence is suitable for the intended conclusion. Recover the intended result, quality and critical-error predicates, Work products, and stopping conditions.
3. **Recover Methods and direct-owner inputs.** Identify applicable target Methods or MethodDescriptions, specialist results, assignments, authority, access, environment, tools, and supports. State any missing external condition or contribution and what depends on it.
4. **Select representative cases.** Cover the variants that can change demand. Depending on the Work, these may include familiar and unfamiliar situations, allowed and withdrawn assistance, time or workload limits, AI-output challenge, coordination interfaces, specialist-return conditions, and material quality or critical-error boundaries.
5. **Derive human demand claims.** For each case, state which contribution the named person must be able to make for the intended result under the protected conditions and why the evidence warrants that requirement. Contributions may include, for example, noticing a signal, handling an object, coordinating a specialist return, or justifying a decision. Record required tools and supports as conditions of the contribution. Keep each contribution distinct from the Method, task, tool output, team result, or personal trait.
6. **Bind evidence and uncertainty.** Relate each demand claim to the cases, observations, work products, inference rule, uncertainty and any observation still needed. Keep instruction events, learner events, learning outcomes, later transfer, and job performance distinct; one does not establish the next by label alone.
7. **Return a conclusion-specific disposition.** Return `qualified current demand`, `prospective demand hypothesis`, `outside-HCD return`, or `demand-evidence-blocked`. Different questions may lawfully receive different dispositions in one use—for example, a prospective hypothesis for future framing and a blocker for qualified current demand.

#### HCD.1:4.2 - Record the Result

A human capability-demand account contains these result positions:

| Result position | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| use boundary | Human holder, receiving question or decision, later-Work family, configuration, effective horizon, evidence window, and direct owners whose results or authority matter. |
| later-Work basis | Cases, what was observed or remains planned, stipulated, or assumed, and the later Work and conditions they represent; reasons the evidence is suitable for the conclusion; intended result, quality and critical-error predicates, Work products, and stop conditions. |
| protected conditions | Allowed or required tools, AI posture, information access, time, environment, assignment, authority, supports, and specialist interfaces. |
| demand claims | Statements of the human contributions required in the named later Work, including material interfaces among simultaneous contributions. Derive these requirements from the cases rather than assigning capability from job labels or traits. |
| evidence account | Evidence and inference for every demand claim, uncertainty, incompatible evidence, and any observation or case still needed. |
| external gaps | Missing Method, description, specialist return, assignment, authority, access, environment, or nonhuman capability with the work or conclusion that depends on it and its responsible source where known. |
| disposition | One conclusion-specific `qualified current demand`, `prospective demand hypothesis`, `outside-HCD return`, or `demand-evidence-blocked`. |
| continuation | Compatible inputs that HCD.3, HCD.4, or a future programme comparison may consume, plus scope limits and reopen conditions. |

For each input that a conclusion needs and still lacks, explain what it would establish and what would allow reconsideration. Use the following fields where they apply.

| Missing-value field | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| missing kind | For example `later-Work-occurrence-missing`, `later-Work-result-claim-missing`, `result-record-missing`, `representative-observation-evidence-missing`, or a named external supplier result. |
| blocked conclusion | The exact conclusion that cannot be supported without this value. |
| available non-substitute, when relevant | If available material could plausibly be mistaken for the missing input, name it and explain why it cannot fill this gap. |
| retry condition | The input that must become available or be confirmed before reconsidering the named conclusion. State its required connection to the person, Work, and conditions, using only qualifiers that affect that conclusion. |

Use qualified direct observations when they suffice. If the claim depends on a result record, establish its connection to the Work and the result.

#### HCD.1:4.3 - Population and Reuse Boundary

A population use may return a distribution over separately identified member or representative demand accounts. It does not create one person's demand by averaging, and it does not turn the population into a capability holder. A population whole qualifies as a holder only through the independent-System condition of `E.23.CDI`, outside this one-human-holder pattern.

For another use, check that the person, configuration, later-Work conditions, horizon and evidence window support the new question or decision. Carry over the applicable limits. HCD.3 may consume the account as evidence input; HCD.4 may consume it as a scope and result frame. Programme comparison (`HCD.2`) may use the same frame. Deriving demand requires no programme-comparison result.

#### HCD.1:4.4 - What Changes in Practice

Ask “What must this person contribute in which later Work, under which conditions, and what evidence makes that demand current?” The answer either supports a bounded demand, makes a future hypothesis testable, returns the question to its owner, or exposes the exact missing evidence.

### HCD.1:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.1:5.1 - Constructed Positive Case: ImpactReview-17

`ImpactReview-17` is a constructed case. Its answer key, `ImpactReview-17-Domain-Oracle-v1`, supplies the engineering correctness and criticality criteria for `PumpWorks-Config-Baseline-42` and `AI-Assist-M4`. The review events and evidence below are stipulated case data.

The human holder is Engineer-P14. The later-Work family is independent review of AI-proposed change-impact claims for mixed physical/software pump-controller changes before separate integration, assurance, and release decisions. The constructed 2026-Q4 conditions include the named configuration and AI assistant, current source access, a forty-five-minute case limit, recoverable audit records, and bounded safety and maintenance specialist returns. Final integration, safety, release, and employment authority remain with their direct owners.

The stipulated work permits a routine reminder to construct and test an alternative configuration hypothesis. The engineer must supply the case-specific hypothesis and test, then decide whether to reject the AI claim. Remembering to initiate the operation without a reminder is a separate, stronger question.

The evidence packet stipulates eight representative review occurrences: four familiar and four unfamiliar variants; four include a plausible but wrong AI dependency claim; two require a specialist return; and every case requires a recoverable audit record. HCD.1 returns this human capability demand for Engineer-P14:

- recognize when the independent-review Method applies;
- trace each release-affecting claim to the current source and configuration;
- independently develop and test an alternative explanation before accepting a plausible AI claim;
- define the specialist contribution needed, obtain it when it is missing and retain the applicable result;
- return auditable evidence; and
- detect every seeded safety-critical omission within the protected time and authority boundary.

Within this example, the stipulated criteria and observations support `qualified current demand` for Engineer-P14. The case shows how to derive required human contributions from representative Work; demand does not establish the person's current capability. For an operational conclusion, use applicable domain criteria, any necessary specialist or safety inputs, and representative evidence for the person and Work in question.

#### HCD.1:5.2 - Missing Case: ReleaseWork-R9

For Engineer-E27, the accepted architecture supports a **prospective demand hypothesis** for 2026-Q4 `ReleaseWork-R9`: AI-output challenge, configuration-impact reasoning, evidence return, specialist coordination, critical-error detection, and adaptation across unfamiliar mixed physical/software variants may be required. The proposed requirements identify what to observe.

The stronger conclusion is blocked by distinct absent values:

| Missing value | Blocked HCD.1 use | Non-substitute and retry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `XRI-21-supplier-result-missing` | Any demand claim that consumes current engineering-culture enactment, its bounded practice-change decision, retained alternatives, or evidence gaps. | The current `SYSE.21` MethodDescription and its constructed PumpWorks demonstration can shape questions but are not the actual supplier result. Retry with a compatible actual `SYSE.21` result—or a receiver-permitted qualified direct substitute—for Engineer-E27, the Method, Work, period, and evidence use. |
| `later-Work-occurrence-missing` | Treating ReleaseWork-R9 itself as current later-Work evidence. | A plan, architecture, MethodDescription, or constructed occurrence does not establish enactment. Retry when an admitted performed Work occurrence identifies Engineer-E27, configuration, period, and actual performer. |
