The person can use the ordinary sources and tools permitted for the target. Establish whether a person, tool or task cue supplied the selection being judged.

Distinguish the relevant contributions as far as the observations allow.

| Contribution | A discriminating observation |
| --- | --- |
| Recognition | The person identifies the relevant difficulty before a diagnostic cue supplies it. |
| Access | The person retrieves or finds a usable response with the permitted resources. |
| Adaptation | The person changes the response when the new condition requires it and preserves the response when it still fits. |
| Enactment | The person carries out the response sufficiently to judge the contribution. |
| Result | The observed action or product meets or misses the applicable domain criteria, including relevant limits and consequences. |

An incorrect final answer can leave several contributions unresolved. Use an existing discriminating observation or a qualified differential when it would improve the requested explanation or response. Otherwise report the supported result and its limits.

Retain the first attempt and identify what any later feedback supplied. If the assessor names the method, the subsequent action can establish how the person applies it with that cue. Independent selection requires an observation before the selection was supplied.

#### HCD.12:4.4 - Return the transferred contribution and its boundary

For transfer, compare the new observations with the earlier claim under the named change. Preserve supported contributions even when another contribution fails. For new-source learning, return the source, access conditions, observations and limits specified in §4.5 instead of inventing a prior-performance claim.

State the change tested, the independent or helped contributions observed, any failed criteria and the uncertainty or variation the evidence leaves open. If a broader claim matters, establish whether suitable evidence already supports it and what further observation, if any, that claim needs. For a single unfamiliar case, name the contribution demonstrated in that case.

If performance returns after a cue, report what the person did with that cue. For a claim of independent recognition or independent adaptation, use suitable uncued evidence or, if it is missing and worth obtaining, select a fresh uncued case. Identify a task or access defect and the inference it prevents.

Finish when the supported finding or a precise limit answers the receiving question. Stronger reliance may require several unfamiliar cases, independent assessment, a coverage argument or evidence of domain correctness and access. Retain the familiar performance under its tested conditions when a transfer attempt fails.

Reopen only the contribution affected by a new variation, changed source or tool, corrected task, or stronger receiving use.

#### HCD.12:4.5 - Separate learning from a new source when that is the intention

For a new-source learning question, identify the method, prior preparation and what is known about familiarity. Identify what the source newly supplies, the source itself and the person's opportunity to use it. For a planned test, state these conditions before it begins. For an earlier attempt, recover them from suitable evidence. Finding a source and learning with it after equal access are different contributions.

Establish the conditions and observations that bear on the question. They may include prior familiarity, initial recognition, first application after access, adaptation, help, time, material errors, correction or unfinished work. Look for the operation the new method contributes. Familiar arithmetic can remain adequate while acquisition of the new method is still unestablished.

An observed first application after reading can establish what the person did under those learning conditions. To establish improvement, compare relevant performances. To establish the contribution of earlier preparation or a programme, use a comparison that distinguishes its effect. Retention needs evidence after the relevant delay. For faster learning at unchanged correctness, compare time and correctness under suitable conditions.

### HCD.12:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.12:5.1 - Transfer requires a positive proposal and a changed resource answer

Fictional learner L17 illustrates how to compare familiar and unfamiliar work.

In two earlier fresh cases, L17 checked configuration evidence and proposed a supported continuation without anyone cueing the mismatch. L17 rejected an FW7 report when HW3/FW8 was required, performed the calculation and explained C's 23-hour limit. Those observations supply the baseline for this case. They leave adaptation to changed capacity open.

The new case has a report that supports HW3/FW8/SCHED2 and confirms the required checks. Preparation takes one hour per homogeneous batch of up to four; required checks take two hours per change. Twelve changes arrive per week. At 24 available hours, ten changes require 23 hours, while twelve require 27. The release manager may authorize a bounded ten-change use and retains responsibility for the growing queue and release decision.

L17 has not rehearsed the evidence-use question with a complete report and no preceding mismatch problem. The new case warrants a positive proposal. Copying the earlier FW7 refusal would leave the available ten-change option unused. Reports, calculator and ordinary source and tool access are available. The traces place L17's first recognition and proposal before any teacher or AI cue identified the decisive condition.

| Observation | What it supports | What it does not support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before any PatternID or configuration cue, L17 checks the complete report and proposes ten changes in three homogeneous batches, requiring 23 hours, with two new changes left in the weekly queue. | Transfer of configuration-evidence use and a bounded positive proposal in this unfamiliar case. | Release authority, elimination of the queue or general transfer across all engineering work. |
| The assessor changes only available time from 24 to 22 hours. L17 initially keeps the ten-change promise. | A demonstrated adaptation failure under the changed resource condition. | A conclusion that the earlier configuration or calculation contribution has disappeared. |
| After feedback asking L17 to check the changed time constraint, L17 calculates that nine changes require 18 + 3 = 21 hours, while ten still require 23, and revises the proposal. | Correct adaptation with feedback. | Independent resource adaptation on the first changed-condition attempt. |

The observations support L17's tested calculation and configuration judgement. They show an initial capacity-adaptation error and a successful correction with feedback. For stronger reliance on independent capacity adaptation, use adequate uncued evidence or arrange a fresh uncued variation when a suitable observation is missing and its attainable contribution warrants the work. HCD.14 can already use this result to propose a small practice revision.

An assessor who accepts “the evidence is never sufficient, so I refuse” would miss the positive-action criterion in the first row. Scoring only the corrected final answer would also hide the error in L17's first response to the reduced capacity.

#### HCD.12:5.2 - The named Method supplies what the test meant to observe

In another constructed task the person makes no relevant first move. After the assessor names a method, the person uses it to produce a correct comparison. That observation supports application with a cue. Under the original task criterion, the first response may show a recognition error or leave uncued recognition unresolved.

If the work routinely supplies the method, application with that support may answer the question. If independent selection matters, use suitable evidence from an occasion when the person had to select the method. If that evidence is missing, select a worthwhile uncued task or state the limit.

#### HCD.12:5.3 - First Use of a Method Supplied by a New Source

Fictional learner S32 can read price and delivery tables and compare individual numbers. The preparation record contains no instruction on finding non-dominated alternatives, and no comparable performance was observed before source access. The question concerns what S32 can do after access to the handout. Successful earlier use of its two-measure method is not a prerequisite.

A one-page handout, *Compare Offers on Price and Delivery*, supplies the Method: with lower price and earlier delivery preferred, an offer dominates another only when it is no worse on either measure and better on at least one. Compare the offers pairwise and retain those that no other offer dominates. The handout includes a worked two-offer example. The result is a set of remaining choices; selecting one of them still needs the buyer's priorities and constraints.

After six minutes with the handout, S32 receives a different three-offer task: A costs 120 and arrives in four days; B costs 135 and arrives in three days; C costs 140 and arrives in five days. The criterion requires the retained set and grounds for each elimination or remaining trade-off. The sheet stays open; a calculator is permitted but unused. The teacher and AI supply no further explanation or answer. In seven minutes S32 retains A and B, eliminates C because A is both cheaper and earlier, and explains why neither A nor B dominates the other.

The assessor then changes C's price to 100, keeping its five-day delivery. With the sheet still available and no feedback on the first answer, S32 now retains all three and explains each price–delivery trade-off. Repeating the previous elimination would fail this task; comparing isolated numbers without the two-measure rule would also be insufficient.

The same observations support different conclusions for three questions.

| Question | Supported answer |
| --- | --- |
| What was performed after reading? | S32 applied the supplied Method and adapted its result in these two tasks with the handout available. The observation does not cover finding the source independently or later use without it. |
| Did S32's capability change? | A relevant comparison is missing. The first observed successful application cannot establish what S32 could do before source access or what will remain available later. |
| Did the earlier preparation help S32 learn? | This case does not isolate that contribution. Such a comparison would need relevant differences in preparation, the same learning opportunity and help conditions, and separate application tasks using new data. It remains open. |

### HCD.12:6 - Bias-Annotation

Unfamiliarity is person-relative. A task familiar to the assessor may be novel to the learner, and a nominally new task may have been rehearsed elsewhere. Use evidence of this person's relevant exposure to qualify the novelty claim.

Use the criterion for the required response. A blanket refusal can avoid one error and still miss a justified action. For an independent-adaptation claim, establish what the person recognized, changed or appropriately retained before an answer-bearing cue. For supported adaptation, identify the cue and what the person did with it.

### HCD.12:7 - Conformance Checklist

- A transfer claim has prior qualified performance for the same person and contribution. A new-source-learning question instead names relevant prior preparation, familiarity, the new source and its access conditions.
- For transfer, identify the material change and what is unfamiliar to this person. For new-source learning, identify what the source supplied and what is known about the person's relevant prior exposure.
- The task preserves the target or explicitly declares the new requirement.
- Positive action and refusal are distinguished where both matter.
- Where independent selection is claimed, the evidence places the person's selection before any cue that supplied it.
- Allowed sources, tools, help and first versus corrected attempts remain visible.
- The conclusion answers the declared transfer or new-source-learning question, with the contribution the observations support, help received, any demonstrated failures and material untested conditions.
- Claims about new-source learning, retention after a delay or authority to deploy have grounds appropriate to each.

### HCD.12:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Better move |
| --- | --- |
| “The names changed, so this is transfer.” | Identify the condition unfamiliar to this person and why it tests whether to retain or change the response. |
| “Every test contains a hidden error.” | When the work requires action on sufficient evidence, include a case in which proceeding is justified. |
| “I named the Method, and the person selected it.” | Report application after a cue; preserve selection as a separate question. |
| “The changed case failed, so the old capability is gone.” | Preserve the earlier finding in its tested conditions. Identify any failure or missing prerequisite the new observation establishes and leave its cause open when the evidence does not distinguish it. |
| “Reading a new source proves retention.” | Report what the person did with the source and the help received. Reading alone establishes neither learning nor retention. |

### HCD.12:9 - Consequences

A well-chosen unfamiliar case can distinguish copied execution, reliance on a cue and useful adaptation. Report the conclusion the receiving question needs within the bounds of the observations. It may identify a target for further practice or confirm the contribution under the tested change.

Establishing novelty and designing criteria take work. Broader claims need evidence over the relevant variation. Leave the cause of an ambiguous failure open. A higher final score or more frequent refusals can mask loss of justified action or increased dependence on feedback.

### HCD.12:10 - Rationale

To judge transfer, relate the person's demonstrated earlier contribution to the new conditions. Preserve the baseline and distinguish recognition, access, adaptation, enactment and result where the observations permit. That account shows which claims can be made and which further observation could change them.

### HCD.12:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**Working question:** how can an unfamiliar task distinguish useful transfer from repeated execution, while allowing learning resources when the intended work uses them?

**Selected line — adopt and adapt.** The [workplace-instruction review by Kraiger and Ford](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109) distinguishes instructional activity, learning and later transfer. HCD.12 turns that distinction into the prior-claim and changed-condition comparison in §4.1–§4.4, with the action-versus-refusal test in §5.1.

**Serious alternatives.** Repetition under new labels can practise execution. Evidence for adaptation requires a consequential change. A resource-free task can test a contribution that the person must supply unaided, while a task with a source can test learning with that source. With comparable task time, choose a variation that exposes the operation in question and state the resource conditions.

The historical [Schwartz and Martin preparation-for-future-learning study](https://aaalab.stanford.edu/assets/papers/2004/Inventing_to_prepare_for_future_learning.pdf) found that access to a later learning resource distinguished outcomes missed by a resource-free test in ninth-grade statistics. Section 4.5 adapts this design distinction. To claim that a particular adult programme accelerates learning, compare learning time and performance under conditions applicable to that programme.

Use a task whose criteria distinguish the contribution the transfer claim concerns. Reopen the comparison if prior exposure defeats the novelty claim, the variant changes an unacknowledged prerequisite, or source access and feedback cannot be separated from the claimed independent contribution.

### HCD.12:12 - Relations

For transfer, HCD.11 or equivalent qualified evidence can establish the earlier performance. A new-source learning question can start with the preparation and source conditions in §4.5. HCD.13 concerns delay and support dependence rather than novelty alone. HCD.14 can use a transfer limitation to revise an affected development assumption without waiting for every other assessment. HCD.3 owns diagnosis of a limiting human target when an unresolved cause matters to the requested explanation or a decision.

E.23.CAE can help distinguish recognition, access, adaptation, enactment and capability change. Recovery after restoring a condition or supplying a cue shows what the person did under that condition. A claim of transfer beyond the tested case requires other evidence.

Target-domain methods supply the grounds for judging the response and its correctness. Whoever designs the assessment selects tasks, timing and instruments for those criteria. This method explains which differences matter to transfer and new-source learning.

### HCD.12:End

## HCD.13 — Test Human Capability Retention and Dependence on Tools or Other Support

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.13:1 - Problem Frame

**Use this when** you need to establish what a person can still do after an interval or how their work depends on a tool or other support. For retention, recover an earlier qualified observation of the same contribution and its conditions. For support dependence, identify the support difference and the evidence needed to compare it.

For retention, report what the person demonstrated after the interval, under which support and with which intervening practice. For support dependence, report what the observed contrast shows under the conditions compared. State what remains unresolved. An established contribution can stand when a resource or configuration problem explains the interruption.

A retention claim requires an already demonstrated contribution. If earlier performance was never established, leave retention open. Use HCD.11 when the question requires a current performance assessment and HCD.12 for unfamiliar work. If a known unavailable source or failed tool explains the interruption, report that condition. Repair or seek the missing provision when the receiving task requires it.

Competent work can include using its required sources. Establish a separate working demand before testing a contribution without them. For stronger reliance in safety, credentialing, employment or deployment, use the applicable domain evaluation and assurance. If a decision is required, establish who is authorized to make it.

### HCD.13:2 - Problem

A delayed failure can arise from a change in practice, tasks, access, tools, cues, fatigue or the criterion, as well as from a change in capability. Testing only after a delay while also removing support confounds the two questions.

A successful delayed attempt can reflect continued use. A warm-up or earlier probe may have taught or primed the response, and a short exercise may cover only a few contributions. Report that history and scope. Retention without practice, broader mastery and unfamiliar transfer each need evidence under the conditions of that claim.

### HCD.13:3 - Forces

| Force | Working tension |
| --- | --- |
| Realistic delay and feasible observation | Use the interval that matters for work while accounting for time, assessor and access costs. |
| Retention and continued development | Describe intervening practice and instruction instead of treating every elapsed week as non-use. |
| Equipped work and independent contribution | Preserve required means and test a separately justified reduced-support target when the question calls for one. |
| Differential evidence and probe reactivity | A reference return can distinguish rivals, but the probe can itself teach, prime or fatigue the person. |
| Useful local claims and causal restraint | Return what the comparison supports without inventing a memory mechanism or programme effect. |

### HCD.13:4 - Solution

#### HCD.13:4.1 - Recover the earlier contribution and the intended interval

For retention, recover the person, contribution, criterion, earlier observations, relevant task variation, permitted means and evidence window. A recollection that the person could do the work needs supporting observations before it can serve as the baseline. If the evidence is inadequate for comparison, state the limit. Use suitable current evidence or assess now when the receiving use needs a current finding or a starting point for later comparison.

Establish the interval that matters to the work. For a planned observation, consider when the contribution will be needed, how long it may go unused, which support will remain available and the consequence of failure. For a past interval, recover its duration and conditions. An infrequent high-consequence task may warrant a different observation and assurance basis from routine work.

Establish intervening use, practice, instruction, changes in sources and which tools the person used, to the extent the evidence permits. Distinguish continued use from an interval without practice. An uncertain history limits the comparison.

#### HCD.13:4.2 - Compare delay under reference conditions

For a planned comparison, choose a delayed task that elicits the same contribution at a comparable demand and criterion. For an existing attempt, establish that comparability from the evidence. Use the earlier qualified support conditions for the reference comparison, or identify a material difference and its effect on the inference. Preserve the access required by the task.

When the question concerns performance before remedial teaching, use an observation made under that condition. Identify help, incomplete work, material errors and subsequent corrections. A changed criterion or source may change the requirement. Assess that requirement if the question calls for it and identify the original comparison it limits.

Compare earlier and delayed performance under the stated reference conditions. The result can establish retention across the tested interval and practice history. An explanation of the change needs evidence that distinguishes the relevant intervening influences.

#### HCD.13:4.3 - Test support dependence as a separate question

State which support matters and why. A tool contrast is useful when the question concerns working without it, the suitability of a fallback, or what the person contributed with the tool available.

For work under reduced support, identify the contribution required, data, permitted means, time and criteria. Preserve the accessibility aids and current sources required by that task. If the intended work requires unaided recall, state and justify that separate demand.

Match the available comparison to the question.

| Comparison | What it can answer |
| --- | --- |
| Earlier and delayed attempts with relevant reference support | What remains demonstrable after the interval under that support and recorded history. |
| Matched current attempts with a support difference material to the contribution | What the observed performance depends on in that contrast. |
| Only a delayed attempt with support also withdrawn | What happened in that combined condition; delay and withdrawal are not separately identified. |

Account for order, cueing, rehearsal and fatigue to the extent they affect the inference. In a planned comparison, control material effects where feasible. Use fresh comparable material or separate occasions when an earlier task could supply the answer. For a completed sequence, report material order effects and any remaining uncertainty. A reduced-support result covers the contributions tested under those conditions.

#### HCD.13:4.4 - Investigate apparent loss when its explanation matters

Check whether the current demand falls within the earlier claim. If it does not, state which condition has changed. If configuration or access already explains this interruption, use that finding for the question it answers.

When competing explanations matter to the requested finding or response, use an existing qualified comparison if it distinguishes them. If a new E.23.CAE differential is safe, permitted and worth its cost, use a previously successful or separately qualified reference condition without teaching the answer and vary the smallest condition that distinguishes the explanations. A reference–changed-condition–reference sequence can expose an order or transition effect.

Use observations to distinguish recognition, access, adaptation, enactment and result where they support those inferences. An incorrect final product can leave the location and cause of the failure unresolved.

Recovery without relearning under the qualified reference condition weighs against a global-loss explanation within that scope. For a claim about unfamiliar transfer or a memory mechanism, obtain the evidence that claim requires. If the probe supplies the answer, support effects remain inseparable, or the necessary contrast is unsafe, state the unresolved distinction.

Revise a capability claim when evidence about this person distinguishes a change in capability from relevant differences in the task or configuration. A single unsuccessful return, without evidence distinguishing those alternatives, does not establish capability loss.

#### HCD.13:4.5 - Return the supported conclusions

Report each conclusion the evidence supports. These may concern delayed performance with reference support, a separately tested reduced-support contribution, dependence on certain help, a difficulty in access, adaptation or execution, or a warranted change to a capability claim. Identify unresolved possibilities and consequential untested conditions.

State the relevant interval or support contrast, practice history where it bears on the comparison, conditions, observations, inference and limits. When further work is needed, it might be continued use, a discriminating observation, access repair, a proposed revision of a development assumption through HCD.14, or a specialist contribution. A choice about that work belongs to the authorized holder.

Finish when the supported finding answers the receiving question. If an unresolved limit prevents the intended reliance, identify it. Stronger reliance may require a qualified baseline, comparable tasks, broader observation, independent judgement or controls for learning during the probe. If further observation is needed, establish that the time, assessor and access it requires are available before relying on it.

Reopen only the affected claim when delay, use history, source, tool, task, criterion or intended reliance changes.

### HCD.13:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.13:5.1 - A matched eight-week comparison with an independent core

Fictional learner L17 illustrates a separately resourced follow-up with an assessor and source access. The observations below are stipulated for the comparison.

At reference time T0, a qualified assessment records three selected contributions associated with F.1, C.16 and C.11. The engineering tasks require HW3/FW8. A supplier report for FW7 cannot justify FW8; a complete HW3/FW8/SCHED2 report can support the stated configuration. SCHED2 requires two hours of checks per change and one hour of preparation per homogeneous batch of up to four. Ten changes require 23 hours, twelve require 27; at 24 available hours, a ten-change proposal leaves two of twelve new changes in the weekly queue. At 22 hours, nine changes require 21 and ten cannot be promised.

The existing alternatives are A, a second stand still requiring a shared-power check; B, the supplier option with the FW7 report; and C, the compatible SCHED2 arrangement with the stated capacity limit. Supplied financial assumptions give A/B/C approximate NPVs of 48.9/51.6/44.6 thousand. B ranks highest on the supplied financial assumptions. Its report establishes compatibility for FW7 only.

Two stipulated weekly logs each record ten accepted changes, all required checks completed and twelve arrivals; together they show four additional queued changes. The logs establish accepted changes and queue growth over those periods. The 23 hours come from the batch model. L17 uses the logs, configuration reports and assumptions to prepare a bounded recommendation. The release manager holds the release decision in this case.

The assignment is to determine whether L17 can resume preparing these recommendations eight weeks after T0. That date sets the interval for this local assessment. The stipulated history includes two intervening source-selection uses and one comparison exercise, with no rehearsal of the follow-up cases. The question concerns retention under intermittent practice.

At T0 and follow-up, the main task permits the framework and technical sources, calculator, AI assistance with search or calculation, and teacher clarification of instructions. Required accessibility aids remain available. In both constructed attempts, L17 uses AI only to open files L17 has already named; the teacher supplies no additional explanation. The recorded choices and reasoning precede any assistant output that could select the decisive sources, interpret the quantities or recommend an option. The main-task result therefore includes help with document access, while the selected judgements remain observable as L17's contributions.

| Selected contribution | Qualified observation at T0 | Constructed observation eight weeks later |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F.1: select sources that can change the current answer | L17 retains the exact configuration report and relevant resource/throughput evidence, explains each contribution, and excludes a general product brochure from the compatibility answer. | With a fresh comparable case and normal source access, L17 again selects the answer-changing sources and preserves the report's configuration limit. |
| C.16: preserve units, conditions and the distinction between a modelled quantity and an observed result | L17 distinguishes modelled hours per proposed batch plan from observed changes per week, and refuses to treat the former as measured throughput. | L17 preserves units, observation periods and the same distinction; a missing observed value remains unknown. |
| C.11: support a bounded comparison of existing options | L17 identifies the release manager as chooser, compares the given options against current compatibility and time conditions, and states the remaining check or queue consequence. | L17 gives the corresponding bounded recommendation without replacing a failed constraint by financial rank. |

The comparison covers these selected contributions from F.1, C.16 and C.11.

The same assignment starts with a fifteen-minute handoff in which the approved AI service is unavailable, but an accessible offline packet and calculator are available. L17 must still identify the required configuration, notice an unsupported report and reconstruct a feasible time-limited proposal for the release manager. That working requirement justifies the separate core; the later full recommendation can use normal sources and AI.

At both T0 and follow-up, the fifteen-minute core uses the supplied tables and calculator, with required accessibility aids, but no AI or teacher cue. In both constructed observations, L17 distinguishes the configuration and time constraints and explains why ten cannot be promised at 22 hours.

The reduced-support exercise precedes the source-dependent task on different material. Neither exercise includes corrective teaching before both are complete. This order supports a conclusion about the core under its conditions and equipped performance after that core. A claim about an entirely unwarmed first attempt requires an observation in that condition.

In this constructed case the compared contributions remained demonstrable over the eight weeks of intermittent practice under the stated support conditions. The separately tested core supports the contributions observed there. A claim about retention without practice, untested work or an intervention's causal effect needs different evidence.

#### HCD.13:5.2 - A failed source link changes the arrangement result

During an additional constructed source-dependent task, the required technical source is inaccessible. The earlier qualified contribution depended on using that source. The assessor can verify the access failure directly.

Report the verified access failure and identify what this attempt leaves unassessed. If the service must be restored, use an available remedy or seek the responsible provider's contribution. Qualify any later observation with restored access by its own conditions.

#### HCD.13:5.3 - Recovery after a cue narrows an apparent-loss claim

In a separate constructed comparison, the person does not select a familiar Method for the current problem. Without teaching its content, the assessor supplies a previously qualified task cue; the person then produces the familiar response. If that cue is a legitimate reference condition and the contrast addresses the live rival, the result supports availability under that condition and a possible selection difficulty.

The observation supports performance with the cue. Uncued selection, unfamiliar transfer and the mechanism of remembering each require their own evidence. If the cue also teaches the solution, the resulting response cannot distinguish access to an earlier capability from relearning after a loss.

### HCD.13:6 - Bias-Annotation

Consider changes in access, support, practice or task before attributing a difference to forgetting or resilience. If required assistive technology was removed, that observation alone does not warrant lowering the person's capability assessment for work with the aid.

Repeated probes can favour people who learn from the test itself. Use the practice history and test order to determine which retention claim a later improvement can support.

### HCD.13:7 - Conformance Checklist

- For a retention claim, earlier qualified evidence concerns the same person and contribution, or its absence is identified as the limit.
- For a delayed comparison, the account names the interval and the known history of intervening practice. Material gaps limit the conclusion.
- Delay and support questions have separate interpretable comparisons, or the combined-condition limit is stated.
- If a reduced-support core is used, it has its own justified target and preserves required access arrangements.
- Help, feedback, unfinished work and probe reactivity remain visible.
- Any apparent-loss differential uses a qualified reference and addresses live rivals without hidden teaching.
- Retention, support dependence, access difficulty and capability-loss claims remain distinct.
- The result identifies which contributions and conditions were tested, its limits, whether it suffices for the intended use and what would warrant reopening it. It identifies resources for further observation when the receiving use requires that work.

### HCD.13:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Better move |
| --- | --- |
| “Eight weeks passed, so this is retention without practice.” | Recover the use history and qualify the conclusion. |
| “The delayed no-tool test failed, so the person forgot.” | Separate delay from support withdrawal or report the combined condition. |
| “The answer returned after coaching, so there was no loss.” | Distinguish a qualified no-relearning return from newly taught performance. |
| “The fifteen-minute core proves the whole course.” | State its selected contributions and preserve untested coverage. |
| “The follow-up is in the plan, so resources exist.” | Verify that the planned observation has the time, assessor and access it requires. Obtain any missing provision if the observation is to proceed. |

### HCD.13:9 - Consequences

The result can support continued use, identify an access repair or locate a remaining uncertainty. A short independent core may answer an important fallback question while leaving normal source-dependent work intact.

A retention comparison requires a suitable baseline. The known intervening history determines how specifically the result can be described. Further observations can cost time and access, and some causes may remain unresolved. A single score can hide tool withdrawal, teaching during a probe, a change in the work or that only a narrow contribution was tested.

### HCD.13:10 - Rationale

Elapsed time establishes the interval of a comparison. Explaining a performance change requires evidence that distinguishes the relevant conditions. Using a required support can be part of competent work. A qualified return can show what the person can do under reference conditions. When a support failure explains the interruption, address it if needed and retain the established capability finding within its scope.

### HCD.13:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**Working question:** what can a delayed assessment show when practice and support can also change performance?

**Selected line — adopt and adapt.** [Carpenter, Pan and Butler's review](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44159-022-00089-1) supports spacing and retrieval as bounded learning approaches; the [classroom-testing meta-analysis by Yang and colleagues](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33683913/) reinforces that testing conditions can affect learning. HCD.13 therefore records intervening practice and probe reactivity in §4.1–§4.4 instead of treating a test as a passive reading.

**Serious alternative.** One earlier assisted score and one delayed unassisted score can describe performance in those two conditions at low cost. To distinguish delay from withdrawing assistance, compare performance under reference support and add a support contrast if the question requires it. If that contrast is unaffordable, return the finding the combined observation supports.

The [Bastani and colleagues AI study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40560616/) supports the distinction between assisted and unassisted performance in school mathematics. Section 4.3 uses it to define the separate reduced-support target, illustrated by the two assessments in §5.1. Claims about adult occupational performance or long-term retention need evidence under relevant conditions. Use E.23.CAE if a qualified reference comparison is needed to explain apparent loss.

Use the work to justify the interval and evidence from the relevant programme to assess its effect. The cited studies inform the comparison design; the observations in §5.1 are stipulated. Reopen the conclusion if changes in task comparability, practice history, required access or teaching during the probe affect the inference.

### HCD.13:12 - Relations

HCD.11 or equivalent qualified evidence can supply the prior or current performance that the claim requires. HCD.12 concerns meaningful unfamiliarity, which may coexist with delay but needs its own claim. HCD.14 can use a retention or support finding to revise the affected development assumption.

For an unresolved apparent-loss question, E.23.CAE supplies the qualified differential when the comparison is needed. A known configuration failure can answer the explanation. If a repair is required, use A.15.8 as applicable and involve the relevant provider when its contribution is needed. E.23.CDI qualifies claims about capability development for the person and Work family concerned. A claim about an intervention’s effect needs evidence linking it to the change.

Use target-domain criteria and applicable specialist results to judge correctness. Whoever arranges an assessment establishes the needed times, tasks, instruments and resources. Measurement, causal and stronger assurance claims each require their own applicable specifications and evidence.

### HCD.13:End

## HCD.14 — Revise the Human Capability-Development Arrangement from Evidence

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.14:1 - Problem Frame

**Use this when** an observation of performance, transfer, delayed work or support dependence calls an assumption about a person's development arrangement into question. Identify which assumption the evidence bears on and what it supports under the observed conditions.

The finding identifies which assumption the evidence supports, changes or leaves open. If a revision is requested, name the component to change, the improvement expected, the contributions to protect and an observation that could justify retaining, adapting or rejecting it. One compatible HCD.11, HCD.12 or HCD.13 result, or equivalent evidence, can suffice.

The arrangement includes tasks, practice, feedback, sources, tools, providers and other conditions for development. Its design may rely on a local model of proficiency and how it can change. Distinguish a finding about the person, a revision of the model and a change to the learning plan. When revision is warranted, identify the smallest part whose revision would address the finding. Propose or carry out that change as the task requires.

If a score obscures the underlying contribution or observation, use an applicable record or identify the evidence that is missing. Use the responsible practice for clinical treatment, professional correctness, safety, employment or a missing domain method. Seek its specialist or authority when a required contribution is unavailable. A source revision can change the task while the person's previously demonstrated capability remains supported.

### HCD.14:2 - Problem

A development plan assumes that its tasks will elicit the required contribution, feedback will help, support will remain available and practice will prepare the person for later work. Evidence can overturn one hypothesis while leaving the others usable.

Two failures are common. One repeats the same exercise more often without identifying the discrepancy. The other redesigns everything, losing supported contributions and spending resources without evidence that the whole arrangement was at fault. Both can conceal a defective assessment, a cue that supplied the answer, or an unavailable source behind a claim that the person needs more training.

### HCD.14:3 - Forces

| Force | Working tension |
| --- | --- |
| Action and causal uncertainty | Propose a bounded testable change when useful without pretending that one miss establishes its cause. |
| Local repair and shared causes | Preserve working components while enlarging the change when evidence shows that several failures share a cause. |
| Learning and assessment | Distinguish the contribution feedback supplies from the work the person performs with it. If the target requires independent selection or adaptation, observe that part before the answer-bearing cue. |
| Professional Method and local tailoring | Adapt a qualified development Method to the case without inventing expertise from a pattern label. |
| Improvement and protection | A gain in speed or score is unacceptable if it damages a required contribution, access or resource limit. |

### HCD.14:4 - Solution

#### HCD.14:4.1 - Identify the assumption affected by the evidence

Identify the person, intended later Work, human contribution, observation and use of the judgement. State which component was expected to help and which assumption is under examination.

State what the observation establishes. If it differs from the expectation, describe that difference in observable terms. For example, the person applies the capacity rule after a cue but keeps the old promise when the available time changes. Retain successful contributions and the conditions in which they were observed.

If the evidence and target concern different people, work families, configurations or periods, qualify their relation before using the result. Use attributable evidence about this person before identifying their limiting contribution.

#### HCD.14:4.2 - Distinguish explanations that matter to the finding or revision

If the observation differs from the expectation, consider the plausible explanations. Establish which differences matter to the requested finding, the grounds for retaining the arrangement or a possible change.

| Live explanation | Finding or possible response |
| --- | --- |
| The target or later-Work demand changed | Identify the changed demand and retain the old claim within its conditions. Seek a new demand decision from the appropriate holder if it is still needed. |
| The task, criterion or scoring is defective | Identify the defect and the judgement it prevents. Use a suitable existing observation if it answers the question. If further evidence is needed, repair the assessment and obtain a discriminating observation where feasible. Limit the conclusion about learning until adequate evidence is available. |
| Required source, tool, time or access was absent | State the missing condition and the limit it places on the inference about the person. If continued work needs that provision, restore it under applicable authority or seek it from the provider. |
| A cue supplied recognition or adaptation that the target requires the person to contribute independently | If further practice is needed, adjust the cue and the task so the person can attempt that contribution before the cue. For a claim of independent performance, use evidence that locates the response before the cue. |
| The development Method or provider does not fit the target | Identify the mismatch. For a needed replacement, use a compatible method or provider contribution and check its fit to the target. |
| The evidence supports a limiting human capability, misconception or behaviour | Identify that target and retain any relevant unresolved explanation. When a development change is needed, select one qualified for the target. |

A short inspection can establish a missing source or incorrect criterion. Use HCD.3 when a human diagnosis remains unresolved and the finding or response needs it. Use a qualified E.23.CAE differential when distinguishing access, selection, adaptation, enactment or apparent loss matters to that question. An affordable reversible trial can be warranted while the cause remains open if the competing explanations leave its use safe and informative.

One well-observed miss can justify a bounded revision hypothesis. State what could disconfirm it and identify any credible competing explanation. When the evidence is insufficient even for that proposal, identify the limit and any attainable observation worth obtaining.

##### HCD.14:4.2.1 - Decide Whether the Model or the Pathway Must Change

A surprising result can change different things. Use the observation and its conditions to identify the affected claim before prescribing another exercise.

| What the observation changes | Appropriate revision |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence for this person's current contribution, while the descriptions and relations still fit | Update the current profile and retain the model. Use the new evidence for a further decision when one is needed. |
| A category merges different strategies, a purported prerequisite is bypassed, or an omitted condition explains contradictory positions | Use HCD.4:4.2.1–HCD.4:4.3.1 if the local proficiency model needs revision. Revise the description or relation and identify which pathway assumptions used it. |
| The model remains useful but the selected task, help, provider, time or learning mechanism does not fit | Identify the affected pathway assumption and preserve the supported model claims. For a needed revision, use the applicable contribution from HCD.5–HCD.10. |
| The observation itself is defective or cannot distinguish the rival accounts | State the inference the observation leaves unresolved. Use a suitable existing observation or repair the assessment through HCD.11 when further evidence is warranted. |

For a model revision, say what the earlier model predicted, which observation it cannot accommodate adequately, what a proposed replacement distinguishes, and what evidence could challenge it. Reconsider dependent learning opportunities without reopening unrelated contributions. A plausible revised model may support a bounded next trial while its broader developmental claims remain untested.

Retain the tasks attempted, help received, first responses and subsequent corrections under their original conditions. Add the new interpretation and any resulting plan. A claim that the person gained or lost capability requires evidence of their work.

#### HCD.14:4.3 - Specify the positive revised arrangement

For a proposed revision, identify what would change and describe the replacement in terms someone could carry out. For example, replace a cue-led explanation with contrasting cases, obtain the learner's first explanation before feedback, then use a suitable fresh case to test independent selection.

For a change that requires a development method, use a qualified source or provider result and check its target, learner conditions, prerequisites, support and limits. If the method or provider competence is still missing, state which part of the proposed revision depends on it.

Identify the protections affected by the change, including relevant successful contributions, required checks, accessibility, sources, tools, cost or time limits and specialist responsibilities. Change the target itself only when its holder has authorized that change, directly or through a rule or delegation covering it.

#### HCD.14:4.4 - Pair the change with a test and stopping rule

For a revision to be tested, state the expected observable difference, a meaningful failure condition and any observation that could distinguish a competing explanation. Use suitable existing evidence or a fresh task when new evidence is needed.

Design the test to elicit the affected contribution with the support permitted for the target. For a claim of independent performance, obtain evidence of the required contribution before an answer-bearing cue. Keep the domain criteria, distinguish first performance from correction after feedback, and check the intended gain and affected protections.

Set acceptable learner and practitioner costs, required resources and timing for the proposed test. Add a delayed observation only when needed for the claim. HCD.13 can supply that comparison given sufficient resources and qualified evidence.

State which outcomes would support retaining, adapting or abandoning the change, or seeking a missing contribution. A local before-and-after comparison can guide a reversible choice. Estimating the causal effect requires a design and evidence that distinguish the change from relevant alternatives.

#### HCD.14:4.5 - Distinguish proposal, authorization and performed change

Return a proposal when that is the requested result or when implementation still needs resources or authority. Identify the missing contribution and its holder, when known. A supplied contribution or standing authorization can already satisfy its corresponding condition.

When implementation is part of the task and the change is authorized and resourced, the responsible practitioner can carry it out. Establish separately what was proposed, authorized and performed, and what was subsequently observed about the learner.

Stop if the change would breach a protected condition or exceed the mandate. Restore the prior working component when restoration is needed, safe, feasible and authorized.

#### HCD.14:4.6 - Update the hypothesis from the new observation

Retain the change provisionally when the intended contribution improves under the test conditions without unacceptable loss. Adapt it when the result narrows the useful conditions or identifies a more local problem. Abandon or return it when the decisive prediction fails, a protected contribution worsens or the professional basis no longer fits.

Preserve unchanged claims and surviving rivals. Reopen only the assumptions affected by new evidence. Enlarge the revision when a changed demand or adequate evidence shows the problem extends beyond the local component. A shared failed assumption is one such reason.

### HCD.14:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.14:5.1 - A local revision at the transfer return

The fictional case begins with L17's transfer assessment. It develops a proposal before a delayed test is needed.

The earlier evidence supports calculation and configuration checking. In a new case, L17 correctly uses a complete HW3/FW8/SCHED2 report and proposes ten changes within 24 available hours. Required checks take two hours per change; preparation takes one hour per homogeneous batch of at most four. Ten changes need 23 hours, twelve need 27, so a ten-change proposal leaves two of twelve new weekly changes in the queue. The release manager retains release/use authority.

When available time changes to 22 hours, L17 initially keeps the ten-change promise and corrects it only after feedback. Nine changes need 21 hours. The earlier calculation and configuration findings remain supported in their tested conditions.

The prior practice exercise used a teacher question to point out the changed resource condition. The live hypothesis is that practice did not sufficiently require L17 to detect and adapt to that change before the cue. A single miss does not settle the cause: unclear task wording remains a rival, and general resource reasoning may also need investigation.

For this constructed case, the programme owner has supplied a compatible case-practice Method and a qualified practitioner. The Method asks the learner to attempt a case, explain the consequential choice, compare it with a contrasting case, receive criterion-based feedback, and attempt fresh material. Those are stipulated professional inputs to the example.

The proposal changes the cue-led resource exercise.

| Element | Revision hypothesis and protection |
| --- | --- |
| Component changed | Replace only the cue-led resource exercise. Leave the supported financial calculation and configuration practice in place. |
| First five minutes | Recover L17's explanation of the earlier promise and inspect whether the task clearly presented the changed time. If it did not, repair the task before interpreting the miss as a practice problem. |
| Twenty minutes of practice | Use contrasting cases requiring a supported ten-change proposal at 24 hours and refusal of that same promise at 22 hours, with a feasible nine-change proposal. Obtain L17's first explanation before feedback names the decisive condition. |
| Ten-minute fresh test | Give unrehearsed 20-hour and 28-hour variants with complete compatible reports and twelve new weekly changes. Do not name the resource Method or point to the changed number. |
| Expected contribution | At 20 hours, eight changes require 18 hours and nine require 21: do not promise nine. At 28 hours, twelve require 27: a proposal to meet those twelve is supported. Preserve required checks, source fit and any existing-queue limitation. |
| Protected conditions | Same source and calculator access, ordinary permitted AI assistance, accessibility arrangements, domain criteria and separate release authority. Observe L17's first recognition and explanation in the source and assistant traces; a teacher or AI cue that supplies recognition of the changed condition counts as help. |
| Cost and status | Forty learner minutes including a final five-minute result discussion, plus fifteen practitioner preparation minutes, within the example's proposed replacement allocation. The return is a proposal until its responsible owner authorizes that use of time. |

The fresh task tests whether L17 can limit the promise at 20 hours and make a justified positive proposal at 28 hours. Refusing both misses the supported twelve-change proposal. The release manager retains the decision in both cases.

#### HCD.14:5.2 - The next observation decides the smallest update

If the test is authorized and conducted, interpret the observed response under its conditions.

| New observation | Update to the hypothesis |
| --- | --- |
| Both fresh uncued first attempts adapt the promise correctly and preserve configuration checking and calculation | Retain the local change provisionally for these tested variants; do not claim a general transfer effect. |
| Correct answers appear only after a teacher or AI cue names the changed resource | Identify what the learner did after receiving the cue. The independent result remains open unless other evidence establishes it. Use a cue comparison if the remaining question warrants it. |
| The time value is ambiguous or a required source is unavailable | Identify the affected part of the assessment or its access. The attempt leaves the dependent learning contribution unassessed. If further assessment is required, use a suitable existing observation or restore the missing condition before relying on a new attempt. |
| Adaptation improves but configuration checking or required checks deteriorate | Revise or abandon the change: the intended gain does not compensate for the protected loss. |
| Further qualified observations show several tasks depend on the same missing prerequisite | Identify the affected tasks and prerequisite. If the target or arrangement needs revision, enlarge it accordingly and obtain any necessary diagnostic, method or authority contribution. |

If delay or support dependence matters, a later HCD.13 observation can update the hypothesis. Establishing whether the revision caused the result requires evidence for that causal claim.

#### HCD.14:5.3 - Revise a Proficiency Relation before Advancing a Pathway

In the constructed N24 case (HCD.4:5.5 and HCD.6:5.6), independent selection succeeds in a new service context and fails in a familiar one; across four tasks the response also differs with the salient label. Retaining a single familiar-before-unfamiliar position would conceal the difference that changes the next teaching move.

In the constructed N24 case, the local revision separates cue-compatible selection from selection under a misleading cue, drops the assumption that new-context success entails reliable familiar-context selection and preserves arithmetic. The new hypothesis proposes cue contrast and a learner-generated unit check. Its proposed twenty-minute opportunity fits the remaining learner and teacher allocation; a fresh misleading-heading task could challenge it. Preserve the observed misses and successes. The changed proficiency model supports a proposed pathway change. Its effect on N24 would require evidence from using that change.

### HCD.14:6 - Bias-Annotation

A familiar teaching technique can become the default response to every failure. Compare credible assessment, support and target explanations before selecting it as the remedy. If the question concerns the cause, use evidence that distinguishes the competing explanations. An affordable, reversible and sufficiently informative trial of a remedy can be warranted while the cause remains uncertain.

Check whether a revision compromised independent selection, source access, correctness, workload, confidence in a justified action or another protected contribution. A rising score alone does not resolve those questions.

### HCD.14:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The account identifies the observation, the assumption it bears on and what it establishes, or the specific judgement still open. If it proposes retention or revision, its grounds cover that person and work.
- The conclusion retains successful contributions and any competing explanations that matter to its use.
- A proposed change identifies the component and an executable replacement. A decision to retain the arrangement or a finding of insufficient evidence has its own grounds.
- When the revision needs a development Method or professional input, its fit or the specific gap is established.
- If a trial is proposed, the expected observation, task, cost, protections and stopping rule are explicit.
- Proposal, authorization, performed work and outcome remain distinct.
- Retain, adapt, abandon and return conditions affect the smallest justified claim or component.
- No whole-programme causal effect or new development direction is inferred from a local comparison.

### HCD.14:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Better move |
| --- | --- |
| “The score fell, so prescribe more practice.” | Recover the contribution and observation. Distinguish the causes that matter to the requested finding or to a proposed revision. |
| “One miss proves the training Method failed.” | Identify the hypothesis the observation supports and what existing or obtainable evidence could distinguish it from a credible rival. |
| “Replace the whole course.” | Preserve supported components and enlarge the change only when evidence warrants it. |
| “The new plan means the person has developed.” | Separate the proposal, performed work and observed outcome. |
| “The final score rose, so the revision worked.” | Use evidence of the targeted human contribution and protected conditions. Establish the grounds for any claim that the revision caused a gain. |

### HCD.14:9 - Consequences

The practitioner can return a supported change, a proposal to test, grounds for keeping the arrangement or a concrete reason why the evidence is insufficient. Local revision preserves independently supported contributions and exposes the cost and evidence the next use would require.

A missing contribution may concern the assessment, a source or a provider. A locally supported change can be retained while broader transfer or delayed retention remains untested.

### HCD.14:10 - Rationale

A development arrangement depends on claims about how the person will prepare for later work. Revise the smallest assumption or component the evidence warrants. A bounded test can be worthwhile while a causal alternative remains live if its expected contribution warrants the cost and the protections can be maintained.

### HCD.14:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**Working question:** how should performance evidence change development when the cause may lie in the task, feedback, support or learning?

**Selected line — adopt and adapt.** The [Kraiger and Ford workplace-instruction review](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109) separates instructional design, learner activity, learning outcomes and work transfer. HCD.14 uses those distinctions to locate the affected assumption in §4.1–§4.3 and retain other programme findings that still have support.

**Serious alternative:** repeat or redesign the whole course after a poor result. That may be appropriate when the demand or evidence shows a broad mismatch. It wastes supported contributions when only one cue-led exercise is implicated. At comparable decision effort, a component revision can specify the change, a test and the results to protect. A small trial supports an update within its tested conditions.

The [Bastani and colleagues study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40560616/) makes assistance design a credible rival in its school-mathematics setting; it supplies no adult-provider prescription. The [Yang and colleagues testing synthesis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33683913/) makes testing and feedback conditions relevant to learning. Sections 4.4 and 5.2 distinguish the learner's first attempt from a correction. A claim about the cause of later improvement needs separate evidence.

Reopen the revision if a protected contribution worsens, a rival explanation changes the useful repair, the supplied professional Method does not fit, or broader observations overturn the local scope. The §5.1 proposal makes a prediction to be tested. A completed authorized test can support, narrow or defeat that prediction under its conditions.

### HCD.14:12 - Relations

Use applicable evidence of observed performance, transfer, delay or support, including a suitable HCD.11, HCD.12 or HCD.13 result. HCD.3 supplies a qualified limiting target or non-training return when diagnosis remains unresolved. HCD.4 can use changed contribution evidence in its existing profile comparison.

HCD.5, HCD.6, HCD.9 and HCD.10 supply development methods, practice, providers or support under their own conditions. Use a qualified contribution when the revision needs it. If it is unavailable, identify the missing method or provider result and the proposal that depends on it.

E.23.CAE supplies a useful differential when apparent loss, access or expression is at issue. C.11 governs a choice among existing alternatives when its chooser and comparison conditions apply. Target, resource and programme holders retain their respective decisions. A causal-effect claim requires an applicable causal evaluation, including C.28 when its question is live.

For a concrete programme or instrument, the Learning Product holder can authorize a change under its mandate, and the assigned performer can carry it out. The person's development direction, commitment, clinical care and employment are separate questions. An HCD finding can inform the corresponding decision holder.

### HCD.14:End

## HCD.15 — Sustain Continuing Human Capability Development

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.15:1 - Problem Frame

**Use this when** a programme ends, a development assumption changes or a successful work episode raises a worthwhile question about a particular person’s contribution. The question may concern what happened, what to retain or what the person will need as the work, tools or qualification conditions change.

Begin with the person, the later work and the question the evidence opens. Section 4.2.1 can also help the person find a worthwhile question in a successful episode and learn what to retain. If continuing development is needed, specify what should trigger it, the practice and support contributions, the evidence and reassessment, the responsible performers and decision holders, the protected conditions, the burden, and when to resume or stop.

Retain what the evidence supports. Reopen the part affected by a change and obtain evidence sufficient for its intended use. Credit, attendance, membership and a booked session can each establish a different fact about participation or access.

For a one-off local adjustment already settled by **HCD.14**, use that result. Whole-programme comparison belongs to **HCD.2**. Current operations, organizational change, career or employment allocation, clinical treatment and professional-community design have their own Methods. Use the relevant result or seek the missing contribution when the development question depends on it.

### HCD.15:2 - Problem

A change in later work can affect the reach of a capability claim. Relevant changes include the Method, configuration, tool or AI system, a critical-error finding, support, the qualification window or new evidence of transfer or retention. Establish which condition matters to the person’s work.

Recurring activity can hide a missing opportunity to perform the contribution the later work requires. Renewed credits, community attendance, familiar exercises and tool access may leave it untested. Repeating an entire programme after a local change can also displace useful practice and discard contributions that already work.

For a continuing arrangement, identify what can reopen the question, what would answer it, what work or observation is needed, who can act and when to stop. Claims about completed development or a change in capability require evidence of those events.

### HCD.15:3 - Forces

| Force | Working tension |
| --- | --- |
| Continuity and change | Preserve supported capability claims and arrangement components while responding to material changes in later Work. |
| Cadence and evidence | Keep useful opportunities available without letting a calendar become the reason for development. |
| Participation and capability | Use practice, feedback, supervision and communities as contributions while requiring direct evidence for relied-on capability claims. |
| Access and independence | Permit tools, AI and specialist support needed in real Work while separately observing contributions that must survive changed or withdrawn support. |
| Provider service and holder development | For a service the arrangement would rely on, establish the needed provider capability, access and operating conditions. Use evidence of the provider’s work to support a service claim and evidence of the person’s work to judge their development. |
| Improvement and burden | Reassess often enough to protect the later-Work use without imposing unnecessary tests, surveillance, workload, or exclusion. |
| Action and authority | Return a usable arrangement while distinguishing proposal, authorization, performed development Work, later Work, evidence, and decision. |

### HCD.15:4 - Solution

#### HCD.15:4.1 - Fix the holder, later Work, and current claim window

Identify the person, later-work family and material conditions. If the question concerns a capability claim, recover the claim and the interval its evidence covers. State the requested finding or decision and the consequences it must protect. Use the applicable domain or specialist criteria for correct, safe or useful performance.

State what the available evidence establishes and any uncertainty that affects the question. A successful work record can yield a bounded learning question before it supports a capability conclusion. A programme design, prior assessment, credential, community record, MethodDescription or planned work arrangement can frame that question. A claim about present capability or completed later work needs evidence covering that person, contribution and time.

If a necessary fact about the person, work, evidence, configuration or intended use remains uncertain, identify it and any available way to establish it. Use an applicable observation or source, seek a needed contribution from its holder, or return the limit. Establish the fit of a generic role plan before applying it to an individual.

#### HCD.15:4.2 - Recover the smallest affected development question

Use a compatible **HCD.14** revision hypothesis or other qualified evidence to identify the assumption in question. A successful episode may raise a question about repeating a sound action, understanding its limits or improving it. Use §4.2.1 where its explanation matters. Retain unaffected claims, tasks, feedback, support, provider contributions, accessibility and specialist boundaries.

For a changed condition, establish which assumption it affects, if any. A changed AI configuration may reopen independent challenge while leaving source tracing intact. A failed delayed observation may reopen retention without reopening a demonstrated fresh-task contribution. An unavailable specialist may block one later-Work condition without proving a human deficit.

Enter directly from evidence that fits the person and work. If one local revision answers the question and no continuing arrangement is needed, the **HCD.14** result suffices.

##### HCD.15:4.2.1 - Learn from a Successful Work Episode

Examine a successful episode when its explanation matters to the requested finding, a future action or a development choice. Select a consequential decision or operation. The successful outcome can depend on the person’s action, tools, help or favourable conditions. Where the relevant grounds and limits are already known and no worthwhile question remains, use them and finish the inquiry.

**Recover what happened before explaining it.** Establish what counted as success under the work’s criteria. Use relevant plans, work products, logs or corrections to reconstruct the action, help and conditions that preceded the result. Consult a participant when their observation is needed. Distinguish what the person knew at the time from later information and from information they could have obtained but did not. A later recollection alone cannot establish a first independent attempt.

**Form an explanation the episode can test.** When the person is learning from their own work, have them identify what they noticed, what they chose, why it could have mattered and under which conditions. Use an existing explanation if it already supplies this connection. Compare it with the records of the action and any help. For instance, the exception log can show whether its flagged mappings were compared with the source before acceptance.

**Compare plausible explanations.** Identify observations that support or challenge each account and any observation that could distinguish them. Detection by automation, a rule supplied by a colleague or a case without the relevant difficulty may explain part of the success. Use the sequence, work products, subject evidence or a participant’s relevant observation. Seek further evidence if the attainable improvement to the finding or its use justifies retrieval, attention and displaced work. If the alternatives remain open, give the supported part and the unresolved question.

**State the bounded lesson.** Identify the person’s observed action and help, the conditions of the episode and the result. Say which connection the evidence supports, which explanation remains proposed and what could defeat reuse. For example, with the same source format, approved checks and mapping help, retain the comparison of exceptions with the source. A new format or missing check can reopen its fit. A better explanation can support keeping the existing procedure.

Return the supported lesson. If a question remains, use the applicable continuation.

| What the comparison establishes | Useful next move |
| --- | --- |
| The action and its present conditions are supported, and no development question remains. | Retain the action and return to Work. Keep the condition that would reopen the question. |
| The practical action remains warranted, but the person's explanation overstates its contribution. | Revise the explanation and have the person use the corrected distinction in a bounded example when that understanding matters. A change to the work procedure does not follow automatically. |
| A changed case could expose a needed distinction or adaptation. | If the attainable result justifies the work, select a safe, representative application with a criterion, permitted help, time, feedback and a stopping condition. For the completed attempt, record help used. Preserve the first response when independent use is at issue. |
| A decisive fact, subject rule, permission or support contribution is missing. | Identify the missing input and the conclusion or action it limits. Use an available fact or applicable rule, seek a needed decision or contribution from its holder, or return the open condition. |

Use **HCD.23:4.1–HCD.23:4.3** when another person needs to reconstruct or challenge the explanation: give them the bounded event and evidence, with any material competing account or unresolved connection. Use **HCD.24:4.4–HCD.24:4.6** when learning to judge or respond to that judgement is the purpose. For an intended use in another project, **HCD.25:4.2–HCD.25:4.5** develops comparison of the qualified source case, receiving conditions and a difference that could defeat reuse. An adequate conclusion about the person’s own case can finish the task.

If the next step is practice, use **HCD.6** and **HCD.7**, or a compatible existing result, to provide the task and support. Use **HCD.9** as needed for feedback, correction or reasoned retention. Provide for the attempt and the use of feedback. Count preparation, evidence retrieval, case comparison, learner and provider time and any promised follow-up. If a contribution is unavailable, narrow or defer the affected activity and retain the lesson already supported.

Distinguish the next observation from the original episode. If a colleague supplied the decisive relation, identify what the person did with that help. An independent contribution would need evidence under conditions in which it was theirs to supply. A first response to a changed condition supplies a separate observation. For a claim about performance, transfer or retention, use **HCD.11–HCD.13** as applicable. For a claim that the review caused learning, establish the connection to the change. Stop the added development when its question is answered.

**Recognition and assurance.** A person may want to repeat a success while their own contribution and its enabling conditions remain unclear. For consequential reliance, use compatible subject criteria and evidence that addresses the intended finding or action. A successful total, recollection or agreement among participants may leave the contribution unresolved.

#### HCD.15:4.3 - Make triggers decision-bearing

Name the changes or observations that can reopen the affected question. Useful triggers include:

- a material change in later Work, its Method, configuration, tool, AI behavior, or specialist interface;
- a critical error, failed unfamiliar transfer, changed delayed performance, or changed support dependence;
- a successful work episode whose unexplained contribution or possible reuse raises a consequential development question;
- loss or change of provider, source, supervision, access, fallback, protected time, or permitted support;
- expiry of a qualification or evidence window that matters to the receiving decision;
- a source contradiction or target-domain result that changes the relied-on claim; or
- a newly relevant specialist, safety, clinical, legal, employment, or operating result.

Use an interval when elapsed time changes the reach of the evidence or the opportunity for later work. An annual qualification rule, a retention interval or expiring access can justify a calendar trigger. Name the condition and the finding or action it reopens.

#### HCD.15:4.4 - Configure the contributions that can answer the question

Select the contributions the affected question needs. These can include representative practice and its first response, feedback or coaching, supervision, community participation, current sources, professional or provider services, tools or AI, human checking, accessibility, fallback and protected time.

For each needed contribution, state what it supplies, to whom, at what time and load, under which conditions and what happens if it is absent. If a community is part of the arrangement, establish the relevant practice, access, suitable coordination and development use. Membership and message volume can show activity. A claim about learning or operation of the provider’s service needs evidence of the corresponding work.

Choose a safe way to practise the affected contribution that preserves the condition the person must notice. Include justified action or refusal, critical errors, source and configuration use or a specialist referral where the later work requires them.

##### HCD.15:4.4.1 - Make an ordinary work episode a repeatable learning opportunity

Use ordinary work where it provides suitable practice and timely help. Select a recurring contribution with a meaningful result, such as reconciling a discrepancy, preparing a design rationale or obtaining a usable response. Use a simulator where the work conditions call for one.

**Choose a real next occasion.** Recover its recipient, completion conditions and permitted assistance. Give the learner an attainable part that still requires the contribution to be learned.
