A mentor can retain release of the result while the learner prepares and revises it. If the receiving consequence cannot wait for learning, let the qualified contributor complete that part and arrange another suitable occasion. Completing the job and supplying the learning opportunity are different results.

**Put help where it can be used.** A demonstration can expose an unfamiliar operation, a reference can remain available during work, and a qualified colleague can respond to a particular uncertainty. For time-sensitive help, establish the provider’s availability and what the learner can do if the help does not arrive. Use a safe fallback where one exists; otherwise limit or defer the dependent work. Include the support demand in the workload and assignment.

**Make feedback lead to another action.** Let the person revise the current draft before it is used, correct a reversible action, or handle the same requirement in a later suitable case. Reopening a customer's completed transaction only for practice can damage the work. In that situation, use the retained case for comparison or the next legitimate occurrence. To report corrective practice, establish what the person did with the feedback.

**Change participation with the result.** Increase the range of cases or responsibility when the person's contribution supports it; retain a useful reference or review when it belongs to the intended arrangement. A more experienced person may need only a new exception or interface. A novice may need several opportunities with a competent model. Neither tenure nor job grade supplies that diagnosis.

Arrange another occasion only when there is a worthwhile unresolved learning question. If ordinary work already supplies a suitable attempt and feedback, use it without adding a parallel learning record. If workload prevents attempts, mentors cannot respond or assignments exclude the needed cases, HCD identifies that missing condition; use the available organizational remedy or seek a change from the holder of the required authority. Where the condition stays open, narrow or defer the affected opportunity. HCD.28 can design the learning offer. When changing the organization is necessary, OCE.6, OCE.9 and OCE.11 address effective assignments and access, the combined organizational contribution, and coexistence with continuing service.

#### HCD.15:4.5 - Match evidence and reassessment to the receiving use

For planned practice, identify what would be observed and the inference it could support. For a completed episode, use the evidence of what happened. Distinguish first attempts and helped corrections, familiar and unfamiliar work, immediate and delayed performance, normal and reduced support, participation and personal contribution. A cohort report may describe the group without resolving an individual case.

Use the least burdensome evidence adequate for the requested finding and the consequences of relying on it. A qualified prior observation can settle a local question. A fresh discriminating attempt may be worthwhile when a specific condition remains open. Safety or qualification may call for representative cases, critical-error coverage, delayed or changed-support observations, qualified criteria and independent checking.

Before a new observation, state which outcomes would support retaining, adapting, narrowing, reopening or stopping the arrangement. For completed work, use the criteria that applied or identify any later criterion used for a retrospective judgement. State which explanations the observations distinguish, which remain open and what the result supports. Broader transfer, retention or a causal effect requires evidence for that claim.

#### HCD.15:4.6 - Make ownership, authority, burden, and stops executable

For each required contribution, identify who can provide it, under which conditions and, where a decision is needed, who has the authority to make it. Keep the person’s participation and consent distinct from provider allocation, specialist judgement, employment decisions, release authority, clinical governance, platform access and programme design wherever these matter.

Set the applicable limits on cost, workload, protected time, privacy, accessibility and service pressure. Identify a safe fallback where one exists. If a criterion, operating service, observation, authority or safe working condition is missing, or the burden exceeds the agreed limit, stop or narrow the dependent activity and give the reason.

When the evidence suffices and no reopening condition applies, retain the arrangement or conclude with the supported lesson.

#### HCD.15:4.7 - Return the arrangement or the exact missing result

If a successful episode yields a sufficient lesson and no continuing development question remains, return that lesson and its conditions. If a continuing arrangement is needed, specify the following positions to the extent they apply.

| Position | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| Use frame | Person, later-work family, material conditions, qualification and evidence window, requested finding or decision, and protected consequences. |
| Affected question | Changed assumption or evidence, or a bounded question obtained from successful Work; preserved claims and components, and serious unresolved alternatives. |
| Re-entry | Work- or evidence-bearing triggers and any materially justified cadence. |
| Contributions | The practice, feedback, community, source, provider, specialist, tool or AI support, accessibility, fallback or protected time the arrangement requires. |
| Evidence | First and helped attempts, representative performance, unfamiliar transfer, delay, changed support, critical errors, burden, criteria and inference limits as applicable. |
| Governance | Owners, permissions, authority, participation or consent conditions, cost and workload limits. |
| Response | Conditions for reassessing, retaining, adapting, narrowing or stopping the arrangement. For a blocked use, identify the missing contribution and any known condition for resuming. |

Distinguish the proposed arrangement, its authorization, development work performed, subsequent work performed, observations, an inference about capability and a claim about effect. If an indispensable input is unavailable, return `continuing-arrangement-blocked` for the affected use. Identify the missing contribution, any safe narrower scope and any known supplier or condition for resuming.

### HCD.15:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.15:5.1 - A constructed continuation arrangement for Engineer-E27

Engineer-E27, `CapabilityDevelopmentTeam-E27`, `ReleaseWork-R9` and the observations in this example are constructed. For operational reliance, use the applicable engineering, safety, release, employment or specialist findings and decisions.

The intended later-Work family is independent review of AI-assisted mixed physical/software release claims. The work may require configuration-impact reasoning, challenge of plausible wrong AI output, auditable evidence return, justified action or refusal, and bounded safety and maintenance specialist use. The constructed 2026-Q4 window preserves the current configuration, permitted AI conditions, current sources, critical-error criteria, and specialist-return boundary.

The example stipulates one compatible HCD.14 input: familiar review practice remains supported, while weak independent counter-hypothesis generation in unfamiliar AI-error cases calls for replacing one cue-led correction exercise with action/refusal contrasts and one fresh uncued counter-hypothesis case. This is a proposal. To report its authorization, use or effect, establish the corresponding decision, work or evidence connecting an outcome to that change.

The continuing arrangement is:

| Position | Constructed arrangement |
| --- | --- |
| Preserved | Familiar trace-to-source practice, configuration checking, evidence return, permitted tool access, and required specialist returns remain available under their existing conditions. |
| Triggers | Reopen independent challenge after a material release-Method or configuration change, a changed AI model or assistance rule, a newly observed critical error, failed unfamiliar transfer or delayed performance, changed specialist access, a source contradiction, or expiry of the bounded qualification window. A quarter boundary alone does not reopen it. |
| Practice contribution | On a trigger, use one fresh representative case containing a plausible AI claim and a material configuration variation. Obtain E27's first trace, counter-hypothesis, action or refusal, and specialist return before coaching or AI prompts name the decisive alternative. |
| Feedback and support | Provide criterion-bearing feedback, one contrasting case, current source access, the permitted AI configuration, coaching, and bounded safety or maintenance specialist access. Record help that supplies recognition separately from E27's contribution. |
| Community contribution | A provider review forum may compare anonymized reasoning traces only if facilitation, access, confidentiality, the exact practice question, and a responsible feedback owner are present. Attendance does not count as evidence of E27's capability. |
| Evidence and reassessment | Keep first and corrected attempts, critical errors, source/configuration use, unfamiliar variation, support, burden, and unresolved rivals separate. One successful fresh case can retain the local arrangement provisionally; it cannot establish broad transfer, retention, or causal effect. |
| Burden and authority | No protected learner and provider time has been allocated for the case and feedback. Return `continuing-arrangement-blocked` for that practice contribution and identify the shortfall to the allocation holder. Resume when the allocation covers preparation, the attempt, feedback and comparison. Any follow-up needs its own authorized time, assessor, task and access. Release, safety, employment and provider-operation decisions remain with their respective holders. |
| Stops and returns | If a required engineering criterion, configuration, specialist route, safe case, provider service or authority is missing, hold the affected use. Identify the missing contribution and the decision or claim it limits. Stop the added practice if burden or a protected contribution worsens. |

The following outcomes are hypothetical.

| Later observation | Arrangement response |
| --- | --- |
| E27 independently generates and tests a relevant counter-hypothesis on the fresh case while preserving trace and specialist return | Retain this local response provisionally for the tested configuration; do not claim general capability or causal effect. |
| Correct challenge appears only after a coach or AI prompt names the alternative | Report what E27 did after the cue. If the receiving question requires independent challenge, assess that contribution on appropriate evidence or revise the cue arrangement. |
| The AI configuration or source changes before the attempt | Check whether the change affects the task or its evidence window. Retain the earlier qualification if it still applies. |
| Specialist access is absent for a case that requires it | Identify the missing access or service and seek it from the responsible provider when needed. Preserve conclusions about the person that still have their grounds. |
| Traceability or another protected contribution deteriorates | Stop or revise the local change; the intended gain does not compensate for the protected loss. |

#### HCD.15:5.2 - A professional credit rule is not yet an arrangement

An annual credit requirement can establish a qualification or re-entry condition. To design continuing development, also establish the affected person and work, the relevant practice or service, evidence, burden and what should happen if the arrangement fails. A credit record can answer a credit question directly.

#### HCD.15:5.3 - Continue when time and support are available

Consider a separate constructed variant of E27. The programme owner has authorized a thirty-minute simulation and eighteen practitioner minutes, including preparation and the result record. A qualified practitioner has a compatible case-practice Method and a checked pack of short cases whose reading and feedback fit those windows. The Method calls for a first explanation, feedback, correction, a contrast and a fresh attempt. Current sources, accessibility arrangements and the permitted AI configuration are available. These allocations belong to this variant. Section 5.1 has no such allocation.

The domain owner supplies the simulated criterion: a review claim needs a report for the proposed configuration and all required checks; an out-of-scope safety question returns to the specialist. E27 is to challenge the AI claim in simulation. An operational release would require separate authority. The constructed episode unfolds as follows:

| Time and contribution | Attempt, help and result |
| --- | --- |
| Five practitioner minutes before the episode | Prepare the already qualified short pack, confirm source/tool access and preserve the fresh case from rehearsal. |
| Learner minutes 0–6; no practitioner contact | E27 traces the AI claim to its report but initially accepts a claim for FW8 backed by an FW7 report. Trace-to-source succeeds; the configuration challenge is missed. |
| Minutes 6–10; four practitioner minutes | The practitioner points to the mismatch and explains the criterion. This supplies the missed recognition and is recorded as help. |
| Minutes 10–14; no practitioner contact | E27 corrects the claim and explains why the report cannot support FW8. This is a correction after help. |
| Minutes 14–18; four practitioner minutes | A contrasting report does cover the requested configuration and checks. E27 explains why a positive review conclusion is now warranted; feedback checks the reason, rather than teaching blanket refusal. |
| Minutes 18–25; no practitioner contact | On unrehearsed material for FW9, E27 proposes a possible configuration mismatch, checks the report and the required checks, rules the mismatch out and supports the AI claim within the stated scope. No new coach or AI cue supplies that alternative. |
| Minutes 25–30; five practitioner minutes | The practitioner compares the separate attempts and help, checks preserved traceability and the specialist boundary, and records the next decision with E27. |

The episode uses thirty learner minutes and eighteen practitioner minutes, including five minutes of preparation. If preparation or checking exceeds the allocation, report the resulting capacity gap as in §5.1.

The first decision is to retain the local arrangement provisionally. The fresh response supports E27’s observed challenge under the stated source and AI conditions. The earlier correction followed help, and the contrast included feedback. Neither establishes independent challenge in those attempts. Keep the initial miss in the history. If another development opportunity is justified, use the record to select a different relevant AI-error case and establish that its time and support are allocated.

Later, suppose an AI update stops exposing the report identifiers needed for source tracing. Without the identifiers, this assessment cannot rely on the new output. Give the platform owner the specific need for source access. The earlier permitted configuration remains available and authorized in this variant, so compatible practice can continue there. Preserve the recorded human results and specialist returns. Resume the new configuration when usable report access is supplied and checked; add a learning episode only if a human contribution remains unresolved. Repeating the original course would not restore those identifiers.

#### HCD.15:5.4 - Keep a Useful Import Procedure without Inventing Its Cause

In this constructed case, a specialist examines their contribution to a successful import of forty reference records. The domain owner supplies the criterion for this case: each accepted identifier and mapping must match the authoritative source, and any unresolved exception prevents acceptance. The approved V1 procedure includes automated validation, resolution of its exceptions and two manual passes. The specialist knows how to use those records and can explain their own actions; a qualified colleague is available for the bounded comparison.

The final forty records satisfied the criterion. The specialist says, “The two manual passes made it work, so I can rely on them next time.” The available record supports a more limited account:

| Available evidence | What it permits the participants to say |
| --- | --- |
| The incoming file and validation log show two exceptions before either manual pass. | Automation exposed these two problems before the manual checks. |
| The specialist corrected one identifier; the colleague supplied the mapping used for the other correction. | The specialist performed the corrections with the stated help. Independent recovery of the mapping was not observed. |
| Two subsequent manual passes recorded no further change; comparison of the accepted output with the authoritative source met the criterion. | The complete sequence succeeded in this episode. The record does not isolate the necessity or sufficiency of either manual pass. |

The specialist wants to know what to retain for the next import. The order in the log and the colleague’s recorded mapping show that automated detection and help contributed to the corrections. The record leaves the value of the manual passes open. If those records are unavailable, seek the relevant log, mapping basis or other discriminating evidence only when it could improve the answer enough to justify the effort. Otherwise state the unresolved causal question.

The specialist's lesson becomes: “For V1, retain the approved sequence and reconcile exceptions with the source before acceptance. I used mapping help in this episode. The final success does not show that two manual passes can replace validation or that I can recover every mapping alone.” The action is retained, while its explanation and condition of reuse become narrower. Removing the manual passes requires a decision under the authority governing the V1 procedure.

Here the person must use that distinction in a forthcoming import, so a short application is worthwhile. The colleague supplies a permitted ten-record V1 practice copy, an authoritative mapping and a validation log. One duplicate identifier and one unfamiliar code expose the same two kinds of return. The specialist must locate the exceptions, correct from the supplied basis or request the missing mapping, and explain why the unresolved item prevents acceptance. The colleague compares that response with the criterion. HCD.9 supplies correction if a step fails; if the response is already supported, it supplies reasoned retention. This is an application with declared resources, not evidence of unaided mapping knowledge.

The owner has allocated thirty-two learner minutes and twenty colleague minutes for this review and application. The records and small practice copy already exist. The planned added burden is:

| Contribution | Learner minutes | Colleague minutes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prepare the permitted records, criterion and short practice copy | 0 | 4 |
| Reconstruct the episode and write the initial explanation | 6 | 0 |
| Compare the explanation, sequence and alternative together | 8 | 8 |
| State the bounded lesson and choose the next application together | 4 | 4 |
| Make the ten-record first application with declared sources | 8 | 0 |
| Check the response, use feedback and record the next decision together | 4 | 4 |
| **Total** | **30** | **20** |

The unused two learner minutes cannot replace colleague attention. This budget does not guarantee completion after an error: correction requires a targeted retry, and a requirement that cannot be corrected and retried within the remaining learner and colleague time stays unresolved. Arrange another episode if the remaining question warrants it and the required time and support are available. The completed import adds no new practice time to this budget. Its observed help remains part of the evidence. If locating the records or preparing the practice copy takes longer than the supplied allowance, revise the arrangement before promising the application.

Now change the receiving conditions before that application: the next import uses V2, no compatible automated check is available, and the colleague has not confirmed further time. Eighteen learner minutes and sixteen colleague minutes have already been spent on preparation, reconstruction, comparison and the lesson. Repeating the V1 exercise cannot answer whether manual checking is sufficient for V2. The specialist can use four of the remaining fourteen learner minutes to state the changed conditions and send the domain owner the missing validation and mapping question. Stop the dependent application; cumulative added use is twenty-two learner minutes and sixteen colleague minutes. The V2 validation service is still missing. There is no observation of a further feedback session.

If a V2-compatible procedure and support are later supplied, compare the cases through HCD.25 and select only the remaining learning contribution. If the specialist can already explain and perform it under the required conditions, return to Work without another exercise. If the original V1 conditions remain and the bounded question was already answered by the recorded episode and explanation, the application could likewise be omitted. Neither stopping decision turns the historical success into proof of a new configuration or of the review's effect.

### HCD.15:6 - Bias-Annotation

A new tool, source or incident can make retraining seem necessary even when the existing qualification still holds. Identify any claim about this person that the change affects. Familiar credits or regular assessments can also make repetition seem sufficient. Establish what the interval or opportunity contributes to the requested finding or decision.

Community and provider visibility create another bias: participation is easy to count, while independent transfer and critical errors are harder to observe. Keep activity useful as an arrangement contribution without upgrading it to capability evidence.

### HCD.15:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The person, later-work family, material conditions, evidence window and intended finding or decision are identifiable.
- The development question and preserved claims have compatible evidence. An account of a successful episode identifies the relevant conditions, help used and any plausible competing explanation.
- When a continuing arrangement is needed, it has work- or evidence-bearing triggers. Any selected cadence has a material justification.
- Practice, feedback, community, source, provider, specialist, support, tool, access, fallback, and protected-time contributions are named only when needed and have owners.
- First, helped, unfamiliar, delayed, changed-support, critical-error, burden, and participation observations stay distinct at the strength the receiving use needs.
- Proposal, authorization, performed development Work, later Work, observation, capability, and causal effect remain separate.
- Limits on burden, cost, workload, privacy, accessibility, safety and authority are usable for the intended arrangement. Relevant reopening, stopping and resumption conditions are stated.
- The lesson, continuing arrangement or identified gap answers the receiving question at the scope the evidence supports.

### HCD.15:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Better move |
| --- | --- |
| “Renew twelve credits every year.” | Tie re-entry to a material qualification, Work, evidence, source, support, or risk condition and name the finding or action that condition would reopen. |
| “The person attended, so capability is current.” | Treat participation as one contribution and obtain evidence for the relied-on human contribution. |
| “Repeat the whole programme after every change.” | Recover the smallest affected question and preserve supported claims and arrangement components. |
| “The community will keep everyone current.” | Name facilitation, access, practice, feedback, provider, and evidence contributions; membership proves none of them by itself. |
| “The plan means continuing development is happening.” | Separate the designed and authorized arrangement from performed development Work and observed result. |
| “More frequent assessment is always safer.” | Choose evidence adequate for the intended reliance. Stop further assessment when its attainable contribution no longer warrants the burden or it exceeds an applicable protection. |
| “It succeeded, so repeat everything I did.” | Recover the consequential action, help used and relevant conditions. State the lesson within what those observations establish. |
| “A lesson must change the procedure.” | Preserve a supported action when the grounds warrant it; changing its explanation or stopping unnecessary development can be sufficient. |

### HCD.15:9 - Consequences

The practitioner can retain supported contributions and reopen the affected question when work or evidence changes. A continuing arrangement identifies what the person is expected to do, who can provide its needed support and what would justify stopping. A bounded lesson can itself be sufficient.

Maintaining a continuing arrangement costs time and access. A missing provider, source, authority, safe task or observation can limit one use. Where the contribution is needed, identify a qualified source or the remaining gap. Continued reliance may require further evidence of transfer, retention or performance under changed support.

### HCD.15:10 - Rationale

Continuing development relates a material change or worthwhile unresolved question about this person’s work to the contributions and evidence it requires beyond one episode. A well-supported lesson from the current episode can stand on its own.

Reopening the smallest affected question preserves other supported results and limits the burden. What the person did, the conditions of performance and its effect each require evidence appropriate to the claim.

### HCD.15:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**Working question:** how should continuing workplace development respond to changed conditions and useful questions from successful Work without equating recurring instruction or participation with capability?

**Selected line — adopt and adapt.** Kraiger and Ford's [science of workplace instruction review](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109) is the best-known-line candidate for the evidence spine used here: instructional events, learner activity, learning outcomes, transfer, and job performance remain different, while learner, design, work environment, opportunity, and support condition the result. HCD.15 adapts that line in §§4.1–4.7 by connecting one changed later-Work or evidence condition to a holder-specific continuing arrangement, explicit re-entry, owners, burden, and reassessment. The review does not supply one cadence, intervention, or E27 trajectory.

The serious default is annual-credit, repeat-course, or membership-based continuation. It is cheaper to administer, but it cannot show which development claim changed, whether the relevant contribution was elicited, or whether it survived unfamiliar, delayed, or changed-support conditions. HCD.15 rejects activity count as the capability inference while retaining a credit rule, course, or community as a bounded contribution or external condition when it genuinely changes access or qualification.

Matsuo and Tsukube's [cognitive-apprenticeship review](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijme.2020.100417), Wiese, Kilty, and Bennett's [realist synthesis of supervised workplace learning](https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.13655), Abedini, Abedin, and Zowghi's [review of adult online communities of practice](https://doi.org/10.1111/bjet.13120), and Brooks and colleagues' [community-support study](https://doi.org/10.1002/lrh2.10412) support bounded modeling, coaching, supervision, access, facilitation, platform, and coordination questions. They are contribution and boundary sources, not evidence for a universal provider form, transplanted clinical governance, community effect, or this holder's capability. This comparison changes §§4.4–4.6 and the participation checks in §§5 and 7.

For learning from success, §4.2.1 **adapts** Matsuo's [*Supporting experiential learning for expanding successes*](https://doi.org/10.1080/13678868.2024.2401301) (online 2024, issue 2025). Its qualitative study of 203 managers in one Japanese manufacturer suggests ways to recognise, analyse, share and apply successful experiences. It does not test their effectiveness or establish a mandatory sequence. Ellis and Davidi's [after-event review study](https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.90.5.857) (2005) supplies a historical working comparison: the person's explanation is confronted with data and feedback, and a sound action can be retained. Its military navigation setting and comparison conditions do not establish a general workplace effect.

HCD.15 constructs the bounded connection in §4.2.1 and §5.4: qualify an explanation of the episode, select the next question, reuse HCD.23–HCD.25 where their contributions are needed, and stop when development adds no useful answer. The serious alternative is to repeat the successful procedure unchanged because the outcome was favourable. That is sufficient when the relevant basis and conditions are already known; otherwise it carries an unsupported explanation into the next use. The selected comparison costs evidence retrieval and qualified attention, but can preserve the useful action while exposing a condition that defeats reuse. These comparisons show how the available evidence can change an explanation or its use. Attributing a change in the learner to this review requires evidence that distinguishes its effect from other influences. Reopen the choice if stronger evidence, a changed work context or a lighter comparison changes those gains or costs.

Compared with counting attendance alone, this line makes the affected claim, proposed local change, protected conditions and needed returns explicit; it requires more case-specific work. Reopen the comparison if stronger current workplace-development evidence supplies an equally truthful lower-burden arrangement, or if a changed population, Work family, provider form, support condition, measure, horizon, or serious alternative defeats one of the relied-on contribution claims.

[Eraut (2004)](https://doi.org/10.1080/158037042000225245) is a historical field-based source for the connection among task allocation, attainable challenge, support and confidence. [Ford, Baldwin and Prasad (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-032117-104443) develop the transfer question beyond the course itself. Compared with simply assigning more work, the arrangement specifies a contribution the person can learn, the help it requires and an occasion for using feedback. Establish that these are available before relying on them.

[De Grip and Sauermann's field experiment](https://docs.iza.org/dp5976.pdf) is a historical existence case: a package for experienced call-centre agents combined instruction and discussion with supervised real calls. Its design supports a bounded effect of that package; it does not identify the effect of each component or prescribe the clerk arrangement in Application:10.3. A corporate university is compared here through the contributions it can supply, not assigned a general success or failure rate.

### HCD.15:12 - Relations

**HCD.14** can supply a revision hypothesis and supporting evidence where the person, later work, conditions and interval fit. Equivalent qualified evidence permits direct entry. If continuing development is needed, establish the relevant triggers, contributions, access, provider conditions, burden, authority, reassessment and stops.

HCD.1–HCD.13 may supply the holder, later-Work demand, target, programme, Method, task, support, practice, performance, transfer, retention, and evidence values they each govern. Use their relevant results directly. If a necessary result is unavailable, qualify the dependent conclusion or obtain it from the relevant practice when warranted. E.23.CDI supplies the cross-holder development spine under its own entry conditions; HCD.15 supplies the human-specific continuing arrangement.

HCD.23–HCD.25 can use a qualified episode and bounded lesson for explanation, evaluation or comparison across projects. For a selected practice episode, HCD.9 helps the person use feedback for correction or reasoned retention, or identify what remains unresolved. Each continuation needs the task and support appropriate to it. A sufficient conclusion about the original work can finish the inquiry.

Observed use of an HCD.15 arrangement may later supply HCD.16 with qualified human-development evidence. The designed arrangement, attendance, community membership, or provider report is not by itself evidence of Method fit, transfer, retention, or worth. HCD.16 remains independently enterable from another exact evidence change.

**HCD.2** addresses whole-programme comparison, **OPS** current operations, and **OCE** organizational change and culture. Strategy, advice, Administration, Learning Product, clinical, employment, safety, legal, provider, platform and target-domain practices retain their respective decisions, Methods, services, access and criteria. Use an established result or obtain the particular contribution or decision the development question still needs.

### HCD.15:End

## HCD.16 — Keep Human Capability-Development Method Claims Current

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.16:1 - Problem Frame

**Use this when** you need to assess a claim about using a particular human capability-development Method or candidate in a specified repertoire. A change in the learner population, later work, provider, tool, AI, source, transfer or retention result, safety condition or available alternative may reopen the question.

Identify the Method or candidate, its status, the human-development claim and the use in question. Return the strongest supported use and its limits. The evidence may support retaining a practice, narrowing a claim, leaving a comparison open or stopping a use at a protection limit. When a change or inquiry is warranted, give its disposition: adopt, revise, branch or retire the use, or select an obtainable, worthwhile further inquiry.

Preserve the Method’s identity and status, the provider and learner conditions, the scope of the evidence and the relevant domain authority when reconsidering its use.

Use Method Engineering for general questions about Method identity, construction or maintenance (§4.2). A bibliography update, publication rebuild, local choice or declaration of an already grounded set can proceed directly when it needs no assessment of a human-development claim.

### HCD.16:2 - Problem

Human-development Methods are often named at the wrong grain. “Coaching,” “deliberate practice,” “apprenticeship,” “retrieval,” or “AI tutoring” can hide different operations, learner conditions, supports, providers, tasks, and evidence claims. A new source, tool version, or local success is then used either to replace the whole repertoire or to preserve it unchanged.

A source may contradict one mechanism, one population claim or one inference from assisted practice. A failed attempt may concern the provider, access, assessment or domain criterion. A favourable average may conceal a critical error, failed transfer, limited retention or dependence on support. Establish which part of the claim the evidence addresses.

Use this Method to assess the evidence for the specified human-development claim. Retain its supported scope and revise the particular use where the evidence warrants it. For generic Method identity or repertoire maintenance, use the relevant Method Engineering result.

### HCD.16:3 - Forces

| Force | Working tension |
| --- | --- |
| Currentness and stability | Respond to material evidence without treating every new publication or tool version as a new Method. |
| Method identity and HCD use | Preserve generic Method semantics and status while deciding whether a human-development use remains warranted. |
| Local evidence and transfer | Use direct observations where they fit without generalizing across learners, Work families, providers, supports, or horizons. |
| Improvement and critical error | Reward useful performance while preventing aggregate gains from hiding unacceptable errors or protected losses. |
| Assistance and human contribution | Use tools, AI, coaching and scaffolding where appropriate while separating equipped performance from later unassisted or changed-support performance. |
| Decision and uncertainty | State the strongest supported use or a qualified unresolved comparison; select a new probe only for an obtainable contribution worth its full burden. |
| Repertoire and selection | State what the evidence supports for this field and use. Local selection, admission and a decision about all uses each require grounds at their own scope. |

### HCD.16:4 - Solution

#### HCD.16:4.1 - Fix the repertoire use and exact claim

Identify the practitioner or receiver, the repertoire use, target human capability, later-work family, population, material conditions, the relevant evidence or qualification window and consequences to protect. Identify the decision holder and their authority when a decision is requested. For a historical finding, use the conditions of the period under examination and any authority relevant to that finding.

Identify the Method or candidate and the claim to examine. State the action, relevant population, task or work, practice and feedback, provider or support, measure, horizon and inference to the extent they affect it. A claim that a Method works needs this scope before it can support reliance.

If the repertoire use, subject, status or claim is unclear, identify the missing fact and what would establish it. Use an applicable record, source or observation. If the fact cannot be recovered, state which conclusion remains open. A school name, prompt, citation or activity label may help locate the evidence.

#### HCD.16:4.2 - Recover Method and candidate status from Method Engineering

Identify the reusable action and whether the item is an admitted Method or a candidate. Where construction, admission, description, lineage, provenance, trial, fit, worth, introduction or currentness matters to the claim, use the applicable Method Engineering result. Seek a missing specialist decision or contribution if required. A candidate keeps its status until a separate admission establishes otherwise.

A change in a file, source, prompt, support, tool, provider or execution may leave the reusable Method unchanged. When the evidence suggests a change in a reusable operation, dependency or condition for entering or stopping, identify that feature and use **A.3.1.MV** to determine whether it is a variant. For a change in description, support, introduction or performed work, use the pertinent result or seek the missing contribution from its responsible holder.

Use the established identity and status to interpret human-development evidence. Local repertoire judgements retain their stated scope.

#### HCD.16:4.3 - Bind human-development evidence to the correct conditions

Recover the evidence needed for the particular claim. Identify the intended action and the starting conditions relevant to the inference. For a claim about later work, establish how the available tasks or observations represent it. Where they affect the inference, account for practice, feedback, timing, transfer or retention, how performance was assessed, the provider’s capability, tools and assistance permitted and used, critical errors, burden and protections. Use the level of assurance the intended reliance requires.

Keep these evidence states separate:

- assisted practice performance;
- unassisted performance after practice;
- performance under changed or withdrawn support;
- same-job performance after prior assisted exposure;
- unfamiliar same-family transfer;
- transfer to other Work;
- delayed retention under stated intervening practice; and
- provider, cohort, service, organization, or product outcomes.

Use evidence at the scope of the observed performance. A corrected learner response, a provider’s demonstrated service or productivity with a deployed tool can each support its own claim. If the receiving question requires a conclusion about change in the learner or performance under other conditions, identify and use the additional evidence it needs.

#### HCD.16:4.4 - Compare the current claim with serious alternatives

Identify what the new evidence confirms, contradicts or leaves open. Compare the claim with a credible competing explanation or alternative where that distinction matters. If a decision is due, assess the consequences of retaining, narrowing, separating or withdrawing the use within its stated scope.

If the evidence exposes a problem, locate it in the claim, the assessment or the conditions in which the learner or provider did the work.

| Candidate locus | Decision-changing question |
| --- | --- |
| Source and claim | Which population, task, measure, horizon, support or provider did the source cover? Does its evidence support the claimed transfer or causal relation? |
| Method-use condition | Does the already admitted Method still fit this learner, later Work, provider, support, risk, and evidence need? |
| Population or condition branch | Does evidence defeat only one subgroup, configuration, support posture, or qualification window? |
| Assessment | Did the task, scoring, cue, tool, or missing criterion fail to expose the intended contribution? |
| Provider or access | Was the Method available under the required conditions? Did a qualified provider perform it? If those conditions failed, what does the observation establish about the Method? |
| Reusable Method semantics | Did an operation, dependency, entry, stop, or other reusable claim change, requiring an A.3.1.MV return? |

Reopen the claims that depend on the changed evidence. A later publication date, new name, interface or carrier warrants reconsideration where it changes a condition of use.

#### HCD.16:4.5 - Settle the current result before selecting further inquiry

State what the available evidence supports and any comparison still unresolved. Retain supported uses, narrow the claim or stop a use whose protection condition is unmet. Consider a new observation for a remaining question whose answer matters.

Select a further probe when an observation is obtainable within the relevant window and its attainable contribution to the finding or its use warrants the full burden. Include design, preparation, attempts, feedback, comparison, learner and provider time, delay, specialist access and displaced work or protection. Establish that the required resources and authority are available. Use **C.11.DUA** if the evidence demand needs appraisal.

For a selected probe, specify what or whose work would be observed, which help, sources, tools or provider contributions it requires, and which observations would affect the finding. Include a first response, changed case, delay, support comparison or critical-error observation where the claim depends on it. Establish the resources, protections and stopping conditions. Keep domain criteria and safety decisions with their responsible holders. An unavailable or unwarranted probe leaves the current supported conclusion and any dependent uncertainty.

Use the Core Method-development family or direct responsible practice for a generic trial, admission, variant or organizational rollout. The choice or design of an HCD inquiry can establish a planned comparison. An observed result comes from its performance.

#### HCD.16:4.6 - Return the supported slice and any selected change

State the supported use and its limits, any comparison that remains open or the condition that prevents use. For a warranted change or inquiry, identify the applicable disposition and distinguish a recommendation from a decision the holder has authority to make.

| Disposition | Meaning here | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adopt` | Include an admitted Method in the specified HCD repertoire under its supported conditions. | Admission, selection for one person, authorization of work and evidence of effect have their own grounds. |
| `revise` | Change the exact HCD claim, evidence condition, population scope, support condition, or use statement while preserving Method status. | A semantic Method change returns to A.3.1.MV; a text edit alone is not the result. |
| `branch` | Keep separate use conditions or populations when different evidence supports different dispositions. | Keep the Method or candidate status that has been established. A change of Method semantics needs its own variant judgement. |
| `retire` | Stop offering the Method or claim for the stated use. | Preserve its history and other supported uses. |
| `further probe` | Select an obtainable and worthwhile observation for the receiving question. | Establish burden, access, protections, stopping rule and how the possible results would affect the finding or decision. Report what the probe established after it is performed. An unavailable observation limits its dependent claim. |

Keep the grounds, material alternatives, uncertainty and conditions of change with the finding. A comparison can remain open while the evidence supports a particular use. Describe a further probe if one has been selected. Keep separate claims and their warranted outcomes even when they draw on the same observations.

#### HCD.16:4.7 - Return the current repertoire slice and route stronger results

Retain the positions needed by the current repertoire slice and its receiving use:

| Position | Content for the receiving use |
| --- | --- |
| Use and authority | Practitioner or receiver, bounded repertoire use, population, later work, relevant evidence or qualification window and protected consequences. Identify the decision holder, mandate and any stopping constraint where relevant. |
| Subjects and status | Exact admitted Methods and separately status-preserved candidates; current reusable semantics, descriptions and lineage supplied by ME. |
| Human-development claims | Target contribution, learner starting state, practice and feedback, representative Work, transfer, retention, provider, support, safety, tool and AI conditions. |
| Evidence and currentness | Direct observations and sources with population, task, comparator, measure, horizon, support, provider, causal, and currentness limits. |
| Alternatives and result | Supported use and limits, material alternatives, any unresolved comparison or protection stop. Identify the scope and safeguards for any selected `adopt`, `revise`, `branch`, `retire` or `further probe`. |
| Gaps and reopening | Identify what is missing, the affected use and conditions for reconsideration. Name a needed contribution and its holder where known. For retirement, give its scope. For a selected probe, give its burden, access, stopping rule and response. |


When several exact already grounded members must be declared for one selector-facing use, pass the members and basis to G.5. When a shipped maintained set, source pack, publication, or other named currentness object needs targeted refresh, use G.11. HCD.16 does not recreate either result for an ordinary claim-sized decision.

### HCD.16:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### HCD.16:5.1 - A constructed E27 repertoire decision

The E27 repertoire, its stipulated Method and candidate statuses, and the observations in this case are constructed.

For the bounded 2026-Q4 development use, stipulate one admitted `Trace-and-Specialist-Return Method-E27` for developing source/configuration tracing and appropriate specialist return. Its learner attempts a representative review task, traces the claims to the supplied sources/configuration and returns a question to a qualified specialist when the case crosses the stated boundary. A provider gives criterion-bearing feedback; the learner corrects or justifies the response and retries the affected contribution on a changed case. These practice and feedback operations constitute the stipulated development Method; the review operation is the target being practised. Preserve it as admitted only inside the example. Also stipulate two status-preserved candidate accounts: `Cue-Led-Correction Candidate-E27` and `Counter-Hypothesis-First Candidate-E27`. Their names and derivation do not admit Methods or establish variants.

The current evidence question comes from unfamiliar AI-error cases. Assisted correction was accurate after a cue, but no current observation establishes that E27 independently generates and tests a counter-hypothesis before accepting plausible wrong AI output. Trace and specialist-return contributions remain supported in the stipulated earlier cases. The unresolved question concerns independent challenge with unfamiliar AI errors.

For the present repertoire decision, stipulate that a valid comparison would require three learner-hours and two provider-hours in total, including design, task preparation, attempts, feedback and comparison. Only half an hour of provider time remains before the decision; extending it would displace already committed development Work. Retain the supported tracing and helped-practice uses and leave the independent-challenge comparison open for this window.

The current repertoire slice is:

| Exact subject or claim | Constructed disposition | Boundary and next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Trace-and-Specialist-Return Method-E27` for guided trace-and-return practice | `adopt` for this development use under the stipulated conditions. | The admission and relevant claims already have their stipulated grounds. Operational use in ReleaseWork-R9 needs separate evidence. |
| “Accurate assisted practice demonstrates independent learning” | `retire` for this use. | Assisted correction remains useful practice evidence, but it cannot support the independent-challenge claim. |
| `Cue-Led-Correction Candidate-E27` | `branch` as a candidate account for helped correction episodes only. | Keep candidate status; do not use its helped result as evidence for independent unfamiliar performance. |
| `Counter-Hypothesis-First Candidate-E27` | Comparison unresolved; preserve the candidate account without selecting a new probe. | No independent-challenge, superiority, Method-admission, fit or worth claim follows. The narrower supported repertoire slice is complete for this window. |

Now consider a later decision about offering the independent-challenge use. The three learner-hours and two provider-hours, current criteria, specialist access, participation and authorization are available within the protected window. Distinguishing candidate-supported independent challenge from helped correction can change that offer enough to justify the full burden. Select `further probe` for this changed condition; the earlier limited result did not require it.

The selected probe uses two matched unfamiliar release-review cases with current stipulated criteria. In each, capture the first trace, configuration hypothesis, challenge, action or refusal, critical error, and specialist return before help. One case then permits the ordinary cue-led correction; the other permits the candidate counter-hypothesis prompt only after the first attempt. A later fresh case under normal permitted support and, only if the decision needs it, a separately resourced delayed or perturbed-support observation can distinguish local independent contribution from helped correction. Stop on missing criteria, unsafe use, absent specialist access, unacceptable burden, or damage to traceability.

Suppose both initial attempts need help, E27 corrects each, and on the fresh case E27 generates and tests the relevant counter-hypothesis before a coach or AI cue supplies it, while preserving traceability and the specialist return. The result now supports that observed contribution under the fresh-case conditions after both practice episodes. It does not identify which practice produced it or rank the two candidates: order, carryover between episodes and case differences remain possible explanations. Keep both candidate statuses and the earlier helped results.

The observation question can finish with that result. If choosing between the practices depends on a comparative effect, use a suitable existing comparison or seek a qualified comparison design through **A.3.1.WT**. Before selecting a new trial, assess design, participant and provider time, access and displaced work. The present allocation covers the stated probe. Leave the ranking open if a further comparison is unavailable or not worth its burden.

Possible results remain bounded:


| Observation | Repertoire response |
| --- | --- |
| Independent challenge appears in fresh unfamiliar cases after both practice episodes while tracing and specialist return are preserved | Report that performance under its observed conditions and preserve the two candidate statuses. Ranking their effects needs evidence that distinguishes them. Adopt only an admitted Method for a supported use. Branch when evidence supports different dispositions for different conditions. |
| Correct challenge appears only after the counter-hypothesis prompt | Identify the learner’s contribution after the prompt and the resulting scope for helped practice. For a claim about independent challenge, use an observation in which the learner supplied the decisive challenge before anyone supplied it to them in that attempt. Seek another observation only where warranted. |
| Traceability or specialist return worsens | Reject or revise the candidate use regardless of aggregate accuracy. |
| The task, source, configuration or critical-error criterion is defective | Identify the affected inference. Use an adequate existing observation or repair the missing condition if a further observation is needed. Evidence from a defective assessment cannot by itself justify retiring the Method. |

#### HCD.16:5.2 - Unlike evidence states do not select an engineering Method

Studies of AI-assisted customer service, consulting and school mathematics examine different results. Customer service can provide evidence of productivity with equipment and a bounded same-job outage signal. In the consulting experiment, assistance helped on tasks inside the tested frontier and could impair performance outside it. Mathematics studies can distinguish assisted practice from later unassisted performance. Use each result within its population, work, tools, measures, horizon and provider conditions. A claim about E27’s independent learning, transfer or comparative advantage needs compatible evidence. Until then, retain the supported use or return the open comparison.

#### HCD.16:5.3 - A source contradiction can reopen one claim without opening treatment

An emerging human counterconditioning review can reopen one source-to-claim row about an extinction-learning mechanism. A publication-bias critique can reopen a pooled claim about choice-architecture effects. HCD.16 may return `revise`, `retire`, or `further probe` for an exact HCD use, but it prescribes neither clinical treatment nor public-policy nudging. Use the competent domain judgement and applicable authority for an intervention decision, and subject evidence for a claim about its outcome.

### HCD.16:6 - Bias-Annotation

Novelty and prestige can make a new source, tool, model, or school seem repertoire-changing before the affected claim is named. Familiarity creates the opposite bias: a long-used Method is protected from contrary transfer, retention, provider, or critical-error evidence.

A well-documented candidate, a successful local deviation or a revised description may still lack Method admission. Use the applicable status and reusable semantics for the item under review. Keep a favourable HCD conclusion within the local use it establishes.

### HCD.16:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The account identifies the bounded repertoire use, population, later work, relevant evidence or qualification window and protected consequences. Any decision identifies its holder and authority.
- The account identifies the admitted Method or the candidate with its status, and the particular human-development claim under examination.
- The identity, status and semantics have the grounds the intended use requires. Use the relevant Core Method-development result for a claim that depends on it.
- Assisted, unassisted, changed-support, same-job, unfamiliar-transfer, other-Work, delayed, provider, and organization evidence states remain distinct where material.
- Source population, task, comparator, measure, horizon, support, provider, causal, and currentness limits travel with the claim.
- The account identifies any consequential contradiction or missing evidence and compares serious alternatives where they would change the finding or its use. Each claim has the outcome supported by its evidence.
- The result gives the supported use and limits, any unresolved comparison or protection stop and any change selected. A further probe has an attainable contribution worth its full burden, with adequate access and protection and usable stopping and response conditions.
- Candidate status is preserved; adoption and retirement do not change universal Method status.
- Use G.5, G.11, a Core Method-development result or the relevant professional practice where its own contribution is needed. Use an existing result or identify the outstanding input or authority.

### HCD.16:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Better move |
| --- | --- |
| “A newer paper replaces the Method.” | Name the exact source-to-claim row and reopen only the use that consumes the changed claim. |
| “The tool changed, so this is a new Method variant.” | Check whether the change suggests a different reusable operation, dependency or condition. Use A.3.1.MV to decide a possible variant. Use the applicable description, support or work result for a change confined to that item. |
| “The candidate worked locally, so adopt it.” | Report the observed local use and preserve the candidate status. For admission, fit or worth beyond that finding, use the relevant Core result or identify what is missing. |
| “Assisted scores improved, so learning occurred.” | Report performance under the assistance received. A stronger learning, transfer or retention claim requires relevant evidence. Seek new evidence when the remaining use calls for it and acquisition is feasible and worthwhile. |
| “One subgroup failed, so retire the Method everywhere.” | Branch or retire only the defeated population, condition, or use and preserve supported uses. |
| “Refresh the whole publication after every source change.” | Reopen the affected claim; use G.11 only for a maintained currentness object under its own conditions. |

### HCD.16:9 - Consequences

Practitioners can identify the warranted scope of a Method, any claim newly supported or defeated, the evidence needed for another use and the status of a candidate. A local revision can preserve the rest of the repertoire.

Checking how the evidence fits the claim takes effort. An inquiry may finish with a limited use or an open comparison. A new probe consumes the resources of the people or services required to perform it. Retiring a local use can leave other applications available.

### HCD.16:10 - Rationale

The question is whether a particular human-development claim is warranted for this population, later work, provider and support arrangement, evidence window and intended use.

Separate evidence for a use from evidence of admission or lineage. A new observation can change one supported claim while leaving other uses and the identity of the Method intact.

### HCD.16:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**Working question:** what do the evidence and alternatives support for this use of a human capability-development Method or candidate, and when should the repertoire change?

**Selected line — adopt and adapt.** Assess each affected claim with its population, task, comparator, measure, horizon, support, provider and Method status. Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond's [deployed customer-support study](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044) separates assisted productivity from a noisy same-job outage signal; Dell'Acqua and colleagues' [task-frontier experiment](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838) supplies a bounded independent-error challenge; and Bastani and colleagues' [school-mathematics trial](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122) separates assisted practice from later unassisted performance. HCD.16 adapts these unlike evidence states in §§4.3–4.6 and §5.2 rather than pooling them into one AI-learning verdict. None establishes E27's capability, a universal tutor, other-Work transfer, or long retention.

Using the newest publication, a school name, an average score or a tool release as a shortcut costs less than checking each affected use. It may conceal a critical error, a difference between supported and independent work or a change in the conditions for transfer. The additional comparison is worthwhile where those differences affect the evidence for the intended use. An unresolved claim can remain open.

Bauer and colleagues' [review of counterconditioning and reward-related extinction directions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nlm.2024.107994) and the Mertens/Maier [choice-architecture synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2107346118) and [publication-bias critique](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2200300119) serve as failure and contradiction evidence: a credible current line may be emerging, heterogeneous, or sensitive to bias without supporting a universal HCD or specialist intervention. This changes the source-row and `further probe` rules in §§4.4–4.6 and the domain return in §5.3.

A.3.1.MV supplies generic Method semantics and lineage; A.3.1.MI supplies introduction, observations and later-use returns. Use those results when the bounded HCD judgement depends on them. Reopen the comparison when stronger direct evidence changes an affected population, Work, learner state, provider, tool, support, measure, horizon, causal limit, or source role, or when an improved Method-repertoire practice returns the same status distinctions and local repair at lower decision effort.

### HCD.16:12 - Relations

Introduction and later-use support are supplied by [FPF A.3.1.MI](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#a31mi---introduce-a-method-into-practice-and-decide-what-to-keep-or-change). Its result keeps the target practice, introduction strategy and support distinct.


An observed use of an **HCD.15** arrangement or compatible direct evidence can inform this Method. Use attendance, membership or provider performance for the claim it supports. Fit, transfer, retention and worth need evidence for that further claim.

**A.3.1.MV** can supply Method semantics, candidate lineage, provenance, applicability, evidence positions, currentness and the meaning of retirement. **A.3.1.MI** can supply observations about introduction and later use. Distinguish the target practice from its introduction strategy, description, plan, performed work, capability, authority and externally obtained results. If the contradiction concerns a Method-engineering or introduction claim, identify what changed and use the corresponding Method Engineering or Implementation Support result, or seek the missing contribution. Method Engineering addresses continuing Method-engineering practice and culture.

Use compatible **HCD.1–HCD.14** results on demand, target, programme, task, support, practice, performance, transfer, retention or revision within their qualified scope.

A bounded HCD.16 disposition or candidate variation account may inform **HCD.17**. For a claim about enactment, culture, prevalence or authority to intervene, use evidence about the corresponding work, population or governing relation.

G.5 declares a selector-facing shortlist, ranked shortlist, joint-use set, handoff, abstain, or escalation only after exact members and basis exist. G.11 scopes currentness refresh for a named maintained object. Use C.11 where a local choice is being made. Clinical, safety, legal, employment, provider, organization, platform, learning-product, and target-domain owners retain their Methods, correctness, service, and authority.

### HCD.16:End

## HCD.17 — Deliberately Continue and Change Human Capability-Development Culture

> **Type:** Human Capability Development practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### HCD.17:1 - Problem Frame

**Use this when** you need to establish how a human capability-development practice was generated, transmitted, used, recognized, chosen, remembered, retained or lost in a specified population. The inquiry may also ask whether the practice should continue or what change is warranted.

Name the HCD Discipline or smaller practice, population, place and period. Identify whether the evidence concerns an admitted Method or a candidate or observed practice, and state the cultural claim to examine. Return the supported account, its limits and any consequential alternatives. For a decision about continuation, give the grounds for continuing, revising, branching, replacing or stopping the practice, or identify the open question.

Providers and practitioners can continue a supported practice or, within their authority, change how it is generated, transmitted, used, recognized, selected, remembered, retained or lost. A local decision has its own scope. Wider prevalence, later retention and a human capability outcome each require evidence for that claim.

Use **HCD.11–HCD.16** for their respective questions about individual development or Method use. Use **C.36** for general cultural evolution, **C.36.MC** for Method Engineering culture and **OCE** for organizational culture or change. A learning product, curriculum, publication history, formal standard or the introduction of one Method may instead have its own direct question. Use the established result or seek the needed contribution under that practice.

### HCD.17:2 - Problem

HCD practices can pass through teaching, peer work, assignments, feedback, assessments and communities. Descriptions, tools, repositories and remembered cases can carry material for that work. To establish a cultural claim, identify what happened to the practice in the specified population and period.

A document can be published and never reach its intended readers. Trainers can teach a practice that recipients never recognize or choose, or that they use and later abandon. A required form can be completed without the development work it describes. Activity in a community can be observed before there is evidence of a change in the person’s later work.

A publication, event or adoption decision can establish a fact about dissemination or authorization. To establish a change in culture or capability, examine the corresponding practice or performance. A well-supported current account can finish without another experiment. Consider a new observation or intervention where it would address an important remaining question.

### HCD.17:3 - Forces

| Force | Working tension |
| --- | --- |
| Familiar labels and testable relations | Schools, standards and communities aid recognition, while the label may conceal generation, transmission, receiving use, selection, memory, retention or loss. |
| Carriers and practice | Identify what the descriptions, tools or forums contributed to the practice, or which event they document. To establish continuation, use evidence about the practice in the relevant population. |
| Method status and observation | To report enactment of a Method, establish its admission and the work that instantiated it. A candidate or source-described practice can support a different account of what people did. |
| Local action and population scope | A provider can act within its local mandate. A claim about the wider field needs evidence for that population. An intervention affecting other parties needs authority covering those parties and that action. |
| Culture and human capability | A cultural relation may matter because later capability matters, while neither observation proves the other or their causal link. |
| Timely learning and retention | Receiving use can be observed soon, while long-term retention and loss require later intervals. |
| Continuation and explanation | Evidence can warrant continuing while the explanation remains open. Investigate a credible rival where the attainable improvement to the conclusion or its use justifies the burden. |

### HCD.17:4 - Solution

State what the available evidence establishes about the practice in the specified population. If continuation or change is at issue, identify the supported decision, proposal or remaining limit. An account of past receiving use can finish with the observations for its period and the limits of any inference about human capability.

Select a new observation or intervention when its attainable contribution warrants the full effort, delay, participant burden and displaced development or protection. Include design costs. Preserve the grounds a recipient needs. Claims about an implemented change, later use, retention or capability require evidence of the particular event or outcome.

#### HCD.17:4.1 - Bound the HCD practice, population, and decision

Identify the HCD Discipline from a qualified result, or name the smaller practice the evidence covers. Identify the participants in the cultural relation being examined. State the place and period, relevant later-work family, the evidence or qualification window that bears on the claim, and the requested finding or decision.

Bound the population and identify its participants’ roles in the practice. A local provider group and its learners may be sufficient. A wider claim about an organization or field needs evidence covering that population.

If the practice, population, period, intended finding or requested decision cannot be bounded, identify the missing fact and what it would establish. Retain the conclusion supported at the narrower scope.

#### HCD.17:4.2 - Choose the Branch that Matches Method or Candidate Status

Use the **admitted-Method branch** when the claim concerns enactment of an admitted HCD Method or variant. Identify the admitted Method and evidence that the relevant performance instantiated it. Teaching a description, publishing a card or configuring a tool can be evidence about those events. For a claim of enactment, establish the relation between the work and the Method.

Use the **candidate or observed-practice branch** for a candidate, source-described practice, local routine or material such as a card, template or description. Give its supported status and what the evidence independently establishes about the work. Establish the stronger status separately if claiming an admitted Method, its MethodDescription or enactment of the whole.

Carry the status into the result. If admission, description membership, reusable semantics, lineage or introduction matters, use the relevant Method Engineering result or identify the specific remaining question.

#### HCD.17:4.3 - State one cultural value and predicate

Identify the development practice whose continuation matters. For a teaching practice, use evidence of how the receiving practitioner taught. For a learning practice, use evidence of how the learner studied or practised. A trainer’s use of a feedback sequence, the learner’s answer and performance in the target job can be three separate observations.

Identify the practice value and the particular relation being claimed. Specify the following where they bear on the conclusion.

- the participants and their roles in the relation, such as who transmitted the practice and who used it;
- applicability conditions and qualification window;
- a case that would count as an instance of the relation;
- a contrasting case that would fail that test, fall outside its scope or leave the answer unresolved, including when information is missing; and
- the conclusion or decision that a different observation could affect.

Use an existing direct predicate when it fits. Otherwise use FPF A.6.RCD to determine whether a bounded relation-bearing claim can be derived from the available predicates and permitted constructors. Identify the basis still needed when it cannot. A convenient cultural label does not create a relation kind or occurrence.

Give separate results for generation, publication, transmission, receiving use, recognition, selection, memory, retention and loss when more than one is claimed. Their evidence and scope can differ.

#### HCD.17:4.4 - Identify the actual carriers, Work, and participating subjects

Identify the carriers, performances, participants and relations the claim uses. These can include materials of a known status, assessment or feedback records, publications, tools and AI configurations, teaching or learner work, decision rules, assignments, permissions, access, provider services and memory records.

For a claim that work took place, identify its performer and use evidence that the relevant work was done. Apply the direct Work criteria when its formal status is part of the claim. For Method enactment, also establish the relation to the admitted Method. A programme, platform or school name can identify where to look.

Examine an organization or architecture when its relationships affect the finding or decision. Identify the evidence for the particular claim about transmission, use, selection, retention or capability.

#### HCD.17:4.5 - Recover the authority and protection needed by the intended action

For intended action that requires authorization, identify who may do what, for whom and within what scope. Establish the applicable assignment, permission or decision right and its protections. A sponsor or knowledgeable provider can supply evidence or support; check whether their role also grants the needed authority. For a factual account, establish any authority relevant to what happened during its period.

If a proposed intervention exceeds the mandate, identify the missing authorization and withhold the affected action. Preserve supported cultural findings. Organizational change, employment, care, provider operation, platform administration, learning-product design, privacy, safety and target-domain actions retain their respective authorities.

State participation, consent, privacy, access, workload, exclusion, accessibility, service-pressure, and restoration conditions that matter. Stop the affected intervention if it breaches a protection. Revert only where a safe, feasible and authorized restoration exists.

#### HCD.17:4.6 - Keep human capability and later Work as a separate consequence

If the question concerns human capability or later work, identify the person or population, the observations available, the relevant interval and any uncertainty. For a claim about change, identify the baseline or state what its absence leaves open. Separate an observed consequence from the expected benefit of a proposal. Use **HCD.11**, **HCD.12**, **HCD.13** or qualified equivalent evidence for performance, transfer, delayed use or support dependence where applicable. An established cultural relation can answer the cultural question.

Receiving use can be established while change in learner capability remains unknown. Equally, observed learner performance can leave transmission or selection open. To attribute a consequence to an intervention, use evidence for that causal link.

#### HCD.17:4.7 - Settle the continuation and select inquiry only when it contributes

Retain credible hypotheses whose differences could change this continuation or warranted claim. Examples include carrier sufficiency versus coached feedback, formal selection versus local workaround, community participation versus supervisor access, or remembered description versus repeated receiving Work. Do not invent a second explanation to reach a fixed count. An explanation may remain unresolved while the current bounded practice is worth continuing.

If a continuation decision is needed, assess the relevant options. These can include keeping the arrangement, changing a Method, support, assessment or carrier, branching for a population, replacing the means or stopping. Use applicable existing observations and judgement. Keep the scope of the available population and time evidence visible.

When a material uncertainty, changed receiving condition, or protective concern makes inquiry useful, identify what an attainable observation could change. Compare its whole contribution and burden through C.11.DUA when that demand needs appraisal; use C.11 for an already formed bounded choice and the direct HCD or field Method for the selected inquiry. Recover participants, provider capability, access, resources, opportunity window, and authorization that determine feasibility. For a selected intervention, retain reversibility, burden and protection limits, the discriminating expectation, negative case, and response rule. `unknown` withholds the unresolved claim, not an independently supported continuation. An unavailable or unhelpful trial does not become a completion task.

#### HCD.17:4.8 - Return the supported account and distinguish any later result

Return the supported account, its grounds and limits, with a decision if the task called for one. For a tested change or a later occurrence, use work and observations from the relevant interval. Apply the same predicate to the stated participants and identify any change of population. If the predicate changes, state what comparison it still permits. Distinguish positive, negative, inapplicable and unresolved cases, including missing information. Keep a proposed test separate from its eventual result.

For a retained or shared account, include the positions its claims and receiving use require.

| Position | Content when used |
| --- | --- |
| Boundary | HCD Discipline or smaller practice, population, participants, place, period, relevant later work, qualification window and requested finding or decision. |
| Subject branch | Admitted Method and grounded actual enactment, or candidate/observed practice with materials of the stated status and independently supported Work facts. |
| Cultural claim | Value, predicate, applicability, a positive case and a discriminating countercase, the observations available for the stated interval and any evidence gaps. |
| Participating subjects | Actual carriers, descriptions or candidate materials, publications, Systems, Work, assignments, permissions, authority, access and support relations relied on. |
| Selected intervention or inquiry | Material alternatives, attainable contribution, full burden, feasible work, required authority and protections. For an intervention, give the safeguards for stopping or safely reversing it. For a selected comparison, identify the observation that would discriminate and what its outcomes would warrant. |
