Each mentor visits groups at 11:02–11:08, 11:12–11:18 and 11:22–11:28. The inputs are ready before the visits, and the four-minute gaps allow movement or connection. Each group can use the response. The 36-minute activity makes B’s core 96 minutes. The staggered starts and finishes require the separate group windows shown below.

For this cohort, the eight minutes per person cover checking the first response and preparing usable feedback. Allow four further minutes to check a correction or subsequent response and return the finding. The eight fixed hours include preparing the unit-support material and briefing its provider. Helping the six entrants who use the branch takes four provider-minutes each within their twenty-minute activity.

| Provider contribution for one cohort | A: individual help | B: four-person groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed case, material and provider preparation | 8 h | 8 h |
| Help with the six preparation branches | 24 min | 24 min |
| Main subject-help appointments or booked group window | 144 min | 60 min |
| First-response checks and feedback, 24 × 8 min | 192 min | 192 min |
| Correction checks, 24 × 4 min | 96 min | 96 min |
| Cohort contact, collection and return of work | 48 min | 72 min |
| Qualified recovery reserve | 48 min | 72 min |
| Recurring provider allocation, including reserve | 552 min = 9.2 h | 516 min = 8.6 h |
| Fixed plus recurring allocation for this one cohort | 17.2 h | 16.6 h |

The 48 and 72 coordination minutes cover cohort scheduling, missing submissions and returning results. Fixed preparation and the booked group window are already in their own rows. At eight minutes each, the recovery reserves cover six interventions in A and nine in B. Reserved time counts toward provider allocation even if the cohort uses less.

The proposed two-day schedule makes the feedback usable under these conditions.

- Before the main work, schedule the six entrants to complete the twenty-minute preparation branch and receive its booked help. In each core, the 20-minute preparation and 10-minute first judgement come before comparison of reasons.
- In A, book the 24 complete six-minute subject-help appointments between 09:00 and 11:24 on day one. Each learner starts their thirty-minute comparison twelve minutes before their appointment: twelve minutes comparing the supplied reasons, six receiving help and twelve using the response. A prepared common channel and preloaded case make opening and closing part of that complete appointment; extra setup would require extra booking. The last comparison ends at 11:36. In B, follow HCD.20's named assignments and staggered group starts; groups finish at 11:26, 11:36 and 11:46. Their later personal responses finish at 11:36, 11:46 and 11:56. The mentors' 60 booked minutes contain the 36 direct minutes and all stated transition gaps.
- On this schedule all 24 ten-minute personal responses can be ready by noon. One qualified assessor has 14:00–17:12 for 192 minutes of first-response checking and feedback. Arrange for each learner to receive their usable feedback by 09:00 on day two.
- Allow fifteen minutes for learners to read the feedback and make a correction or further response if needed, due by noon on day two. From 13:00 to 14:36 the assessor has 96 minutes reserved for the follow-up responses, with results due by 15:00. Each learner has five minutes for their return plan by 18:00.
- From 15:00 a prepared, qualified provider has 48 minutes in A or 72 in B for unresolved corrections or missed opportunities. If demand exceeds that reserve, obtain additional feasible help where needed or identify the remaining limit. To report a learner’s performance, use their work.

For 24 people, A’s 90-minute core needs 36 learner-hours and B’s 96-minute core needs 38.4. Six preparation branches add two hours to each. At fifteen learner-minutes per possible recovery, full use of the reserve adds 1.5 hours in A or 2.25 in B. Total active time at full reserve use is 39.5 and 42.65 learner-hours. The two-day schedule separately shows the elapsed wait for feedback. A requirement to finish on day one would rule out these versions.

B reserves 36 fewer provider-minutes than A. If all learner recovery time is used, B needs 189 more active learner-minutes. Choosing between these burdens depends on the use, and equal learning quality has yet to be established. A later cohort has recurring work of its own and can reuse fixed preparation while the cases, criteria and provider readiness still apply. The four specialist-hours in the pump exercise are simulated. If real measurements are part of the offer, include their actual supply and conditions.

Both variants reserve 288 minutes for first-response and follow-up checks. Group discussion leaves that allocation in place. For a stronger estimate of capacity or cost, use evidence of the responses, correction needs, coordination work and recovery actually observed under the relevant conditions.

#### HCD.28:5.2 - Changed conditions change the construction

If learners need to calculate a known indicator reliably, a supported individual task with a meaningful calculation and error check may cover the target with less coordination. Include a model comparison where selecting or examining a model is part of the work.

If the customer needs only a diagnostic report by tomorrow, a competent provider able to deliver it in time may complete the service. Compare alternatives if the customer needs a choice. Teaching the customer to diagnose calls for a separate learning opportunity.

For a scarce instrument, work from access, usable observation and the operation each learner must perform. With HCD.20 and HCD.22, identify which actions observers can perform, who needs an operating turn and which tasks can overlap. Choose a group size and timing that fit the instrument and the learning target.

If an entrant already selects models and has limited access to the proposed mentor, HCD.2 can assess the product’s fit or compare feasible programme changes for that person. Use that person’s established performance, later work and actual access to decide which parts they need.

### HCD.28:6 - Bias-Annotation

| Likely drift | Consequence | Corrective question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Topic and media attraction | More content or a simulator replaces the missing selection or connection. | Which required action becomes possible through this addition? |
| Expert rescue | A strong reader fills a gap the material never supplied. | Did the source or actual help provide the decisive relation? |
| Average-learner substitution | An audience hypothesis becomes a personal recommendation. | Which same-person evidence selects this route? |
| Scale optimism | Fixed cost is divided by an imagined unlimited audience. | Over how many uses can the preparation be shared, and what recurring checks and peak demand does that scale entail? |
| Product-success substitution | A polished prototype or shared answer becomes a learning claim. | Which learner action was observed under which help? |

### HCD.28:7 - Conformance Checklist

For a design result, check that the recipient can do the following for its intended use.

- identify the target work, personal contribution, preparation assumptions and meaningful branches;
- use a qualified subject basis, obtain it where feasible or identify the subject contribution still missing;
- follow the connections required from entry through the task, permitted help, feedback and any necessary correction to the intended observation, or identify where the route breaks;
- assess one construction against its requirements or compare the available variants on comparable outcomes and complete burdens;
- locate material and provider dependencies and the peak demand that matters to feasibility;
- identify what can already be used and any personal, subject, material or supply question that still needs work.

For stronger reliance, use evidence of material use, operating provision, personal performance or effects according to the claim. A design can support an offer comparison before those events take place.

### HCD.28:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Failure | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalogue as product | Lessons are present but the learner cannot reach a whole result. | Construct and exercise the connections in one complete task family. |
| Companion as hidden subject invention | The teaching author invents a model-selection criterion without subject qualification. | Use a qualified criterion or identify the missing subject judgement. When developing it is in scope, do so with the relevant competence or obtain it from a qualified source. |
| Universal entry | Different preparation is treated as lack of effort. | Select a bounded branch from a relevant action and return it to the whole task. |
| Group answer as personal result | One participant supplies the target operation for everyone. | Preserve the needed individual actions and observations. |
| Free peer or AI support | Costs and competence disappear from the offer. | Identify actual contributions, checking, preparation and recovery. |
| Successful fragment as full programme | One working task is used to promise outcomes the product does not yet enable. | Identify the task family the route serves and what each wider outcome still requires. |
| Whole rebuild after one failure | A local supply or material defect triggers unnecessary redevelopment. | Diagnose and repair the affected connection. |

### HCD.28:9 - Consequences

A future-audience design can be judged before a particular learner arrives. Subject, teaching and supply findings identify different work. Use established materials and shared tasks where suitable. A claim about an individual still needs that person’s entry, work and conditions.

Making the connections explicit takes work on cases, explanations, help, interpretation and resource limits. An attractive offer may still lack one of these contributions. Reassess the affected construction if a change in preparation, subject criterion, assistance, scale, timing or observed work changes the grounds for using it.

### HCD.28:10 - Architectural Rationale

A sound explanation may be unavailable at the point where the learner needs it. Useful feedback can arrive after their opportunity to act. Following the whole route reveals these failures. A design for a future audience requires stated assumptions about preparation and supply. For a known person, also use their evidence of starting performance and their later work.

A supported individual route can provide the whole learning opportunity. Include shared activity where others supply a needed contribution and preserve the learner’s own work. Use the same applicable subject criterion for explanations, tasks and feedback so the learner is not given conflicting answers to the same question. When the criterion changes, inspect the uses that depend on it. A changed method, a teaching defect and an unavailable service may need different repairs.

### HCD.28:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The official [4C/ID overview](https://www.4cid.org/about/) distinguishes the four contributions used in §4.3. It informs the task-centred design. Evaluating the effect of this module requires evidence about this module.

HCD.5–HCD.8, HCD.18 and HCD.19 explain the learning and material methods used here. HCD.20 and HCD.22 explain the group designs. This chapter combines them to compare whole products and locate subject, teaching or supply gaps. Its diagnostic example uses prospective planning allowances. For empirical claims about costs or learning, use observations appropriate to the claim.

### HCD.28:12 - Relations

- **Consumes:** qualified work and subject-method accounts, audience assumptions, candidate product fragments, access and resource constraints.
- **Uses:** HCD.5, HCD.6 and HCD.6.1 for development and tasks; HCD.7 and HCD.8 for support; HCD.20–HCD.27 for the selected group contributions and their actual conditions; HCD.18 and HCD.19 for material diagnosis.
- **Supplies:** conditional product variants and requirements to HCD.2; tasks and support to HCD.9 and HCD.10; qualified observation needs to HCD.11–HCD.13.
- **Subject and service questions:** Core Method-development patterns and RMP can address an implicit or missing subject method. Use Learning Product practice for Guide or Slidement construction and SYSE.2, SYSE.8 or the responsible provider for the corresponding service question.
- **Revises through:** HCD.14 for affected development assumptions and HCD.16 for the live method-claim question. A market, launch or operational decision retains its own evidence and authority.

### HCD.28:End


# Cross-Pattern Application


## HCD.Application:1 - Instructional-material evaluation profile

Use this profile to assess what an explanation, worksheet, course route or instructional interface enables the intended audience to do under specified task and assistance conditions. The result can guide a material repair or answer how well the existing material serves the task. Claims about a learner’s performance, a teaching service or later learning need their corresponding evidence.

Start with the promised reader work, prerequisites, available material and help, and the finding or decision the evaluation must serve. Use [HCD.18](#hcd18---select-or-construct-a-characterization-and-evaluation-specification-for-instructional-material) to construct a missing or unsuitable specification. With a compatible specification, use [HCD.19](#hcd19---evaluate-instructional-material-through-representative-reader-work-and-diagnose-its-repair) directly to assess the material and available representative reader work. Return the supported property judgement or evidence gap. If a defect is established, identify its reach and what would test a proposed repair.

Use HCD.3 to establish a learning target or HCD.6 to construct a representative task, as needed. Use HCD.7 for a required contribution from assistance and HCD.9 for practice with feedback when needed. Qualified equivalent inputs can serve directly. Recommending personal development needs evidence about the person. A professional reference can be evaluated for its decision use. If it also promises instruction, assess what it enables the intended reader to learn.


### HCD.Application:1.1 - Choose properties from the promised work

Derive the set of required tasks from the promise and qualified subject requirements. Include prerequisites, consequential variations and critical errors. For each required task, find the explanation, example, exercise or accessible outside contribution that supports it. Identify any task the available material leaves unsupported. Chapter headings can help locate those contributions.

Select properties according to the judgement the recipient needs. A difference may affect the finding, grounds for use, repair, observation or protection of an existing contribution. Use HCD.18 to check whether the selected set covers that question.

| Characteristic family | What distinguishes useful support from a limiting defect | Typical repair and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task and dependency coverage | Every promised task and consequential variation has its needed operations and prerequisites available. | Trace required work to actual contributions. Supply an absent operation, usable qualified return, or narrower promise. |
| Subject validity and distinction integrity | Claims, examples, diagrams, and criteria preserve domain-correct kinds, relations, units, conditions, and justified claim strength. | Test a plausible countercase against a qualified subject basis. Correct the relation and its actual dependents. |
| Extractable structural information, when its amount matters | Which selected relations can the specified reader recover from the material episteme through this expression, under the stated conditions? Use C.2.8. | Identify recovered and missing relations. For a count, fix the semantic units. For a fraction, also fix its denominator. When a relation is missing or wrong, repair the account, its expression or the route to the needed contribution. Evidence for effort, adequacy and learning answers separate questions. |
| Explanatory sufficiency | With the declared assistance, can the reader recover why a move follows and when it should change? | Trace the explanation through an application. Restore a missing ground, contrast, transition or operation if needed. Use reader evidence when the claimed result depends on it. |
| Example discrimination | Do the examples distinguish the intended rule from a plausible competing rule where their answers differ? | Apply both to the example or a relevant contrast. Where both would give the same visible answer, choose a changed condition that distinguishes them. |
| Task and criterion validity | The task elicits the promised contribution, and the criterion accepts valid alternatives while rejecting a plausible error. | Independently solve and challenge the task and key. Repair the criterion before blaming the reader or changing a correct explanation. |
| Feedback and continuation support | Can a reader use the criterion to correct an error or retain a supported answer, and try again when the learning question calls for it? | For a design, check what the feedback could supply and whether it can reach the reader in time. For a claim about use, establish what reached the reader and what the reader did with it. If the task includes repair, improve the criterion or feedback, provide a needed retry or address a missing service with its provider. |
| Concrete and expressive support | Does an action, observation, image, example or memorable cue reveal a relation the reader needs, including its limits? | Keep or restore details that help the reader recognize, interpret or use that relation. |
| Representation semantic fit | The chosen text, image, table, or interaction exposes the needed relation accurately and accessibly. | Repair the mapping, label, relation, pacing, or relevant alternative representation. Inspect an export separately when its rendering changes access. |
| Language comprehensibility for the audience | Can the reader interpret the claim and its scope with the language and preparation the material assumes? | In the declared language, clarify an ambiguous referent, correct unintended negation or explain unfamiliar wording when it changes the reading. |
| Currentness of relied-on content | Does the particular claim still support this operation under the stated subject or source conditions? | Check the changed premise and the uses that depended on it. Preserve claims that still have adequate grounds. |
| Practical addressability and access | Can the reader reach the source, prerequisite, task or feedback when it is needed? | Repair the destination or supply another usable route. Report a retrieval failure separately from the truth of the subject claim. |
| Narrative attachment, when relevant | Can the reader tell which question the contribution answers, why it appears here and how the later work uses it? | With NSTD.8, inspect both ends of the connection and restore the relation or placement that the route needs. |
| Progressive reconstruction support, when live | The required operation fits the structure already introduced or legitimately available, with adequate support for the new relation. | Use NSTD.8 to supply a contrast, map, worked relation, recap, usable return, or better order while retaining useful difficulty. |

One observation can support different property judgements. A valid explanation can coexist with an invalid key. A teacher can supply the relation an example leaves ambiguous. A sound diagram can become unreadable in an export. Separate the judgements when their evidence or repairs differ, and count a shared observation once when assessing independent support.


### HCD.Application:1.2 - Interpret material value separately from evidence and fit

For material use and repair, use a qualified ordinal judgement by default. A numerical 0–5 rendering is optional. For a C.2.8 structural amount, use its own justified comparison, count, fraction or other structural scale. Before using the material-quality scale below, bind its meanings to the selected property, material unit, task family and available support.

| Value | Material meaning for the declared use |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The material demonstrably supplies no usable support for the required property, or defeats an explicitly declared non-compensable condition at this evaluation grain. |
| 1 | Some relevant support exists, but a material part of the promised work remains out of reach. |
| 2 | Useful work is recoverable, but repair must rebuild a connected central explanation–task chain or several consequential dependent uses. |
| 3 | The main work is recoverable; a bounded correction to the identified relation, task, representation, or return is still needed. |
| 4 | The property is adequate for the declared tasks, audience, and available support on the evidence required by the specification; no material defect is currently established for that use. |
| 5 | The property has defensible additional useful resilience across the specification's consequential variations or boundary cases; the advantage and its evidence over 4 are stated. |

The numbers express an order. Distances between values are unspecified. For a severe local defect, trace its consequences for the declared task family and any non-compensable condition before judging the whole book. A high average cannot compensate for failure of a condition the intended use requires in its own right.

Set any floor for the intended use. Time-use S1 in HCD.18 requires 4 on each selected property for its bounded supported introduction. A different diagnostic or controlled trial may use a different decision rule while retaining the same meanings for the values.

For each value, identify the grounds, such as source inspection, an observed attempt or a conditional inference. Check object fit before applying the scale. If evidence or grounds for the criterion are missing, state which judgement remains open and why. Keep that required property visible in the result. A demonstrated absence of support can warrant 0, while a lack of evidence leaves the value unknown.

Explain the grounds for the assigned value and why neighbouring values fit less well. The difference between a connected and a bounded repair depends on what must change for the reader. A 5 needs a supported advantage over 4 across a relevant variation. If a useful improvement is available at 4, compare its benefit, burden and effect on the other protected contributions.

Earlier evaluations under other specifications retain their original value meanings. For example, a local Guide scale whose 0 includes wrong kind or no basis is not numerically equivalent to this material scale. A comparison may relate “connected repair” to “bounded repair” while explicitly declining numeric conversion.


### HCD.Application:1.3 - Use the two methods together without adding a lifecycle

Use HCD.18 when the specification is missing or inadequate. Its result identifies fit, the task set, properties and scale meanings, required evidence, treatment of missing values, interpretation, contrasts, protected trade-offs and grounds for stopping or reopening. A.19.ECS supplies general specification construction, and HCD.18 adds the instructional choices.

With HCD.19, use the specification for the material, subject criterion, available reader work and help involved. Qualified source inspection or compatible existing observations can settle a diagnosis. Identify any claim still lacking evidence. Seek further reader work when it is feasible under the relevant access, participation and protection and its expected contribution justifies the full burden. Use E.23 for a needed improvement and E.22 for a comparison on a common qualified basis. If the format or teacher arrangement changes that basis, reassess the affected use and preserve the earlier judgement for its original conditions.

For long material, a whole-route conclusion needs connected inspection of the complete declared route and its cross-part dependencies. For a local defect, inspect the smallest complete semantic reach and reuse unaffected evidence. A moved explanation can change the next-use prefix even if its words are unchanged.

For a narrative question, NSTD.6 distinguishes the product, the fidelity promised between its source and the resulting expression, and how the product was made. NSTD.8 examines placement and what the reader can use by that point. NarrativeRenderingEpiplexity specializes C.2.8 for the selected structure, expressed episteme, expression, observer and reading conditions. Reuse a structural result when those grounds carry over. C.2.8 can also serve non-narrative material through HCD.18 and HCD.19. To assess experienced difficulty, retain the human report at its scope. A material diagnosis may finish while a claim about the wider audience, learning or cognitive load remains open. Consider a timely observation of the intended reader when the necessary access, participation and protection are available. Select it when what can be learned would justify the preparation, reader and provider time, interpretation, delay and displaced work for this finding or decision. Use its result once it has been obtained.

M0’s uninterrupted example is compatible with both active effort and elapsed turnaround. A prepared reader distinguishes them and identifies prior knowledge that the material did not supply. M1 revises the definitions, columns, interruption example and population denominator. The same reader then correctly compares three consumed person-hours with four available in a changed two-person case. These observations support the material repair and this prepared reader’s use. A claim about learning by novices remains open.

The full Time-use S1 specification also requires an example with concurrent participants, an inspected task and key, and evidence of explanatory and feedback support for the intended audience. After the successful agent answers, the HCD.19 assessment identifies which material changes and audience observations would address the remaining gaps. The material judgement can finish before the wider audience question is resolved.


### HCD.Application:1.4 - Why this profile is useful, and when a simpler alternative suffices

A qualified subject inspection may settle a false claim or unit relation. To judge whether intended readers can recover an instruction, use their declared preparation, the material and permitted help. An expert walkthrough may support a bounded recoverability judgement. To report a reader’s response or experience, use evidence of that person. FPF F.19:4.5 explains when an actual reading is needed. Use an existing task-and-scoring specification if its task, population, help and interpretation fit. For a defect confined to one export, inspect that rendered version. For a semantic defect, follow its reach into the other versions that use the same content.

The profile costs the work of establishing tasks and useful contrasts. That work reveals omissions a heading list can miss. When interpreting a score, consider what is known about the material, the reader’s prior knowledge and any assistance received. Establishing which caused the response can require a further comparison. A narrow source defect can be diagnosed and repaired while a stronger claim about learners remains open.

An expert can fill a missing ground, and an evaluator’s cue can supply the answer. Preserve the relevant first response before giving such a cue in a new probe. For completed work, use evidence of the subject criteria, material, audience and help that reached the reader. Reassess properties when a changed premise, material, observed response or recurrent disagreement changes the grounds for their use.


### HCD.Application:1.5 - Source-informed choices and limits

The profile adapts task- and interpretation-sensitive evaluation, examples that distinguish rival rules, and observations that retain assistance and continuation conditions. HCD.18 and HCD.19 explain the comparisons and source limits. To claim that the profile or its ordinal values are validated for a particular use, establish that validation separately.

[Wesenberg et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cedpsych.2024.102328) report ambiguity in worked examples for the topics they studied. Studies by [McCrudden and colleagues in 2022](https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/promoting-integration-and-learning-from-multiple-complementary-te/) and [2024](https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED642756) inform the connection between principles, examples and self-explanation. In this profile the task must make the intended relation consequential. Choose the order of explanation and practice for the learning use.

[Noetel et al. (2022)](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3102/00346543211052329) inform selection of a representation repair by its proposed mechanism. [Sinha and Kapur (2021)](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.3102/00346543211019105) distinguish preparation with subsequent resolving instruction from unsupported difficulty. [Wisniewski et al. (2020)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32038429/) inform examination of how feedback functions. Choose any required reader sample and local threshold for the task being evaluated. Judge whole-book adequacy using the evidence its claims require.

[Bastani et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122) inform the distinction between assisted and later independent performance in their studied setting. [Krieglstein et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-024-09980-0) address the timing and scope of reports of experienced burden. [Bavaresco et al. (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-short.20/) report task-dependent limits on substituting LLM judgements for human judgements. Use these results within their conditions and establish human learning from the relevant human work.


## HCD.Application:2 - APP-HCD-01 - Constructed ImpactReview-17 decision

The constructed `ImpactReview-17` exercise uses `ImpactReview-17-Domain-Oracle-v1` for its engineering criteria and critical errors under `PumpWorks-Config-Baseline-42` and `AI-Assist-M4`. The supplied observations and decision conditions let the reader derive demand, examine the difficulty and compare profile choices. For real work, use qualified criteria and evidence about the actual person and work.

Engineer-P14 must independently review AI-proposed change-impact claims for mixed physical and software pump-controller changes before separate integration, assurance and release decisions. The constructed 2026-Q4 conditions provide current sources and configuration, the named assistant, recoverable audit records, a 45-minute limit and bounded safety and maintenance specialist results. P14 may receive a routine reminder to construct and test an alternative configuration hypothesis. P14 must supply the case-specific alternative and test. A cue that gives the rival changes the evidence about that contribution. Integration, safety, release and employment decisions have their own holders.

For HCD.1 the case supplies eight representative review occurrences, four familiar and four unfamiliar. Four include plausible but erroneous AI dependency claims, and two require specialist results. Within these conditions the demand on P14 includes recognizing applicability, tracing claims to source and configuration, independently challenging plausible AI output, delimiting specialist results, returning auditable evidence and detecting every seeded safety-critical omission.

At baseline P14 correctly traces claims and returns evidence in 8/8 cases, routes both specialist questions correctly, and rejects 2/4 plausible wrong AI claims. In the two unfamiliar misses, the neutral `E.23.CAE`-shaped check preserves method, sources, tool, time, assignment, authority and specialist route. P14 recognizes the need for independent checking but does not generate and test a competing hypothesis. HCD.3 identifies the target **generate and test an independent configuration counter-hypothesis before accepting plausible AI output in an unfamiliar variant**. The small sample and a possible prompt-design limitation still affect that diagnosis.

The HCD.4 profile retains four claims and their separate grounds.

| Claim | Current constructed evidence | Target and trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source/configuration trace | 8/8 | Preserve; do not trade traceability for speed. |
| independent AI-output challenge | 2/4 planted-error cases; both misses unfamiliar | Priority gap; target 4/4 and zero accepted seeded safety-critical omissions, with the forty-five-minute limit visible. |
| bounded specialist return | 2/2 relevant cases | Preserve the authority boundary. |
| auditable evidence return | 8/8 | Preserve; no aggregate may hide a missing critical-error record. |

Within a pre-authorized twelve-hour allocation, Engineer-P14 is the `DecisionSubject` for choosing a self-development focus. The options are `O1`, retain the existing arrangement, `O2`, prioritize independent AI-output challenge for possible programme comparison while preserving the supported claims, and `O3`, defer a personal priority and return the prompt-design question to the method or tool owner.

P14 compares O2 and O3 with the small sample and prompt-design rival in view. The proposed probe uses two further unfamiliar seeded-error cases, one first attempt on each. One has the neutral prompt, the other the explicit reminder specified in HCD.3:5.1. Success with the reminder can establish performance under the allowed assistance while leaving spontaneous recall open. If P14 succeeds only with the reminder, this can favour returning the prompt-design question to its owner. Keep sources, tools, specialist routes and the 45-minute case limit fixed. Up to 90 minutes for attempts and 30 for preparation and comparison fit the two-hour probe budget within the twelve-hour allocation. The possible results could change the O2/O3 preference enough to warrant the probe. Differences between the two cases still limit causal attribution to prompting. P14’s C.11 result is **`ChoiceResult = probe again`**. The focus and programme choices remain open.


## HCD.Application:3 - APP-HCD-02 - Constructed performance, transfer, retention and revision

Learner-L17 is a different fictional person from Engineer-P14 and Engineer-E27. The following observations are supplied as conditions of the worked example.

The exercise requires HW3/FW8. B has the highest stipulated NPV, with A/B/C at about 48.9/51.6/44.6 thousand, but its FW7 report cannot qualify B for FW8. A still needs a shared-power check. C has a compatible HW3/FW8/SCHED2 report. The exercise requires two hours of checks per change and one preparation hour per homogeneous batch of at most four. Ten changes need 23 hours and twelve need 27. With 24 hours and twelve arrivals, proposing ten leaves two changes in the queue. With 22 hours, nine need 21 hours and ten will not fit. The release manager decides what may be released for use. These are supplied engineering assumptions for the exercise.

| Independent Method question | Constructed observation or proposed change | Bounded result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HCD.11: what did L17 contribute? | The first answer calculates correctly but accepts B despite FW7. L17 corrects the answer with a teacher’s cue. In two fresh representative cases, traces show L17 finding the mismatch before any teacher or AI cue and explaining a supported continuation and queue limit. | The initial failure, correction with help and later independent performance have different grounds. Report the contribution for the tested cases and conditions. |
| HCD.12: how does L17 handle unfamiliar conditions? | A compatible HW3/FW8/SCHED2 report is available. With 24 hours, L17 independently proposes ten and gives the queue limit. At 22 hours, L17 first keeps ten and corrects to nine after feedback. | The configuration-evidence result transfers in the stated case. The resource adaptation is supported with help. Stronger reliance on independent adaptation needs an appropriately uncued observation. |
| HCD.14: which arrangement component changes now? | At the transfer return, replace the cue-led resource exercise with action/refusal contrasts and a fresh uncued capacity variation. Keep calculation, configuration checking, source access and resource limits protected. | A local testable revision hypothesis, not a settled cause, performed programme change or causal effect. HCD.13 is not a prerequisite. |
| HCD.13: what remains after the interval? | Matched earlier and eight-week observations cover selected F.1, C.16 and C.11 contributions during stated intermittent practice and normal support. A separately specified 15-minute core allows tables and calculator without AI. The order of tasks is known. Another attempt encounters a source-access failure. | Report retention of the compared contributions and the narrow core under those conditions. The failed access identifies a different limit. Untested patterns, the whole cohort, non-use during the interval and a causal effect of revision require separate evidence. |

Each method supplies its own case and conditions for the corresponding question. L17’s observations apply to L17. ReleaseWork-R9 below still requires evidence about its own performer and work.


## HCD.Application:4 - APP-HCD-03 - Constructed continuation, Method repertoire and culture

This example stipulates the development and cultural evidence for Engineer-E27, `CapabilityDevelopmentTeam-E27` and `ReleaseWork-R9`. It illustrates conditional findings. To report participation, performed work, method status, achieved capability or cultural use in a real setting, establish the corresponding fact there.

The intended later work is an independent review of AI-assisted mixed physical and software release claims. It includes checking configuration impact, challenging a plausible wrong AI output, returning auditable evidence, justifying action or refusal, and using safety and maintenance specialist contributions within their scope. The example supplies a compatible HCD.14 proposal to retain familiar trace and specialist-return practice and replace one cue-led correction exercise with action/refusal contrasts and a fresh uncued counter-hypothesis case.

| Independent Method question | Constructed first result | Boundary preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HCD.15: can development continue under relevant change? | The arrangement identifies representative cases, first-attempt capture, current sources, permitted AI use, coaching, specialist access, reassessment, responsible parties and stop conditions. A material change to release method, configuration, AI, critical errors, qualification, sources, providers or support can require reassessment. Here protected learner and provider time is missing. Return `continuing-arrangement-blocked` while the needed protected time remains unavailable. To restore this arrangement, establish an effective limit and allocation with the responsible party. HCD.15:5.3 gives a separate case with the allocation and qualified inputs in place. | A trigger or plan can support a proposal. Claims of participation, completed development or later work, capability and causal effect need their own evidence. |
| HCD.16: which repertoire claim changes? | Retain the admitted trace-and-specialist-return method at its stated scope, with representative attempts, feedback, correction or reasoned retention, and retry when needed. Withdraw the unsupported independent-learning claim for this use. This finding does not retire the method. Cue-led and counter-hypothesis-first alternatives remain candidates. Their comparison needs three learner-hours and two provider-hours for preparation, attempts, feedback and comparison. Only half a provider-hour is available before this decision. Return the trace and helped-use findings with the candidate comparison open. In a later window with resources, access and protection in place, `further probe` on matched unfamiliar cases may be warranted. | Selecting a probe and obtaining its result are different events. Success after exposure to both practices does not isolate their effects or rank them. Method admission, variant construction, fit and worth require their corresponding grounds. Applying AI findings from customer support, consulting or school mathematics to release engineering needs evidence for that transfer. |
| HCD.17: what cultural continuation is warranted? | In the constructed 2026-Q4 provider group, trainers who received both material-based and coached preparation use the sequence of eliciting an answer before the decisive cue, giving feedback and arranging a suitable retry. Their session records support `continue` under those conditions. Reducing refresher coaching for these trainers requires evidence of what they sustain under the reduced coaching. Use existing comparable observations when available. If a further comparison is worthwhile and feasible, compare the same trainers on equivalent teaching tasks before and after additional coaching. Whether a future group can learn the practice initially is a different question. | A learner’s uncued counter-hypothesis is a separate performance observation. Method admission, wider adoption, retention, general capability and causal effect call for evidence at those scopes. |

An HCD.14 proposal can inform HCD.15 or HCD.17. Observed HCD.15 use can inform HCD.16, and its repertoire finding can inform HCD.17. For each use, check the person or population, later work, status, conditions, evidence period and authority. Use a suitably qualified substitute if the original result does not apply, or state the missing basis.

These stipulated case inputs supply no observations for the ReleaseWork-R9 missing-value table below.



## HCD.Application:5 - APP-HCD-04 - Constructed whole learning product and shared task

An author plans a product for future technical diagnosticians who can calculate energy per unit volume but may mistake an increased indicator for proof of a cause. The aim is to compare rival explanations, select an observation that distinguishes them and state a supported conclusion. [HCD.28:4–HCD.28:5](#hcd28---construct-and-revise-a-whole-learning-product-for-a-future-audience) connects the subject basis, preparation, task, support, feedback and personal observation needed for this offer.

Start with what the available basis lets the learner do. A qualified demonstration and supported practice may make an implicit expert choice learnable. Recover the subject criterion when it is still missing and the intended teaching or use needs it. For a material that hides an available distinction, use HCD.19. For help that cannot arrive in time, use HCD.7 to assess usable support or HCD.8 to obtain or build the missing contribution when that is the task. State any remaining limit.

For 24 entrants, HCD.28 compares a supported individual route with four-person groups for the same outcome and final assistance conditions. The individual core takes 90 minutes. The group core adds six active minutes per learner for qualified help and preserves both personal contributions and reconciliation. In the [HCD.20](#hcd20---compose-and-compare-arrangements-for-individual-and-group-learning) timetable, pairs of groups start at 10:50, 11:00 and 11:10, two mentors are booked from 11:00 to 11:30 and the personal responses can finish before noon. Six 20-minute preparation branches add two learner-hours. [HCD.22](#hcd22---design-shared-learning-tasks-with-necessary-individual-contributions) works through the measurements, conditional models, choice of a distinguishing observation, common conclusion and subsequent personal use. The two-day plan reserves 288 minutes for first-response and follow-up checks. With coordination and recovery, the individual and four-person routes reserve 17.2 and 16.6 provider-hours respectively. At full use of learner recovery, active allowances are 39.5 and 42.65 learner-hours. HCD.20 also compares pairs and their peak demand. A group answer does not establish every person’s judgement.

For a paid distributed offer, establish compatible meeting and response windows, count work outside meetings and provide a usable continuation after a missed contribution or qualify the offer by that limit. If qualified help cannot reach learners in the proposed window, examine feasible staggering, individual support, another provider or a narrower promise. Payment and a cohort assignment provide different evidence from usable participation and instruction.

An internal team can use employer-provided time and equipment without buying a course. Around one instrument, participants might predict, measure, challenge and take turns operating it. Establish applicable access, confidentiality, training data and personal actions, reusing the current arrangement when adequate. Capacity depends on exclusive turns and concurrent work. If only the team’s report is needed, division of labour or competent external delivery may complete the job.

For a future audience learning a familiar calculation that needs no exchange, a sufficient individual route is a complete product. If a named learner later needs a programme assessment or comparison, use HCD.2 with that person’s supported starting condition, later work and access.

These constructed cases show how the contribution and its supply conditions change the design. Report actual participation, operating support, personal learning, coordinated team work or causal effect from evidence for the result claimed.


## HCD.Application:6 - Application return to a programme and instrument designer

The FoundationsProgramme design allocates 340 learner-hours and 240 teaching hours over 34 weeks, with 16 topics and 49 patterns for practice. Its intended outcomes are checked performance of selected whole tasks and lower effort to learn a previously untaught method at unchanged correctness. The release review and support-workload cases illustrate the first. The Q2 instrument below addresses the second. These are design targets. The Learning Product owner designs and resources the programme, tasks and instrument within its remit, using HCD to qualify practice and evidence.

Before individual learners are known, use HCD.28 to design or assess the future-audience product. Programme variants or task-family comparisons developed with HCD.2 can contribute at their stated audience assumptions. Decision Design can compare the author’s A/B/C options when wanted. A personal programme comparison requires the person’s later work, supported target or profile, starting evidence, participation, support, feasible candidates and finite resources. An assessment or comparison can finish before any programme choice or launch.

At ten learner-hours per week, the three 34-week designs each use 340 hours. At six per week only 204 hours are available, leaving a 136-hour excess for each. That establishes incompatibility as proposed. To develop a feasible revision, identify what is removed or replaced and whether the two promised outcomes, whole-task practice and evidence still fit.

For general, domain and joint application, A allocates 202/96/42 learner-hours, B 88/204/48 and C 136/136/68. Each totals 340. A candidate for 204 hours must count the complete learner effort once and accommodate its required preparation, whole tasks, feedback, any needed correction and evidence. Check the separate teaching allocation and timing for the work it must supply.

A comparison for one complete task family can give the author a usable first result. Retain the detail already available for C and develop the missing detail for each alternative in the requested comparison only as far as needed to compare the intended output, audience, practice, help and observation. Use HCD.5 and HCD.6 for instructional contributions, HCD.7 for provider demand and HCD.8 when a required contribution is unavailable and obtaining or building it is in scope. A supported substitution or a precise constraint still leaves the complete 204-hour programme open. HCD.2:5.2 illustrates a narrower 170-hour offer. Changing the intended output requires its own decision.


For twelve participants, `32 × 6.5 + 2 × 16 = 240` teaching hours, averaging 20 per participant. This allocation includes work other than individual contact. With HCD.7, establish who or what can supply the models, feedback, assessments, specialist help, tools, AI and required checks when learners need them, including peak windows. With 24 people and the same per-person checking demand, total checking doubles. To offer that version, allocate the work across available providers and state any changed checking conditions. Recheck the complete provider allocation and timing before retaining the 240-hour estimate.

For the intended learning action, use HCD.5 to select a method on the starting evidence, mechanism, task, provider, risk and observation need. Before the audience is known, make the choice conditional and identify the evidence needed at entry. HCD.6 can supply representative action and refusal cases using compatible FW8 data and the changed 24- or 22-hour limit. Use HCD.7 to assess sources, tables, calculator, AI conditions, assessor competence and capacity, human checking and fallback. Use HCD.8 for a remaining contribution that must be obtained or developed.

Assessor preparation can use three contrasting answers, a ten-change proposal supported by 24 hours, an unsupported promise of twelve under the same limit, and a justified request when firmware evidence is missing. The prospective assessors judge independently and resolve differences against the criterion. In the proposed operating test, examine whether judgement on a 22-hour case is consistent and timely. Evidence from that test concerns the observed service and conditions. Wider competence, whole-window provision and learner effect each need their own basis.

With HCD.9, retain the first response, help received, criterion-bearing feedback and the learner’s subsequent action. In practice, give the learner a targeted opportunity to use the correction. For a finding about subsequent performance, use an adequate observation of the affected action. An adequately supported first response may stand. Use HCD.10 to vary a consequential condition, return after an interval, interleave plausible methods or change support or challenge. Learning, transfer, retention and causal effect require corresponding evidence.

The FoundationsProgramme’s planned delayed visits concern six selected patterns: F.1, F.0.1, C.16, B.5.2, A.10.1 and C.11.

| Planned visit | Selected contribution | Conditions that affect the interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Week 8 | F.1 and F.0.1, about six weeks after their initial work | Ordinary sources and tools; five minutes of independent question recognition before searching. |
| Week 17 | C.16 and B.5.2 in a different managerial or engineering case | Pattern texts and AI for the main task; a separate short internal-core probe. |
| Week 25 | F.1, C.16 and A.10.1 in a configuration question | Record use and practice during the intervening weeks rather than assuming non-use. |
| Week 34 | F.1, C.16 and C.11 in an integration case | Normal means for the main task and a separately specified first move without AI. |

Weeks 8, 17, 25 and 34 are planned returns to selected contributions. HCD.10 uses the spacing and intervening practice to design those returns. For a conclusion about retention or support dependence, HCD.13 uses observations under the relevant conditions. The calendar establishes the planned intervals.

The 30-minute final core includes one 15-minute no-AI fragment using the supplied tables and calculator. The main task retains ordinary pattern and AI access. The fragment tests recovery of configuration and time constraints, rejection of an unsupported release and a viable next proposal. A six-to-eight-week follow-up outside the programme needs a separate agreement covering the assessor, available time and access.

The proposed Q2 unfamiliar-Method instrument remains a distinct design task:

| Minutes | Intended observation |
| ---: | --- |
| 5 | Prior familiarity and relevant conditions. |
| 8 | Unannounced recognition and finding a usable source, without a PatternID cue. |
| 22 | First application after every participant receives the same exact new source. |
| 15 | Adaptation to a material changed condition. |
| 10 | Checking, correction and explanation, with first and helped performance kept separate. |

The 60-minute proposal replaces an existing one-hour task within the 340-hour design. Check whether the component tasks fit before using the instrument. For C.11.MV, test the practical disposition against current alternatives. For SYSE.23, distinguish a change to the project’s system of interest from one to its enabling platform and test the anticipated future benefit. Each proposed task needs evidence of the operation newly required, beyond familiar cost arithmetic or a repeated C.11 comparison.

Retain recognition, first and corrected performance, source contribution, help, time, material errors and unfinished attempts as distinct observations. To claim faster learning at unchanged correctness, compare suitable observed cases under comparable conditions. Differences between the methods and their demands in weeks 17 and 34 prevent this comparison from isolating a training effect. Three to five hours is the estimate for authoring the instrument. An observed Q2 result, a pilot extension and an actual learner trial each need further evidence.


## HCD.Application:7 - ReleaseWork-R9 - Prospective demand and discriminated missing evidence

The accepted future architecture for Engineer-E27 supports an HCD.1 demand hypothesis for 2026-Q4 `ReleaseWork-R9`. The hypothesized contributions include challenging AI output, configuration-impact reasoning, returning evidence, specialist coordination, critical-error detection and unfamiliar-variant adaptation. A current demand conclusion needs evidence of the corresponding work and conditions.

The missing values remain separate:

| Missing value | What it prevents now | Retry boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compatible actual `SYSE.21` supplier result required by `XRI-21` | Any HCD.1 demand use that consumes current engineering-culture enactment, bounded practice-change decision, retained alternatives, or evidence gaps | Obtain that compatible result, or a receiver-permitted qualified direct substitute, for Engineer-E27, the Method, Work, period, and evidence use. |
| actual ReleaseWork-R9 Work occurrence | Treating ReleaseWork-R9 itself as current later-Work evidence | Admit performed Work with Engineer-E27, configuration, period, and performer recoverable. |
| occurrence-produced result or supported direct result claim | Any conclusion consuming the occurrence's obtained quality, error, result, or consequence | Establish the produced result or supported direct claim tied to the admitted occurrence. |
| occurrence-bound result record | Any record-dependent inference | Relate a current result episteme to the admitted occurrence and result; do not require it where qualified direct observations suffice. |
| representative occurrence-bound observations | Qualified current demand, a diagnostic target, and a current profile comparison | Obtain holder- and condition-compatible observations or a named qualified representative set covering performed Method, configuration, work products, quality and critical errors, AI/support posture, specialist returns, variants, and evidence window. |

Use the current `SYSE.21` MethodDescription and its constructed PumpWorks case to identify questions. If a claim about E27 depends on current engineering-culture practice, use a compatible `XRI-21` result or an equivalent accepted for that use. For each other claim, obtain only its required observations; a prospective question can be framed while those observations are missing. Where those grounds are absent, identify the affected conclusion.

HCD.1 retains the prospective hypothesis and returns `demand-evidence-blocked` for current demand. HCD.3 returns `diagnostic-evidence-missing` without selecting training. HCD.4 retains the prospective targets and returns `profile-decision-blocked`. When a missing value becomes available, reassess the conclusions that depend on it.


## HCD.Application:8 - APP-HCD-05 - Explanation, peer judgement and personal return across different settings


### HCD.Application:8.1 - A paid distributed adult programme

Twelve adults from different organizations need to judge whether a recommendation follows from its evidence and apply that distinction in their own projects. This constructed block uses qualified subject criteria and entrants who can read the short cases. It is separate from APP-HCD-04’s diagnostic routes. Each learner must justify their own judgement of a peer’s reasoning and use what they have learned in a personal case.

In this case HCD.20 compares supported individual work with an arrangement for peer judgement. The learners must themselves judge a peer’s reasoning. An expert or AI comment can supply material to examine. It cannot substitute for that required action. With HCD.21, check whether the proposed members can work together with the available time, preparation and permissions. Use established contact where it suffices or arrange and verify the missing contact. For a closed project, use a cleared fragment or a constructed counterpart that preserves the evidence-to-conclusion relation. Evidence about a counterpart does not establish what happened in the undisclosed project.

Each learner prepares a bounded question, ground and conditional conclusion. HCD.27:5.1 specifies the Tuesday-to-Friday handoffs and provider windows. The assessor checks the fragments received. From cases with adequate grounds, the facilitator selects one contrasting pair for each of the three groups, preserving the conditions each group needs for comparison. Each participant reads the selected pair and makes a judgement against the criterion before the common exchange. Use HCD.6.1 where a learner still needs help discerning an observation from a causal claim.

The 30-minute group exercise allows four three-minute judgements and their grounds, six minutes to question and compare them, six for subject help and a final six for personal conclusions. Each learner has 90 seconds to say what they will keep or revise and why. The selected pair supplies common material. All participants can examine their own judgements and retain or revise them on the evidence. HCD.23 supports reconstruction of an explanation, and HCD.24 connects a reviewer’s judgement to their own response to feedback. Original case authors who are present can use the feedback on their underlying recommendations. If the group edits one answer without comparing grounds, use HCD.26 to restore that comparison when needed or identify the missing subject help. Check what participants did with a cue. These times apply to the stipulated short judgements.

Here the three groups have confirmed starts at 18:00, 18:08 and 18:16. After twelve minutes of judgements and six of comparison, the mentor visits at 18:18–18:24, 18:26–18:32 and 18:34–18:40. The booked window is 18:16–18:46 including transitions. The groups make their personal returns and finish at 18:30, 18:38 and 18:46. Each learner has 30 active minutes within the 46-minute cohort window. If everyone must leave at 18:30, A can finish, B’s consultation is interrupted and C misses its consultation. The later groups need another viable arrangement for the promised work. HCD.27:5.1 gives the full timetable.

Each learner applies the relation to a personal or permitted substitute case with a changed condition. With HCD.25, identify the correspondence and what would break it. Two reports from one observation cannot provide two independent observations. If the question is their provenance, tracing it can finish the task. Seek independent evidence when the use requires it. HCD.12 distinguishes transfer to an unfamiliar case from learning the distinction here. Qualify a correction by the help received.

The design allocates three fixed provider-hours for case preparation, criterion qualification and provider readiness. Recurring provider allocation is 370 minutes, including 120 for Tuesday checking and reserve, 20 for selection, 20 for contact and coordination, 30 for Wednesday mentoring, 120 for checking Thursday’s personal returns and the related reserve, and 60 for checking corrections and the Friday reserve. One cohort therefore reserves 550 minutes, or nine hours ten minutes. One provider may cover several duties if the windows fit. The booking counts even when some reserved time is unused.

Each learner’s core allowance is 95 active minutes, including 20 for the initial fragment, 15 for reading feedback and preparing a comparative judgement, 30 for the exchange, 15 for personal application and 15 for any needed correction or further response. Twelve learners therefore have 19 hours allocated. The estimate assumes the stated preparation and short readable cases. A prerequisite branch, translation or restored conversation requires its own time and support. Where demand exceeds the reserve, identify a viable new window, additional qualified help or a narrower promise.

HCD.28 can use this design at its stated conditions. For a delivered cohort, use evidence of the contact participants made, their first and helped responses, their use of feedback and the actual demand on providers, as the question requires. To compare programme effects causally, use a design that addresses the unit of assignment, interaction among learners, attrition and exposure to support. A payment receipt can establish payment and a viable timetable can establish feasibility. Neither shows the effect on learners.


### HCD.Application:8.2 - Internal team learning without a course purchase

An employer releases four technicians to work around one safe training instrument. Under the supplied technical criterion, their learning tasks are to predict, observe, question and manipulate the instrument. HCD.20:5.2 derives capacity from exclusive operating turns and useful simultaneous observer actions. The team’s shared access and context can justify retaining its membership under HCD.21. Compare any changed membership against the material participants are permitted to use.

Use HCD.22 to preserve each required personal action. With HCD.23, an observer can explain a discrepancy before the operator changes the setting. For a quiet observer, HCD.26 can help distinguish ongoing reasoning, inaccessible information and a missed distinction. Use HCD.24 where participants must judge a diagnostic explanation and decide whether to retain or revise it. The authorized technical owner holds any plant decision. The employer supplies time and equipment, and qualified help has to be available where the task needs it.

The team can compare a permitted outside case using HCD.25. Under HCD.27, protect internal data and determine whether a missed operating turn left an unmet need. When one is still needed, arrange a viable replacement or identify the limit. A recording may restore information. To establish that the learner manipulated the instrument, use evidence of their own action. For the team’s coordinated production capability, use OCE and the relevant work method with evidence of joint work.


### HCD.Application:8.3 - An author whose audience is not yet known

An author is preparing instruction for interpreting an indicator under specified assumptions. Use the available subject method, obtain a qualified contribution when needed or identify its absence. With HCD.28, assess a single route or compare supported individual work with a route using peer explanation or judgement. Readable contrasts and accessible qualified feedback may supply the entire target through an individual route.

If a later version promises that learners can judge someone else’s reasoning or respond to a challenge, provide the specific interaction that target needs. HCD.23 and HCD.24 explain those contributions. A supplied AI answer may be material to inspect. For a proposed human exchange, establish access to a suitable participant and an opportunity for the learner to respond. To report an exchange that took place, establish what each contributed. Use HCD.27 if the dependency needs a shared occasion. For a known learner’s programme question, HCD.2 uses that person’s starting evidence, later work and access.

The three cases illustrate how permissions, personal actions, timing and burden change the proposed arrangement. Claims about learning or service operation require evidence of what took place at the stated scope.


## HCD.Application:9 - Clinical unlike case - Return diagnosis and treatment to their owner

For an adult seeking treatment for social anxiety, the relevant service is qualified clinical care. HCD.1 may serve a separately identified question about the person’s participation in non-clinical later work when the person or qualified practitioner provides that remit.

Use HCD.3 to recognize questions that belong in qualified clinical care, including diagnosis, treatment selection, safety, provider competence, consent and clinical outcomes. Symptom measures and treatment plans follow their clinical meanings. A personal mastery question under HCD.4 needs evidence of the particular work contribution.

Qualified clinical professionals address diagnosis, treatment, provider competence, safety and clinical outcomes. The person gives or withholds consent. Other participants decide within their authorized remits. Exposure, clinical homework, counterconditioning, treatment outcomes and provider arrangements require the applicable clinical practice.


## HCD.Application:10 - Combine explanation, experience and participation in a changing practice

The examples use HCD.5 to combine methods for specified learning actions. Their observations, resources and possible responses are stipulated. The practitioner needs the relevant subject knowledge, demonstrations or judgements, either already available or obtainable. Use HCD to construct the learning opportunity. For a claim about teaching effectiveness, establish the effect with suitable evidence.

### HCD.Application:10.1 - From a grammatical account to usable conversation

A learner wants to describe yesterday’s activities and answer a follow-up in the selected variety of English. They can explain a past-tense rule on a worksheet, miss a familiar verb in connected speech and sometimes say *goed* where that variety uses *went*. The teacher has suitable recordings, examples and feedback. Work on the missed speech distinction and on retrieving the conventional form addresses two difficulties that a repeated general explanation would leave open.

The teacher examines the learner’s recognition of the event in a meaningful utterance, retrieval of the required form with preparation, and use of that form while responding to someone else. Replay, a written version or a short preparation interval can help locate the difficulty. Use the evidence already available and select help for the affected task.

For the missed sound pattern, the teacher presents short utterances with the event context available, then changes speaker and surrounding words. The learner identifies the event or selects a fitting continuation. A revealing contrast is repeated when the learner confuses it; broader listening resumes when that difference is accessible. A transcript can connect sound and an already known expression, then be omitted when the intended observation concerns listening without it. Merely replaying unfamiliar continuous speech need not expose the missed relation.

For production, distinguish the regular construction from the selected frequent irregular forms. The learner uses *went* in meaningful accounts and retrieves it again on later occasions. Examples supply the conventional irregular form, and retrieval gives the learner practice using it. Applying the productive rule lets the learner express something new with a regular verb.

In a short exchange about a real or stipulated day, the learner chooses what to say and answers the partner’s follow-up. A phrase list may enable the first exchange. Clarify a misunderstanding in time to preserve communication. A form that leaves the account intelligible can be revisited afterwards. If a correction is needed, give the learner an opportunity to use it in another utterance. A corrected script and an unprompted reply support different conclusions.

If listening now works but the learner pauses while retrieving a form, add manageable production opportunities rather than another listening distinction. If rehearsed narration works but follow-up questions defeat it, practise that interaction with bounded support. If the new colleague uses a different accepted register or variety, compare its conventions with the receiving task before marking a difference wrong. Keep changes in the language, the learner's provisional generalization and ordinary slips distinguishable.

This case can yield a teaching choice and an attainable next conversation. HCD.10 can guide the frequency and variation of practice. Use HCD.11–HCD.13 for stronger claims about performance or later use when those claims matter. Select the balance of regular and exceptional forms, explanation and exposure for the actual language work.

### HCD.Application:10.2 - Reconnect a perceptible cue, bodily coordination and a shared phrase

A dancer keeps the pulse and performs a short phrase alone, but begins the continuation before an unfamiliar partner finishes the invitation. The teacher identifies the convention. The dancer must keep the shared pulse, notice the invitation and give a response the partner can read. Assess that interaction in the intended practice.

Two qualified demonstrations preserve enough of the same phrase to compare an early continuation with a response made once the invitation is available. The learner marks the relevant moment and chooses whether to continue or wait. If that moment is still hard to perceive, use HCD.6.1 to construct a clearer contrast. If the learner notices it but continues early, examine the coordination needed to act on it.

The teacher then selects an attainable movement task that retains the invitation–response coupling while reducing other demands, for example a shorter phrase with a competent partner supplying a clear invitation. The learner makes the response and encounters feedback from the partner and the visible or audible result. An explicit cue can help locate the intended change. Requiring simultaneous verbal monitoring of feet, torso, pulse, invitation and expressive quality would add a different demand; the teacher chooses the one relation currently needing attention and lets already available coordination serve the task.

Return to the whole phrase and vary the partner or musical density where relevant. Observe whether the dancer responds to the invitation at the shared pulse. Slower practice can change timing and dynamics, so test the target coordination at the receiving tempo when that is the intended result. If an exaggerated cue made the response possible, move toward the ordinary interaction while preserving feasibility. If the partner uses a different convention, help the dancer recognize and negotiate that difference. Judge the earlier coordination under its original convention.

Musical accents can support several stylistically acceptable continuations. Compare how the performers preserve the pulse and respond to one another across the possibilities. Use the criterion of the intended practice when deciding which continuations work.

Suppose the dancer wants to develop a different phrasing. The teacher and learner preserve the shared pulse and a partner-readable invitation, vary the placement or duration of a pause and observe how a prepared partner responds. They judge whether the relation survives and whether the phrasing suits the occasion. An unexpected response can inform another attempt. Keep, adapt or set aside the variant according to that result. If the trial warrants another use, try the variant on a suitable occasion and let the participants judge whether to continue it.

The immediate finding concerns this dancer’s perception and action with the stated partners and help. [MDPE.Application:5.3](../MUSIC-AND-DANCE-PRACTICE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mdpeapplication53---connect-style-method-structure-and-acquisition) distinguishes recognizable style, method organization and acquired capability. Where school and event require incompatible performances, use [MDPE.Application:5.1](../MUSIC-AND-DANCE-PRACTICE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mdpeapplication51---renew-a-shared-practice-without-losing-what-makes-participation-worthwhile) for the shared-practice question.

### HCD.Application:10.3 - Learn in a clerk's actual queue and organize support around it

An incoming clerk must route a request with its attachments, identify a missing required item and ask a usable clarification. The current work method and acceptance criteria are available. The clerk handles complete cases but copies the usual route when an attachment changes the required response. A supervisor can review prepared replies before they are sent. The work already contains another suitable case later in the week.

The designer uses cases already present in the queue. A supervisor demonstrates an ordinary case and an exception, showing what changes the route. The clerk prepares a real reply and identifies the relevant evidence. Before the reply is sent, the reviewer can flag a missed condition so the clerk can revise it. An adequate first reply can stand. A later suitable case can supply another attempt. Use a legitimate incoming case when another attempt answers a learning need.

Suppose the agreed weekly allowance is 40 additional clerk-minutes and 20 supervisor-minutes. The planned contrast takes 10 and 5 minutes respectively. The reviewed attempt and any necessary correction take 15 and 5, and the later case 10 and 5. Five minutes remain for each participant to clarify an unexpected issue. Check the estimates in use. If review regularly exceeds the allowance, assess a narrower task set or an authorized change in capacity.

If the clerk recognizes an exception but cannot obtain a required fact, identify the access or response-channel problem. Restore the missing contribution when provision is needed and feasible. If the supervisor gives the decisive choice, qualify the attempt by that help. For a personal selection claim, use an occasion on which the clerk makes the choice. If the equipped arrangement meets the job’s needs, retain the reference and review. Suitable existing work products can supply evidence.

A corporate university can make such learning available across departments. Its useful contribution may include subject-qualified examples, preparation for mentors, a short introduction, agreed work opportunities, accessible references and a way to return recurring difficulties to the process owner. It can also supply a separate course or simulator when the work lacks enough suitable encounters. Choose the mix from the capability demand and actual opportunities, not from the institution's label.

For this queue, compare a standalone course, preparation plus reviewed cases at work, and any suitable existing local arrangement when a choice is needed. Include case supply, learner and mentor time, coordination and continuing service. A course can provide common prerequisites. The queue can supply variable attachments, recipients and timely correction. Each needs its corresponding support. Attendance and satisfaction answer their own questions. For exception handling, examine the clerk’s action.

When mentor time is unavailable across departments, identify the effect on the service. The provider can propose a feasible narrower offer or different support. Use the applicable contributions of OCE.6, OCE.9 and OCE.11 for the organizational change needed. If the common work method is defective, refer the issue to its owner or repair it when that work is yours. A correction to the method may remove the need for compensating training.

### HCD.Application:10.4 - Engineers learn through discussion and learn to coordinate across roles

A design engineer, analyst and operations representative must jointly examine a proposed modification. The subject methods, case information and relevant authority are supplied. The group contains experienced and less experienced participants of different ages. Its immediate difficulty is concrete: the calculation uses an operating assumption that the receiving reviewer does not share.

For **learning through interaction**, participants may need to improve recognition of unsupported assumptions. For **learning the joint work** in this case, participants need to request, communicate, use and challenge one another’s contributions before the decision. With HCD.20, compare the proposed interaction with individual work for the same learning target when that comparison is needed. HCD.22 can develop or assess the interaction it requires.

For the first purpose, prepared participants make an initial interpretation, compare the grounds and explain which observation would change the conclusion. A novice who cannot yet enter the comparison receives a qualified worked example first. The analyst's answer becomes useful teaching material when another participant uses its condition to revise or defend a judgement. Taking turns or reading three reports aloud need not produce that use.

For learning the joint work in this case, connect the design request, analyst’s assumption and result, operations response, clarification, confirmed or revised conclusion, and the receiving decision or unresolved question. The designer requests the condition needed for the calculation, the analyst explains its effect and operations determines whether, and under what conditions, it fits the intended use. Supply technical assistance as needed while preserving those exchanges. If the analyst resolves every mismatch alone, a sound final result can leave the others without practice in resolving it together.

After the episode, retain interactions that served the learning purpose. If a remaining learning question warrants changing the interaction, choose a feasible change for another case. For example, include the operating range in the request, ask the receiver to restate a consequential assumption or establish when an unresolved mismatch should return. Try the selected change within the available window if the task calls for another attempt.

For a later case, suppose an operating condition changes after the initial calculation but before review. The participants must establish which results depend on the changed condition. Return a calculation that needs revision, retain still-supported contributions and explain the confirmed or revised result to the reviewer. The learners practise adapting the handover. If one person supplies the entire repair, decide which part the others still need to learn before claiming a joint learning result. A role exchange can help someone understand the receiver's information need, but nobody is thereby qualified or authorized to replace that professional role.
