Composition follows those learning actions. Experience with an unusual failure can be valuable; so can a newcomer's question about an unexplained convention. Age itself establishes neither. Similar-preparation work can be useful for an initial technical exercise, followed by a mixed group for the receiving comparison. Keep a quieter participant's consequential judgement available through a draft, a question or an assigned decision where suitable. Give the experienced contributor a bounded teaching role with time for their own learning target, rather than assume unlimited free tutoring.

Suppose everyone understands the assumption, but operations information reaches the team after the decision window. Identify the missing timely contribution. Use OCE and the responsible participants to change the arrangement when that is the task. If the organizational arrangement changes and the team performs the connected work, retain evidence of the changed timing and what the individual participants did. A team outcome and individual test performances support different claims.

### HCD.Application:10.5 - Use the construction without waiting for an unattainable experiment

The examples connect a bounded teaching action to its grounds. A qualified language teacher can select a contrast, a movement teacher can simplify the task while preserving its coordination, a supervisor can arrange review of a live reply, and engineers can practise a missing exchange between roles. Evidence for the local choice can be sufficient before comparative teaching effectiveness is known.

Ask which additional knowledge could change the requested finding, its grounds or a pending decision. An ordinary case may reveal continued reliance on a cue. A record may establish that no mentor is available. A comparison may identify a route that fits the workload. A causal study can help when the intended inference or programme choice depends on an effect and an informative study is attainable at justified cost. Otherwise return the supported finding, feasible action, narrower commitment or known limit.

For a new arrangement, establish what the learner will encounter and do, what help will be available, how each activity prepares the next contribution and where the task can finish. For an account of a completed arrangement, report what the learner and providers did under the observed conditions. Identify any change that would materially affect the conclusion.

## HCD.Application:End


# Human Capability Development Principles Framework Sources and Edition Notes

## HCD.Sources:1 - Source use and currentness

The source qualifications for HCD.1, HCD.3 and HCD.4 are dated **1 September 2026**. The [NICE social-anxiety guideline](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg159/chapter/recommendations) (`BEH-05`) was checked on **31 August 2026**. Reassess the affected clinical boundary if the recommendation changes.

HCD.1 uses [Kraiger and Ford’s workplace-instruction review (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109) (`COG-10`) to distinguish an instructional event from evidence of transfer. Dell’Acqua and colleagues’ [Navigating the jagged technological frontier](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838) (`AI-03`) informs the bounded task of independently challenging a plausible wrong AI result. Use the applicable FPF edition and qualified target-domain and later-work evidence for the actual demand on a person.

For HCD.3, Melanson and Fahmie’s [Functional analysis of problem behavior: a 40-year review](https://doi.org/10.1002/jaba.983) (2023, `BEH-01`) supports distinguishing the conditions that sustain an observed difficulty before intervening. NICE supplies the clinical stop. Sheeran and colleagues’ [Self-determination theory interventions for health behavior change](https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000501) (2020, `MOT-01`) and [Does increasing autonomous motivation or perceived competence lead to health behavior change?](https://doi.org/10.1037/hea0001111) (2021, `MOT-02`) inform limits on target engagement. Use `E.23.CAE` when distinguishing plausible causes could change the supported diagnosis, its grounds or the response. Use qualified specialist evidence for the question it addresses. These health sources do not establish a general capability diagnosis or authorize HCD clinical practice.

For HCD.4, Winget and Persky’s [A practical review of mastery learning](https://doi.org/10.5688/ajpe8906) (2022, `COG-06`) informs local thresholds, correction and retesting. Gutierrez de Blume’s [Calibrating calibration](https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000674) (2022, `COG-07`) informs self-monitoring accuracy. Arieli-Attali and colleagues’ [Expanded evidence-centered design](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.00853) (2019, `COG-08`) connects claims, tasks, evidence and inference. Abdelrahman and colleagues’ [Knowledge tracing: a survey](https://doi.org/10.1145/3569576) (2023, `COG-09`) informs the limits of model predictions. C.32.MWA, C.11 and task evidence supply the relevant architecture, choice and case conditions. For each claim about P14’s capability, transfer, retention or a causal learning effect, establish whether the available evidence supports that inference. The cited design work does not establish those effects or a universal progression.

HCD.2 and HCD.5–HCD.10 use the following sources for programme comparison, method selection, task design, support, provider and environment operation, focused practice and progression. The relevant method explains how the source is used and what would change that reliance.

| Source group | Contribution and limit used by HCD.2 and HCD.5–HCD.10 |
| --- | --- |
| [Schwartz, *Achieving an adaptive learner*, online 2024](https://aaalab.stanford.edu/assets/papers/2024/achieving_an_adaptive_learner.pdf) | Preparing to use an explanation through a common account across contrasts. HCD.6:4.2.2 compares this with explaining a worked solution; the original STEM studies establish neither a universal sequence nor the effect of the constructed lesson. |
| Maintained [4C/ID model](https://www.4cid.org/about/) and Paas and van Merriënboer ([2020; `COG-05`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0963721420922183)) | Sufficiently whole complex tasks, integrated information, worked support and expertise-sensitive guidance; no local programme effect, mandatory sequence or universal fading rule. |
| Winget and Persky ([2022; `COG-06`](https://doi.org/10.5688/ajpe8906)) and Wisniewski, Zierer, and Hattie ([2020; `MOT-05`](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.03087)) | Corrective activity, retest and information-bearing feedback under task and receiver conditions; no universal threshold, feedback type or later-work inference. |
| Carpenter, Pan, and Butler ([2022; `COG-01`](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44159-022-00089-1)), Brunmair and Richter ([2019; `COG-03`](https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000209)), and Czyż, Wójcik, and Solarská ([2024; `COG-04`](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2024.1377122)) | Spacing, retrieval, interleaving and delayed-transfer candidates whose value depends on material, similarity, setting and horizon; no universal gap, mix, repetition count or professional schedule. |
| Kraiger and Ford ([2021; `COG-10`](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109)), Matsuo and Tsukube ([2020; `SOC-02`](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijme.2020.100417)), Brooks and colleagues ([2024; `SOC-05`](https://doi.org/10.1002/lrh2.10412)), and Wiese, Kilty, and Bennett ([2018; `SOC-03`](https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.13655)) | Separation of instructional events, learner activity, provider contributions, access, supervision, trust, risk and service pressure; no generic provider credential, capability effect or transplanted clinical governance. |
| Tullis, Goldstone, and Hanson ([2015; `COG-11`](https://doi.org/10.1080/00222895.2015.1008686)), Dell’Acqua and colleagues ([`AI-03`](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838)), and Bastani and colleagues ([2025; `AI-04`](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122)) | Assisted and later unassisted performance, human checking, and AI-support conditions remain distinct; laboratory, consulting-task and school-mathematics results establish neither a universal support schedule nor an adult workplace effect or AI ban. |
| Macnamara, Hambrick, and Oswald ([2014; `BEH-02`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614535810)), Nurse and colleagues ([2024; `BEH-03`](https://doi.org/10.1080/10503307.2024.2308159)), and Sheeran and colleagues ([2020; `MOT-01`](https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000501), [2024; `MOT-03`](https://doi.org/10.1080/10463283.2024.2334563)) | Limits on universal deliberate-practice doses, bounded focused-practice ingredients, target engagement, and conditional if–then planning; no fixed hours threshold, cross-domain causality or professional transfer guarantee. |

The source uses for HCD.11–HCD.14 were qualified on **3 September 2026**. The table identifies the assessment or revision contribution of each.

| [Kraiger and Ford, workplace instruction, 2021](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109) | Instruction, learner activity, learning and work transfer remain distinct; no particular programme's effectiveness is established. |
| [Carpenter, Pan and Butler, 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44159-022-00089-1) and [Yang and colleagues, 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33683913/) | Retrieval/testing can affect learning under specified conditions; no universal delay, engineer effect size or all-domain transfer guarantee. |

HCD.18 and HCD.19 use the [material profile's source-informed comparisons](#hcdapplication15---source-informed-choices-and-limits) within the scope specified in those methods. Task-based evaluation and the ordinal anchors are professional adaptations. Validation for a particular assessment use needs its own evidence. The M0/M1 walkthrough includes recorded responses of a prepared agent, constructed task facts, a changed material and the author’s diagnostic replay. Evidence of learning or experienced burden for the intended human audience remains separate.

The programme and L17 exercise supply designed tasks, stipulated engineering facts and constructed observations. For an engineering, safety or professional claim about a real case, use qualified applicable domain sources and evidence from that case.

The `ImpactReview-17-Domain-Oracle-v1` supplies the stipulated engineering and criticality criteria for this exercise. For a corresponding real-world claim, identify the target-domain method or result applicable at the time in question and the qualified safety or specialist source the claim requires.

When a relied-on premise changes, reassess the affected pattern or case claim. Relevant changes may concern an FPF distinction, a source or subject method, a specialist boundary, the person or work, configuration, evidence period, critical-error criterion, case facts, assistance, task conditions or receiving use. Preserve conclusions whose grounds still apply.

HCD.20–HCD.28 use the specified contributions of 4C/ID, TBL, Jigsaw and FROG and bounded research on collaboration, visibility and active observation. Each method’s SoTA-Echoing section identifies the adopted operation and its limits. HCD.21 explains how to form or retain a compatible group and establish usable contact when it is missing. HCD.24 and HCD.25 distinguish a comparative judgement from observed transfer. HCD.26 distinguishes a cue from participants’ use of it. Apply Juxtapeer, group-formation, contact and feedback research, including Edwards and the later CMU study, at their stated tasks, populations and observation conditions. For tutor-facing assistance, HCD.7 also requires competence, checking and usable capacity. The diagnostic product, resource figures and recovery options are constructed planning examples. Determining the best grouping in a particular setting requires its own comparison.

## HCD.Sources:2 - Edition return

This edition of the **Human Capability Development Principles Framework** includes an architectural reference, an instructional-material profile and twenty-nine pattern bodies. The Table of Contents links to the bodies. Use the version date below to identify the edition.

The [Human Capability Engineering DPF Suite (HCE)](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) includes HCD and Somatic Movement Modeling. HCD addresses deliberate development of a person’s capability for later work. The [Engineering DPF Suite](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) refers readers to this specialized suite. To establish use, provider operation, performed development work, personal capability, cultural continuation or causal effectiveness, use the evidence for the claimed result. Decisions to launch or rely on an arrangement also need the relevant authority.

**Description:** HCD is a pattern language for deriving human capability demand from later Work, designing and sustaining development arrangements, judging human contribution, transfer and retention, and evaluating instructional material under stated audience, task, support and time conditions.

**Author:** Anatoly Levenchuk with AI-assisted development and review.

**Edition:** Twenty-nine-pattern edition dated 12 October 2026

**Status:** Eternal alpha: used in working development projects and open to continuing correction.

**License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for original framework content; third-party material retains its own terms.

**Publication:** [FPF Library repository](https://github.com/ailev/FPF).

Each pattern body states its status and the scope of its claims. For a conclusion about a particular person, provider, programme or population, use the evidence and conditions for that application.

## HCD.Sources:3 - Citation

Levenchuk, Anatoly, with AI-assisted development and review. *Human Capability Development Principles Framework*. Twenty-nine-pattern edition, 12 October 2026. [FPF Library repository](https://github.com/ailev/FPF).

For a specific pattern, include its PatternID. When its wording matters, give a permanent link to the file at the commit you used or to an accessible archived copy.

The [Architectural Reference](#human-capability-development-principles-framework-architectural-reference) explains the connected language and the consequences of these sources for its use.
